body.translated_text: Oṃ. Salutations to the one whose essential nature is the Supreme Reality of the Consciousness-Self.
Now,
the <s>Paramārthasāra</s> (Essence of the Supreme Reality),
composed by the eminent master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, the foremost teacher among the great Māheśvara (<s>Mahāmāheśvara</s>) teachers,
accompanied by the commentary (<s>vivṛti</s>) composed by the teacher <s>Yogarāja</s>.

children.text: cidghano 'pi jaganmūrtyā śyāno yaḥ sa jayatyajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Though a dense mass of consciousness (<s>cidghana</s>), He who, in the form of the universe, is [as if] congealed — He, the unborn (<s>aja</s>), triumphs!
He, the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), who is skilled in the play of concealing His own Self. // 1 //
This concise summary of the <s>Paramārthasāra</s> was composed by the <s>Guru</s> with proper reasoning;
I, <s>Yoga[rāja]</s>, urged by the learned, compose a brief commentary (<s>vivṛti</s>) on it. // 2 //

body.text: iha śivādvayaśāsane dehādipramātṛtāprādhānyasvasaṃkalpasamutthaśaṅkātaṅkālasyasaṃśayādirūpavighnaughaprasarapradhvaṃsapūrvikāṃ śāstraniṣpattiṃ manyamānaḥ parimitapramātṛtādhaspadīkāreṇa cidānandaikaghanasvātmadevatāsamāveśaśālinīṃ samastaśāstrārthasaṃkṣepagarbhāṃ prathamatastāvatparameśvarapravaṇatāṃ parāmṛśati /
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here, in the teaching of the non-duality of <s>Śiva</s> (<s>Śivādvayaśāsana</s>), [the author], believing that the composition of a treatise must be preceded by the dispelling of the flood of obstacles — in the form of doubts, apprehensions, laziness, uncertainty, and the like, arising from one's own mental constructions due to the predominance of identification with limited subjectivities such as the body — sets forth, first of all, an inclination toward the Supreme Lord, which brings about immersion in one's own Self-deity, whose nature is a solid mass of consciousness and bliss, through the subordination of limited subjectivity; [an inclination] that contains within it the summary of the meaning of all treatises.

children.text: paraṃ parasthaṃ gahanādanādimekaṃ niviṣṭaṃ bahudhā guhāsu /
children.translated_text: [Verse:] The Supreme, beyond, from the unfathomable, beginningless, one, dwelling in manifold caves,

children.text: sarvālayaṃ sarvacarācarasthaṃ tvāmeva śaṃbhuṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye // 1 //
children.translated_text: the abode of all, abiding in all things moving and unmoving — to You alone, <s>Śambhu</s>, I take refuge. // 1 //
[Commentary:] 'You' —
whose essence is the luminosity of all subjects, who is in the form of one's own Self-deity —
'<s>Śambhu</s>' —
whose nature is the unsurpassed good (<s>anuttara-śreyas</s>), whose essence is Being (<s>sattā</s>) —
'refuge' —
protector; I resort to [You] for the attainment of immersion in You.
The particle

children.text: kāraḥ śaṃbhuṃ svātmadevatākārameva prapadye na punarmāyāntaścāriṇaṃ kañcidbhinnaṃ devamityanyayogaṃ vyavacchinatti / anyacca kiṃbhūtam
children.translated_text: 'eva' (alone) excludes any other yoga, [meaning:] 'I take refuge in <s>Śambhu</s> in the form of my own Self-deity alone, and not in some distinct god who wanders within <s>Māyā</s>.' And moreover, of what nature [is He]?
'Supreme' (<s>param</s>) —
full, of the nature of the unsurpassed, replete with the powers of consciousness, bliss, will, knowledge, and action. Likewise,
'beyond the unfathomable' (<s>parasthaṃ gahanāt</s>) —

children.text: iti gahanānmāyābhidhānāttattvātparasminpūrṇa eva śivādividyātattvaparyante śuddhādhvani svarūpe tiṣṭhantaṃ na punastattadavasthāvaicitryeṇāpi sphuratastataḥ parasmātpūrṇātsvarūpāttasya pracyāvo bhavati / yaduktam
children.translated_text: that is, standing in His own essential nature in the pure path (<s>śuddhādhvan</s>), extending from the <s>Śiva</s> principle to the <s>Vidyā</s> principle, beyond <s>Māyā</s> — the principle called 'the unfathomable'; yet even though He shines forth with the variety of various states, there is no falling away from His supreme, full essential nature. As has been said:
'Even in the distinction of waking and other [states], that [Reality] spreads forth undivided;
it never turns away from its own nature as the perceiver.'
'Beginningless' (<s>anādi</s>) —
ancient, because He is primordially established as the experiencer, by virtue of being the subject of all cognitions.
'One' (<s>eka</s>) —
that is, without a companion, because from the unity of consciousness as luminosity, duality is impossible. Likewise,
'dwelling' (<s>niviṣṭam</s>) —
and so forth. Although of such a nature, by His own freedom (<s>svasvātantrya</s>),
'in manifold ways' (<s>bahudhā</s>) —
in various kinds of distinctions,
'in the caves' (<s>guhāsu</s>) —

children.text: rudrakṣetrajñarūpāsu hṛdguhāsvantarāviṣṭaṃ caitanyarūpo 'pi svayaṃ jaḍājaḍātmatāmābhāsya naṭavannānāpramātṛtayā sthita iti yāvat / ata eva
children.translated_text: He has entered into the caves of the hearts, which are in the form of <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (the field-knower); though He is of the nature of consciousness, He himself manifests as both inert and non-inert natures and, like an actor, abides in the form of manifold subjectivities. Therefore,
'the abode of all' (<s>sarvālayam</s>),
that is,
of all —
the universe in the form of subjects and objects such as <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Kṣetrajña</s>, and so forth —
'the abode' (<s>ālaya</s>) —

children.text: viśrāntisthānaṃ / sarvamidaṃ kila pūrṇapramātari sthitaṃ sadgrāhyagrāhakayugalakāpekṣayonmagnamiva bhedena prakāśamānaṃ nānārupairvyapadiśyate 'nyathaitasyaprakāśādbhinnasya sattaiva na syātkuta idaṃ viśvamiti sarvanāmapratyavamarśaḥ / naitāvatā bhagavataḥ samuttīrṇaṃ svarūpamityāha
children.translated_text: the resting-place. Indeed, all this abides in the full Subject; appearing as though submerged in its true reality of the subject-object pair, it manifests in differentiation and is designated by various forms. Otherwise, for something whose existence is separate from the light [of consciousness], there could be no existence at all — whence then this universe? This is the reflection on the pronoun 'all.' But the essential nature of the Blessed One is not exhausted by just this much — hence he says:
'abiding in all things moving and unmoving' (<s>sarvacarācarastham</s>) —

children.text: iti / sarvamidaṃ yajjaḍājaḍasvabhāvaṃ viśvaṃ tadrūpatayā tiṣṭhantaṃ
children.translated_text: that is, standing as the very nature of all this universe, which is of both inert and non-inert character.

body.translated_text: Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Spandaśāstra</s>.

body.text: kartāsi sarvasya yataḥ svayaṃ vai vibho tataḥ sarvamidaṃ tvameva /
body.translated_text: 'Since You are yourself the agent of all, O Lord (<s>Vibhu</s>), therefore all this is You alone.'
By this reasoning, indeed, because for something separate and non-manifest, being an effect is impossible.
'The enjoyer alone, in the form of the enjoyed, ever abides everywhere.'

body.text: iti bhagavāneva tathā tathā cakāstīti / evaṃvidhaṃ tvāmanuttaraṃ sarvasya svātmadevatāsvarūpaṃ parāhantācamatkārasāramapi gṛhītanānātvamatha cātyantākhaṇḍitasvasvātantryaparamādvayaprakāśasvabhāvaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaṃbhum

children.translated_text: 'I take refuge' (<s>prapadye</s>) —

children.text: śarīrādikṛtrimāhaṅkāraguṇīkāreṇaitādṛśaṃ tvāmeva svātmānaṃ parāhantācamatkārasvarūpaṃ samāviśāmīti yāvat / anena grahaṇakavākyena paramopādeyāṃ svasvabhāvasamāveśamayīṃ daśāmupadiśatā guruṇā vakṣyamāṇaheyopādeyatayā sakalagranthārthopakṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: that is, by making subordinate the artificial ego-sense rooted in the body and the like, I enter into You — who are indeed my own Self, whose nature is the supreme I-consciousness (<s>parāhantā-camatkāra</s>). By this opening verse, the <s>Guru</s>, while teaching the supreme state of immersion in one's own nature as the most desirable, has made an introduction to the entire meaning of the treatise through what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted, as will be explained. // 1 //

body.translated_text: Thus the Blessed One shines forth in this way and that. Such are You — unsurpassed, the very Self-deity of all, whose essence is the savor of the supreme I-consciousness (<s>parāhantā-camatkāra</s>), yet who has assumed manifoldness; and yet whose nature is the supreme non-dual light of utterly unbroken freedom — the Blessed <s>Śambhu</s>:

[Commentary:] Having thus established the purport of the treatise — the non-dual essential nature — through the medium of praise, now, in order to state the descent into the treatise [proper], the author of the text speaks of the connection, subject matter, and so forth, in two verses:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] Bewildered in the wheel of suffering ending in death, beginning with dwelling in the womb,
the disciple asked the Blessed Lord, the foundation (<s>Ādhāra</s>), about the supreme reality (<s>paramārtha</s>). // 2 //
The <s>Guru</s> addressed him through the <s>Ādhāra</s> verses; that essence
<s>Abhinavagupta</s> expounds through the perspective of the <s>Śiva</s> teaching and yoga. // 3 //
'the Blessed <s>Ādhāra</s>' —

children.text: śeṣākhyaṃ muniṃ samyagārādhya paramārthopadeśasvarūpaṃ pṛṣṭavān / tadā tadyogyatāparipākasvarūpapariśīlanakrameṇa
children.translated_text: the sage called <s>Śeṣa</s>, he asked about the supreme reality in the form of the teaching of the highest truth. Then, in the course of examining the maturation of his fitness,
'him' —

children.text: śiṣyaṃ vigalitāntaḥkaraṇaṃ matvā so 'pyanantanātho niḥśeṣaśāstropadeśajñaḥ paramārthasāranāmnā
children.translated_text: that disciple, knowing that his inner faculties had dissolved, he too — <s>Anantanātha</s> (the Lord of the Infinite), knower of the teaching of all treatises without exception — [taught him] by the name <s>Paramārthasāra</s>,
'through the <s>Ādhāra</s> verses' —

children.text: ityaparābhidhānagranthena sāṃkhyanayoktopadeśānusāreṇa prakṛtipuruṣavivekajñānātparabrahmāvāptirityevametaṃ śiṣyaṃ proktavān / sa eva brahmopadeśaḥ paramādvayasvarūpasvasvātantryadṛṣṭyā pratipāditaḥ sanyuktiyukto bhavatīti matvā sarvaṃ janamanugrahītuṃ paramādvayaśaivanayayuktyā
children.translated_text: that is, through the text of another name [i.e., the <s>Ādhārakārikā</s>], following the teaching stated in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system — namely, that the attainment of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> comes through the discriminative knowledge of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness) — thus he instructed this disciple. That very teaching of <s>Brahman</s>, when presented through the perspective of the supreme non-dual freedom, becomes well-reasoned and proper. Thinking thus, in order to benefit all people, through the reasoning of the supreme non-dual Śaiva system,
'the <s>Guru</s>, by <s>Abhinava</s>' —
by an extraordinary, supernatural flash of the splendor of consciousness,
'<s>gupta</s>' (hidden) —
secret, mysterious. And this is a blessed series of letters bearing an auspicious name [i.e., Abhinavagupta].
'that essence' (<s>tatsāram</s>) —

children.text: tasya paramārthopadeśasya yatsāraṃ dadhno navanītamivopādeyaṃ parānugrahapravṛttaḥ sanpratipādayatīti / evaṃ saṃbandhābhidheyābhidhānaprayojanādaya upapāditā neha punaḥ śāstragauravabhayātpratanyante / kīdṛśaḥ sa śiṣya ityāha
children.translated_text: that which is the essence of that teaching of the supreme reality — like butter from curd, the most desirable — being engaged in benefiting others, he sets forth. Thus the connection, subject matter, designation, purpose, and so forth have been established; they are not expanded upon here for fear of making the treatise too long. Of what character is that disciple? He says:
'dwelling in the womb' (<s>garbhādhivāsa</s>) —

children.text: iti / garbhādhivāsaprārambhaṃ jāyate 'sti vardhate vipariṇamate 'pakṣīyate vinaśyatīti tattadavasthāvaicitryeṇa ṣaḍbhāvavikāranemiyuktaṃ yat
children.translated_text: that is, the cycle of the six modifications of existence (<s>ṣaḍbhāvavikāra</s>) — beginning with dwelling in the womb: one is born, exists, grows, transforms, declines, and perishes — with the variety of these different states,
'of the nature of suffering ending in death' (<s>maraṇāntakaduḥkharūpam</s>) —
like a wheel, by virtue of the nature of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), through appearance and disappearance,
'wheel' (<s>cakram</s>) —
in that [wheel],
'bewildered' (<s>vibhrāntaḥ</s>) —

children.text: viparivṛttaḥ / anenāsya prāgjātismaraṇasvabhāvo bodhāvirbhāvo dyotito 'nyathā kathaṃ kāṣṭhāprāptilakṣaṇaṃ praśnakutūhalitvaṃ syāt / evaṃ ca yaḥ samutpannavairāgyaḥ parameśvarānugrahaśaktividdhahṛdayaḥ samuditasamyagjñāna upadeśapātratāmavāpya parameśvarākāraṃ samucitamapi guruṃ samāsādya paramādvayajñānamabhilaṣate sa eva ca gurūpadeśabhājanaṃ syāditi / etadeva cānyatroktam
children.translated_text: revolving. By this, his awakening (<s>bodha</s>) — characterized by the remembrance of former births — is indicated; otherwise, how could there be the curiosity of questioning that marks the attainment of the ultimate point? And thus, he who has arisen in dispassion, whose heart has been pierced by the grace-power (<s>anugrahaśakti</s>) of the Supreme Lord, in whom right knowledge has dawned, having attained the fitness to receive instruction and having approached a suitable <s>Guru</s> who is of the nature of the Supreme Lord, desires the supreme non-dual knowledge — he alone is fit to receive the <s>Guru</s>'s instruction. And this has been stated elsewhere:

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] A certain [disciple], in whom dispassion had arisen by the grace of the Blessed Lord, whose mind had turned away from <s>saṃsāra</s>, thinking 'I am one who should be instructed by the <s>Guru</s>,' having duly worshipped the true <s>Guru</s>,
'By the force of the descent of grace (<s>śaktipāta</s>), O Goddess, one is led to the true <s>Guru</s>.'
And this will be stated further on here. // 3 //

body.text: adhunā samutpattikrameṇa pīṭhikābandhaṃ vidhāya viśvavaicitryacitre 'smiñjagati pārameśvaramanuttamaṃ svātantryamekameva saṃyojanaviyojanakartṛtvaheturiti tacchaktivikāsameva viśvamaṇḍacatuṣṭayamukhenāvedayangranthamavatārayati
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, having laid the groundwork in the order of manifestation, in order to make known that in this universe — wondrous in the variety of its forms — the supreme, unsurpassed freedom of the Supreme Lord is the sole cause of conjunction and disjunction, and that the universe is nothing but the expansion of His power, he introduces the text through the four eggs (<s>aṇḍa</s>):

children.translated_text: [Verse:] From the fullness of the splendor of His own power, these four eggs (<s>aṇḍas</s>) [are manifested] in division:

children.text: śaktirmāyā prakṛtiḥ pṛthvī ceti prabhāvitaṃ prabhuṇā // 4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, and <s>Pṛthvī</s> — thus brought forth by the Lord. // 4 //
'by the Lord' (<s>prabhuṇā</s>) —

children.text: svatantreṇa bhagavatā maheśvareṇāṇḍacatuṣṭayaṃ viśvācchādakatvena kośarūpatayā vastupiṇḍabhūtam
children.translated_text: by the independent, Blessed <s>Maheśvara</s>, the four eggs — which, by virtue of being the coverings of the universe, are in the form of sheaths, constituting aggregates of reality —
'this' (<s>idam</s>) —
As has been said:

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] By the one whose nature is a solid mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānandaikaghana</s>),
'... an aggregate of reality is called an egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>).'

children.translated_text: 'brought forth' (<s>prabhāvitam</s>) —
manifested, or employed as the agent of [their] creation. By what [reason]? He says:
'from the fullness of the splendor of His own power' (<s>nijaśaktivaibhavabharāt</s>) —
that is,
'His own' (<s>nija</s>) —
belonging to His own Self — that unshared [power] beginning with Will (<s>Icchā</s>) and the rest —
the multitude of powers (<s>śaktipracaya</s>);
of that, the
'splendor' (<s>vaibhava</s>) —
the variegated expansion; and of that, the
'fullness' (<s>bhara</s>) —

children.text: samudrekastasmāditi / bhagavataḥ kila svaśaktivikāsasphāra eva jagannirmāṇam / yaduktaṃ śrīsarvamaṅgalāśāstre
children.translated_text: the overflowing abundance — from that. Indeed, the creation of the universe is nothing but the expansion of the Blessed One's own power (<s>svaśaktivikāsa</s>). As has been stated in the blessed <s>Sarvamaṅgalāśāstra</s>:

body.translated_text: Thus.

children.translated_text: '<s>Śakti</s> and the possessor of <s>Śakti</s> — these are said to be the two categories of reality.
His powers are the entire universe; the possessor of <s>Śakti</s> is <s>Maheśvara</s>.'
'<s>Śakti</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, and <s>Pṛthvī</s>' —

children.text: iti / viśvasya pramātṛprameyarūpasya parāhantācamatkārasārasyāpi svasvarūpāpohanātmākhyātimayī niṣedhavyāpārarūpā yā pārameśvarī
children.translated_text: that is, the supreme, lordly <s>Śakti</s> (<s>pārameśvarī śakti</s>) — which is in the nature of non-recognition (<s>ākhyāti</s>), consisting of the negation-operation of the self-concealment of one's own essential nature — [this applies to] the universe in the form of subjects and objects, whose essence is the savor of the supreme I-consciousness:
'<s>Śakti</s>' —

children.text: saivācchādakatvena bandhakatayā śaktyaṇḍamityucyate / sadāśiveśvaraśuddhavidyātattvaparyantadalaṃ sadvakṣyamāṇamaṇḍatritayamantaḥ samantādgarbhīkṛtyāvatiṣṭhata iti kośarūpatayaiṣā śaktiranena śabdena saṃjñitā / etasminnaṇḍe sadāśiveśvarāvevādhipatī /
children.translated_text: that very [power], by virtue of being a covering, a binding, is called the <s>Śakti</s>-egg (<s>śaktyaṇḍa</s>). It stands having encompassed within itself on all sides the three other eggs to be described, with their portions extending to the principles of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Śuddhavidyā</s>. In the form of a sheath, this <s>Śakti</s> is designated by this word. In this egg, <s>Sadāśiva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> are the presiding lords.

body.translated_text: Of what nature is the enumeration of the four eggs? He says:

body.text: anyacca malatrayasvabhāvaṃ mohamayaṃ bhedaikapravaṇatayā sarvapramātṝṇāṃ bandharūpaṃ puṃstattvaparyantadalaṃ māyākhyamaṇḍamityucyate / tacca vakṣyamāṇamaṇḍadvayamantaḥ samantātsvīkṛtya sthitam / aṇḍādhipatiścātra gahanābhidhāno rudraḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, that which is of the nature of the three impurities (<s>malatrayasvabhāva</s>), consisting of delusion, inclined solely toward differentiation, binding in nature for all subjects, with its portion extending to the <s>Puruṣa</s> principle — this is called the <s>Māyā</s>-egg. And it stands having incorporated within itself on all sides the two eggs to be described. The presiding lord of this egg is the <s>Rudra</s> called 'the Unfathomable' (<s>Gahana</s>).

children.translated_text: '<s>Prakṛti</s>' (primordial nature) —

children.text: kāryakaraṇātmanā pariṇatā satī paśupramātṝṇāṃ bhogyarūpā sukhaduḥkhamoharūpatayā bandhayitrī prakṛtyabhidhānamaṇḍamityucyate / tatrāpi mahāvibhūtiḥ śrībhagavānviṣṇurbhedapradhāno 'ṇḍādhipatiḥ /
children.translated_text: having transformed into the form of effects and instruments, being the object of enjoyment for the bound subjects (<s>paśu-pramātṛ</s>), binding in the form of pleasure, pain, and delusion — this is called the <s>Prakṛti</s>-egg. There too, the blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Mahāvibhūti</s>, predominantly concerned with differentiation, is the presiding lord of the egg.

body.translated_text: Likewise, consisting of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>,

children.translated_text: '<s>Pṛthvī</s>' (Earth) —

children.text: caivaṃ manuṣyasthāvarāntānāṃ pramātṝṇāṃ pratiprākārarūpatayā sthūlakañcukamayī bandhayitrīti kṛtvā pṛthvyaṇḍamityucyate / tatrāpi caturdaśavidhe bhūtasarge pradhānatayāṇḍādhipo bhagavānbrahmeti / evaṃ parameśvaravijṛmbhitamidamaṇḍacatuṣṭayaṃ bhagavatetthaṃ prakāśitaṃ parisphurati // 4 //
children.translated_text: thus, being in the form of a wall-like [enclosure] for subjects ranging from human beings down to immovable entities, binding through gross coverings — this is called the <s>Pṛthvī</s>-egg (Earth-egg). There too, among the fourteen-fold creation of beings, the presiding lord of the egg is the Blessed <s>Brahmā</s>. Thus this fourfold egg, the sport of the Supreme Lord, manifested by the Blessed One in this manner, shines forth. // 4 //

body.translated_text: Likewise,

[Commentary:] Having thus established this fourfold egg, now, with the intent of establishing the nature of the enjoyed and the enjoyer right here, he states a verse for the determination of the nature of the universe:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] Within that, this universe — a continuous stream of manifold bodies, instruments, and worlds;

children.text: bhoktā ca tatra dehī śiva eva gṛhītapaśubhāvaḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: and the enjoyer there is the embodied one — <s>Śiva</s> Himself, who has assumed the condition of a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>). // 5 //
[Commentary:] 'There' (<s>tatra</s>) —
in those four eggs, well-known from scripture (<s>āgama</s>),
'this universe within' (<s>viśvam idam antaḥ</s>) —
exists in the middle. Of what kind? He says:
'manifold' (<s>vicitra</s>) —
that is, differentiated by the distinctions of <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower), in the form of arrangements of various faces, hands, feet, and the like,
'bodies' (<s>tanavaḥ</s>) —
forms, wondrous by virtue of their distinctive configurations. Likewise, surpassing one another through mutual differentiation,
'instruments' (<s>karaṇāni</s>) —

children.text: cakṣurādīni / tadyathā rudrapramātṝṇāṃ niratiśayāni sarvajñatvādiguṇagaṇayuktāni taiḥ kila sarvamidamekasminkṣaṇe yugapajjñāyate saṃpādyate ca / kṣetrajñānāṃ punaretānyeva karaṇāni parameśvaraniyatiśaktiniyantritāni santi ghaṭādipadārthamātrajñānakaraṇasamarthānyeva na taiḥ sarvaṃ jñāyate nāpi kriyate / tatrāpi yogināmatiśayaḥ karaṇānāṃ yanniyatiśaktisamullaṅghanāttadīyaiḥ karaṇaiḥ dūravyavahitaviprakṛṣṭamapi paricchidyate parapramātṛgataṃ ca sukhaduḥkhādi jñāyate / evaṃ ca tiraścāmapi niyatiśaktyā saṃkucitānāmapi manuṣyebhyo 'pyatiśayaḥ karaṇānāṃ vidyate / tadyathā gāvaḥ svagṛhaṃ vyavahitamapi paśyantyaśvā rātrāvapi mārgamīkṣante gṛdhrā yojanaśatagatamapyāmiṣamavalokayanti pakṣiṇo makṣikā maṣakaparyantā ākāśavihāriṇo dṛśyante sarīsṛpā urasā panthānaṃ gacchanti dṛśā ca śṛṇvanti śabdānuṣṭrā dūrādapi gartācchvāsamātreṇa sarpamākarṣayantīti / evaṃ sarvatra karaṇavaicitryamūhyam / tathā
children.translated_text: the eyes and other sense organs — for instance, in the case of <s>Rudra</s>-level subjects, these are unsurpassed, endowed with hosts of qualities such as omniscience; by these, indeed, everything is simultaneously known and accomplished in a single instant. For the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (embodied souls), however, these very same instruments, being regulated by the <s>niyati</s> (limitation) power of the Supreme Lord, are capable only of knowing mere objects such as a pot — not everything is known by them, nor is everything accomplished by them. Even among these, the <s>yogins</s> have a superiority of instruments, because through transcending the <s>niyati</s> power, their instruments can discern even what is distant, hidden, or far removed, and they can know the pleasure and pain belonging to other subjects. Similarly, even for animals, whose instruments are contracted by <s>niyati</s> power, there is a superiority of instruments over humans. For example: cows see their home even when it is hidden from view; horses see the path even at night; vultures observe meat even at a distance of a hundred <s>yojanas</s>; birds and even flies and mosquitoes are seen moving through the sky; serpents travel on their chests and hear sounds with their eyes; camels attract a snake from afar by merely breathing over a pit. Thus the diversity of instruments should be inferred everywhere. Likewise,
the worlds (<s>bhuvanas</s>)
are well-known from scripture, having surpassingly excellent configurations in the shapes of circles, triangles, squares, half-moons, and parasols. Thus,
diverse
— having various surpassingly wonderful natures — of these
bodies, instruments, and worlds, the stream

children.text: aviratabandhapravāho yasminviśvasmiṃstadevaṃvidhaṃ viśvam / evaṃvidhe cātra bhogyasvabhāve viśvasminbhoktrā bhāvyamityāha
children.translated_text: is an unceasing flow of connection, in which this universe abides and is of such a nature. And in this universe, which is of the nature of the enjoyed, there must be an enjoyer — thus he says:
"And the enjoyer there is the embodied one"

children.text: iti / malatrayāghrāto deho bhogāyatanaṃ vidyate yasyāṇoḥ sa
children.translated_text: — the one who, being the <s>aṇu</s> (limited soul), scented by the three <s>malas</s> (impurities), has a body (<s>deha</s>) as the seat of enjoyment, that
embodied one (<s>dehī</s>),
whose nature is pleasure, pain, and the like, the embodied one, in this realm whose nature is pleasure, pain, and the like, is the
enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>),

children.text: sukhaduḥkhādyanubhavitā paśupramāteti kathyate / nanu parapramātrapekṣayāṇumātrasyāpi na bhedo vidyate kutastadvyatirikto dehī nāma varākaḥ / yaduktam
children.translated_text: the experiencer of pleasure, pain, and so forth — he is called the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) subject. But if in relation to another subject there is no difference even in the slightest particle of the <s>aṇu</s>, then who is this wretched 'embodied one' distinct from that? As it has been said:

body.translated_text: "Even a portion of <s>Brahman</s> does not transcend its universal nature, and is beyond conceptualization."
"And even in each single <s>tattva</s> (reality-principle), the nature of all thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> is present."

body.text: iti nyāyāccaika eva svaśaktiyukto mahāprakāśavapureva parameśvaraḥ pramātā sarvato 'bhinna evāvabhāsate / tato bhinnasyāprakāśamānasya dehino 'stitvābhyupagame 'pi prakāśamānatvānupapatterna sattā niścīyate / prakāśate cettasminparabrahmātmani tarhi prakāśābhinna evaikaḥ pramāteti punarapi kiṃparatvenāyaṃ bhogyabhoktṛlakṣaṇaḥ sanbheda iti sarvaṃ samarthayamāna āha

children.translated_text: "<s>Śiva</s> himself, having assumed the condition of a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>)"
— this Blessed One who has just been established as a compact mass of consciousness and bliss, whose nature is absolute freedom,
<s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: sa eva svarūpagopanāsatattvaḥ sansvecchayā naṭa iva dehapramātṛbhūmikāṃ samāpannaḥ pālyatvātpaśutvātpaśusattālakṣaṇaśca sukhaduḥkhādimaye svayaṃnirmite 'sminbhogye bhoktā dehīti kathyate na punaḥ śivavyatiriktaṃ kiñcitpadārthajātamasti / eṣa eva ca bhagavāñśivaḥ svātantryādbhoktṛbhogyalakṣaṇaṃ pramātṛprameyayugalakaṃ krīḍanakamiva samutthāpayati yadapekṣayāyaṃ bhedapradhāno vyavahāraḥ / tasmādetadeva parameśvarasya svātantryaṃ niratiśayaṃ yatpūrṇasvarūpatāparityāgena bhoktṛbhogyasvabhāvaṃ paśubhāvamāpanno 'pi sarvapramātṝṇāmanubhavitṛtayā svātmani prasphurañcidānandaikaghanaḥ śiva eva // 5 //
children.translated_text: he himself, whose essence is the concealment of his own true nature, by his own will, like an actor, having assumed the role of an embodied subject — being protected and therefore in the condition of a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), characterized by the state of a bound being — in this realm of enjoyment that is of the nature of pleasure, pain, and so forth, and which is self-created, he is called the enjoyer, the embodied one. But apart from <s>Śiva</s>, no category of entities whatsoever exists. And this very Blessed <s>Śiva</s>, through his absolute freedom, gives rise to the pair of enjoyer and enjoyed, the dyad of subject and object, like a plaything — in relation to which this conventional usage centered on difference operates. Therefore, this alone is the unsurpassed absolute freedom of the Supreme Lord: that while not abandoning his complete nature, even having assumed the condition of a bound soul whose nature is enjoyer and enjoyed, by being the experiencer of all subjects, pulsating in his own Self, he is <s>Śiva</s> himself — a compact mass of consciousness and bliss. (5)

body.translated_text: According to this principle, there is only one subject — the Supreme Lord, who is endowed with his own powers, whose very form is the great Light, and who appears as entirely non-different everywhere. Therefore, even if the existence of a separate embodied one who does not appear is accepted, since it is impossible for it to be luminous, its existence cannot be ascertained. If it does shine forth in that supreme <s>Brahman</s>-Self, then it is one single subject, non-different from luminosity — so again, with respect to what other principle is this distinction, characterized as enjoyed and enjoyer, posited? Resolving all this, he says:

body.text: evamapyekaścitsvabhāvaḥ pramātā sa yadi māyādipramātṛprameyavaicitryeṇa nānātvādaneka iti kathaṃ viruddhayaikatayā vyavahriyata ekaścetkimiti nānārūpa iti cchāyātapavadvirodhādviruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ samāpatati na punaranekarūpa ekaśca padārthaḥ syāt / yaduktam
body.translated_text: Even so, if this one subject whose nature is consciousness, having assumed the states of body, instrument, and world, has thereby become many, then upon the destruction of body and so forth, he himself would be destroyed; and upon their arising, he himself would arise. Thus, for each individual subject, he himself would be subject to the six modifications of existence — being born, existing, and so forth — and through the variety of <s>karma</s> (actions) whose nature is merit and demerit, this very Blessed One would obtain enjoyments such as heaven and hell. How then can it be said that he is <s>Śiva</s> in his own true nature? He resolves even this through an illustration:

body.text: ayameva bhedo bhedaheturbhāvānāṃ yadviruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ kāraṇabhedo vā /
body.translated_text: "Even this difference, which is the cause of difference among entities — namely the superimposition of contradictory properties, or the difference of cause —"

body.text: iti / laukikamatra dṛṣṭāntaṃ pradarśayandārṣṭāntike codyaṃ samarthayate
body.translated_text: — presenting a worldly illustration here, he resolves the objection in the matter to be illustrated:

children.translated_text: "Just as a pure crystal takes on the form of various colors,"
"so too the Lord assumes the form of gods, humans, animals, plants, and other beings. (6)"
Just as
a single
crystal gem,

children.text: tattallākṣānīlādyupādhivaicitryasahasreṇa tattadvaicitryaṃ svātmani dhārayaṃstathā vicitrito bhavati na punastasya sphaṭikatāhāniretāvatā samutpadyate / etadeva sphaṭikamaṇermaṇitvaṃ yattattadviśeṣeṇācchurite 'pi tasminsphaṭikamaṇirayamityabādhitā sarvasya sarvadaiva pratītiḥ / kevalamatrāmī lākṣādayaḥ sphurantīti vyavahriyate na punarlākṣādyupādhiḥ paṭamiva taṃ viśinaṣṭi yena svarūpavipralopo 'sya syāt / tasmādetadevāmalatvaṃ maṇeryadupādhirūpānākārānbibharti svasvarūpatayā ca prathate / tathaivāyamīśvaraḥ svatantraścidekaghana ekako 'pi svacche svātmadarpaṇe devamanuṣyapaśupakṣisthāvarāntānāṃ rudrakṣetrajñādipadārtharūpāṇāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ svayaṃ nirmitānāṃ ca
children.translated_text: bearing within itself the variety of this or that color through the thousands of adventitious conditions (<s>upādhis</s>) such as red lac, blue, and so forth, becomes thus variegated — yet its crystal-nature is not at all lost thereby. This alone is the gem-nature of the crystal: that even though it is tinged with this or that particular color, the cognition 'this is a crystal gem' remains unobstructed for everyone at all times. It is merely said that 'these colors of lac and so forth appear in it,' but the adventitious condition of lac does not cut through it like cloth, so as to cause a dissolution of its true nature. Therefore, this very purity of the gem is that which bears the reflections of the adventitious forms while also manifesting as its own true nature. In exactly the same way, this Lord, who is autonomous, a compact mass of consciousness alone, singular, reflects in the clear mirror of his own Self the forms of the particulars — gods, humans, animals, birds, down to immovable things — which are of the nature of <s>Rudra</s>, <s>kṣetrajña</s>, and other categories, and which are self-created,
the state of having form,

children.text: varṇavaicitryaṃ sphaṭikamaṇivatsvātmābhedena dhārayaṃstato 'pi samuttīrṇatvādahamityevamakhaṇḍacamatkāropabṛṃhitaṃ nānārūpamapyekaṃ svātmānaṃ pratyavamṛśati / itthamapyasyaikatākhaṇḍanāmayo bhinnarūpo deśaḥ kālo vā na kaścidvidyate yadapekṣayaitasya svātmamaheśvarasya viruddhadharmādhyāsādidūṣaṇamucyetāpi / sākṣātkāralakṣaṇaṃ citrajñānaṃ nānābhedasaṃbhinnamapi parairapyekameva tadabhyupagatam / yathā
children.translated_text: the variety of appearances, like a crystal gem, bearing them in non-difference from his own Self, and yet transcending even that, reflecting upon his own Self as one yet of manifold forms, enriched with the unbroken wonder of 'I.' Even so, there is no place or time of differentiated form in which the indivisibility of his oneness might be broken, with respect to which the fault of superimposition of contradictory properties could be stated of this great Lord who is the Self. Direct perception in the form of variegated cognition, even though imbued with manifold distinctions, is accepted as one even by others. As it is said:
"Blue and so forth in variegated cognition, being an adventitious condition of knowledge, is non-separate;
one who is unable to perceive it falls into error by trying to discriminate it with respect to the object."

body.text: iti pramāṇavārtike / kiṃ punaḥ sarvataḥ pūrṇasya jñātuścidekavapuṣaḥ svatantrasya yāvimau deśakālau bhedakatayābhimatau mūrtivaicitryakriyāvaicitryābhyāṃ yasya samullāsakatayā sthitau kathaṃ tasyaiva bhagavato vyavacchedakau syātām / yadi nāma deśakālayoḥ kadācitsaṃvido bhedena sthitirabhaviṣyattadā tatkṛto 'pi viruddhadharmādhyāsa udapatsyateti tatra saṃbhāvanā syāt / yāvatā tayoḥ saṃvitprakāśenaiva svātmasattāsiddhiriti siddha evānekasvabhāvo 'pyeka eva maheśvaraścinmūrtirbhedadharme punarviruddhadharmādhyāso duruddhara eveti // 6 //
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s>. Moreover, for the knower who is complete in every respect, whose form is consciousness alone, who is autonomous — how could these very space and time, which are regarded as causes of difference, and which exist as the efflorescence of his variety of forms and variety of activities, be delimiters of that very Blessed One? If indeed there were ever a standing of consciousness in distinction from space and time, then a superimposition of contradictory properties caused by that would arise, and suspicion regarding it would be warranted. But inasmuch as for these two, their very self-existence is established only through the light of consciousness — it is thus proven that the great Lord, whose form is consciousness, though of manifold nature, is indeed one; while the superimposition of contradictory properties in the domain of difference remains truly impossible to sustain. (6)

body.text: nanveka eva saṃvitsatattvaḥ pramātābhyupagatastanukaraṇabhuvanatāṃ samāpannaḥ sansa evānekatāṃ yāta iti cettarhi tanvādivināśe sa eva vinaṣṭaḥ syāttadutpattau vaiṣa eva tadotpadyeta / evaṃ pratipramātṛ sa eva jāyate 'stītyādiṣaḍbhāvavikāratayā vyavacchidyate puṇyapāpasvabhāvakarmavaicitryeṇaitasyaiva bhagavataḥ svarganarakādibhogaḥ prāpta iti kathamucyate svasvarūpa eva śiva iti / dṛṣṭāntadvāreṇaitadapi samarthayate
body.translated_text: But if one single subject, whose essence is the reality of consciousness, is accepted, and he, having assumed the states of body, instrument, and world, has thereby become many, then upon the destruction of body and so forth, he himself would be destroyed, and upon their arising, he himself would arise. Thus for each individual subject, he himself would be cut off through the six modifications of existence — being born, existing, and so forth — and through the variety of <s>karma</s> whose nature is merit and demerit, this very Blessed One would obtain enjoyments of heaven, hell, and so forth. How then can it be said that he is <s>Śiva</s> in his own true nature? He resolves even this through an illustration:

children.text: gacchati gacchati jala iva himakarabimbaṃ sthite sthitiṃ yāti /
children.translated_text: "As the disc of the moon in water appears to move when the water moves, and appears to be still when it is still,"
"so too this Self, the great Lord, in the array of body, instrument, and world. (7)"
the disc of the moon,
the lunar body, though in reality situated in the sky, itself motionless by nature, though it has fallen into the stream of water, that
moves
— goes,
as it were.

children.text: tathā tasminneva kṣaṇe 'nyatra jalāśaye niḥstimite sati tadeva
children.translated_text: Likewise, at that very moment, when in another body of water it is still, that very
disc of the moon appears to attain stillness

children.text: gacchatīvetyubhayathā sarvapramātṛbhiretatsaṃbhāvyate na punaḥ paramārthena tattathaiva syāt / nāpi jalagatau deśakālau bhedakatayā candramasaḥ svarūpaṃ gaganasthaṃ parāmṛśataḥ kevalaṃ jalameva tādṛśamatha ca tatpratibimbitasya candrabimbasya jalagatacalattācalattādiko bhedo vyavahriyata ityetāvatā gaṅgājalagatasya kardamapatitasya vā śaśinaḥ svasvarūpatāyāṃ na kācitkṣatiḥ /
children.translated_text: — thus in both ways this is imagined by all subjects, but in ultimate reality it is not so. Nor do space and time pertaining to the movement of water touch the true nature of the moon situated in the sky as causes of difference; it is the water alone that is of such a nature. And although the reflected disc of the moon in water is conventionally said to have the difference of movement and stillness pertaining to water, by this much there is no harm whatsoever to the moon's own true nature, whether it be in the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> or fallen in mud.
In exactly the same way, this Self,
whose nature is consciousness, in the self-created
aggregate of body, instrument, and world,

children.text: parikṣīṇe sati samutpanne vā prakṣīṇaḥ samutpannaśceti māyāvyāmohitānāṃ vyavahāramātrametajjalagatacandravanna punaḥ svātmā jāyate mriyate veti / gītāsvevamevoktam
children.translated_text: when it perishes or arises, is spoken of as having perished or arisen — but this is merely conventional usage for those deluded by <s>māyā</s>, like the moon reflected in water; his own Self is not actually born or does not die. As it is stated in the <s>Gītā</s> itself:

body.translated_text: Just as, when a stream of water flows,

children.text: na jāyate mriyate vā kadacinnāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He is never born and never dies, nor having once been does he ever cease to be;

children.text: ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre //
children.translated_text: unborn, eternal, everlasting, primeval, he is not slain when the body is slain."

body.text: iti / tasmādayamātmā maheśānaḥ svatantraḥ sarvasvātmapratyavamarśasvabhāvaḥ sarvapramātṝṇāmanubhavitṛtayā prathamānastatastattadavasthāvipralope samutpattau vā svasvarūpa eva / etadeva ca durghaṭakāri maheśānatvaṃ saṃvittattvasya yattathā tathā paśupramātṛtayā svarganarakādibhogabhoktāpi sarvānubhavitṛtayā saṃvitsvarūpa eva / pratyuta puṇyapāpasvarganarakakṣutpipāsādiko yo 'yaṃ paśubhāvo bandhakatayā niyataḥ sa yadi bhagavatā svātmaprakāśena prakāśitaḥ parāmṛṣṭaśca syāttadā yathoktāṃ svātmani sattāṃ labhate 'nyathā niḥsvabhāva evaiṣa iti kathaṃ svātmanaḥ tasyaiva maheśasya svarūpavipralopāyocyate / sarvathā nirmitameva vastu saṃhāryaṃ samutpādyaṃ vā dehādirūpaṃ syānna punaḥ nitye bhagavati caitanye samutpattivināśau kadācidbhavetām / tasmādeka evātmā grāhyagrāhakatayā nānārūpasvabhāvaḥ sanpunarapi sarvānubhavitṛtayā sarvasyaikatayā prathata iti na kācidadvayavādakṣatiḥ // 7 //
body.translated_text: Therefore this Self, the great Lord, who is autonomous, whose nature is the self-reflection of everything as his own Self, who manifests as the experiencer of all subjects — even in the dissolution or arising of this or that state, he is in his own true nature. And this alone is the hard-to-accomplish lordship of the reality of consciousness: that in such and such a way, even while being the enjoyer of the enjoyments of heaven, hell, and so forth in the condition of a bound subject, through being the experiencer of all, he is in his very nature as consciousness. On the contrary, the bound condition — merit, demerit, heaven, hell, hunger, thirst, and so forth — which is fixed as bondage, if illuminated and reflected upon by the Blessed One through the light of his own Self, then it obtains the existence described in his own Self; otherwise, it is utterly without essence — so how can it be said to cause the dissolution of the true nature of that very great Lord, the Self? In every way, only a created thing — in the form of body and so forth — can be destroyed or produced, but in the eternal Blessed consciousness, origination and destruction can never occur. Therefore, the Self is one alone; though of manifold nature in the form of grasped and grasper, yet again through being the experiencer of all, manifesting the oneness of everything — thus there is no harm to the teaching of non-duality. (7)

body.text: itthamapi sarveṣāmayamātmā viśvaprapañcasvabhāva eva saṃvinmātraparamārthaḥ sarvāvabhāsaḥ sarvatra saṃvidanugamāditi yuktyāgamābhyāṃ pratipāditaścetkimiti loṣṭādāvapyaviśeṣātsvātmatayā sa na pratīyate 'bhyupagame vā jaḍājaḍavyavastheyaṃ bhāsamānā na saṃgacchate lokavyavahāraśca jaḍājaḍarūpa iti kathametatsyādityāha
body.translated_text: Even so, if this Self of all beings is indeed of the nature of the entire phenomenal expansion, whose ultimate reality is pure consciousness alone, the illuminator of everything, since consciousness pervades everywhere — as has been established by both reasoning and scripture — why then is he not recognized as one's own Self even in a clod of earth and the like, since there is no difference? Or if this is accepted, how does this manifest distinction between sentient and insentient hold? And if worldly convention has the nature of sentient and insentient, how can this be? To this he says:

children.translated_text: "Just as <s>Rāhu</s>, though invisible, becomes visible when situated in the disc of the moon, so too"
"this Self, though all-pervading, is seen in the mirror of intellect through its association with objects. (8)"
<s>Rāhu</s>,

children.text: sarvatra paribhramannapi nopalabhyate sa eva punargrahoparāgakāle candramūrtisthaḥ prathamāno 'yaṃ rāhuriti parīkṣyate 'nyathā sthito 'pi bhacakre 'sthita iva / tathaivehāpi sarvāntaratamatvena sthito 'pi
children.translated_text: though revolving everywhere, is not perceived. That very same <s>Rāhu</s>, however, at the time of a planetary eclipse, being situated in the lunar disc, manifesting, is observed as 'this is <s>Rāhu</s>' — otherwise, though present in the zodiac, it is as if not present. In exactly the same way here too, even though situated as the innermost of all,
this Self

children.text: svānubhavaikasvarūpatayā pratyakṣaparidṛśyamānaḥ sarvasya tathā nopalakṣyate / yadā punaḥ puryaṣṭakapramātṝṇāṃ buddhidarpaṇe pratibhāmukure grāhyavyavasthākāle śabdādiviṣayasvīkāreṇa śṛṇomītyevamahaṃpratītiviṣayo bhavati tadā grāhakasvabhāvatayā loṣṭādāvapi sthitaḥ sansphuṭarūpastatraiva svātmā
children.translated_text: Although directly perceivable to all as having the nature of self-experience alone, He is not recognized by all as such. But when, in the mirror of the intellect of the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body) subjects, at the time of the determination of the cognizable — at the reflective mirror — through the apprehension of objects such as sound and the like, He becomes the object of the self-awareness 'I hear,' then, as the subject-nature, though present even in a clod of earth, His own self
shines forth

children.text: sarvaiśca svānubhavaikarūpaḥ pratīyate loṣṭādāvatyantatamomayatvātsthito 'pyasthitakalpo 'sau prathate rāhurākāśe yathā / evamayaṃ bhagavānmāyāśaktyā svātmakalpe 'pi bhāvavarge kāṃścitpuryaṣṭakasvarūpānvedyakhaṇḍānapyahantāvyavasthārasābhiṣiktānvedakīkaroti kāṃścidvedyīkaroti yadapekṣayāyaṃ jaḍājaḍavyavasthāsvarūpo bhedavyavahāraḥ susthita evopapadyate / tena loṣṭādirvedyatvājjaḍo vedakatvātpuryaṣṭakapramātāpyajaḍaḥ / na punaḥ paramārthena parameśvarāpekṣayā jaḍājaḍavyavahāra iti // 8 //
children.translated_text: clearly there itself, and He is apprehended by all as having the nature of self-experience alone. Though present even in a clod of earth, because of its utter darkness, He is as if not present. He appears like <s>Rāhu</s> in the sky. In the same way, this Blessed Lord, through <s>Māyāśakti</s> (the power of illusion), even in the realm of entities that are of His own nature, makes certain <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> subjects — portions of the cognizable — into cognizers, anointed with the essence of the I-determination, and makes certain [entities] into the cognizable. With respect to this, the distinction between sentient and insentient is well established as a form of differentiated usage. Therefore, a clod of earth, being cognizable, is insentient; while the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> subject, being a cognizer, is also non-insentient. But in ultimate reality, from the standpoint of the Supreme Lord, there is no usage of insentient and non-insentient. // 8 //

body.translated_text: In the region of space,

body.text: nanu sarvapramātṝṇāṃ buddhau cetsvātmano 'pyaviśeṣeṇa prasphuraṇaṃ tarhi te sarve kimiti svātmavido na syustajjñānavanto mā vā bhūvanviśeṣābhāvāt / yatpunaḥ saṃsārāvasthāyāmapi kecana svātmajñānājjīvanmuktāḥ sarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvaśālinaḥ kecana svātmajñānayogyā ārurukṣavaśca dṛśyante 'pare svātmajñānarahitāḥ santo dharmādharmanimittaśubhāśubhakarmanigaḍaprabandhabaddhāḥ saṃsāriṇa eveti kathametatsaṃgacchata itthamantaḥ sarvaṃ kṛtvā pārameśvaraḥ śaktipāto viśṛṅkhala iti pratipādayati
body.translated_text: Objection: If the self shines forth without distinction in the intellect of all subjects, then why are they not all knowers of the self? Should they be possessors of that knowledge, or should they not be, since there is no distinction? Moreover, even in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, some are seen to be <s>jīvanmuktas</s> (liberated while living), endowed with omniscience and omnipotence through self-knowledge; some are aspirants who are fit for self-knowledge; and others, devoid of self-knowledge, are bound by the continuous chain of auspicious and inauspicious deeds conditioned by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, remaining mere <s>saṃsārins</s> (worldly beings) — how does all this cohere? To this, having made the inner purport of everything, [the author] demonstrates that the descent of the Lord's power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) is unrestrained:

children.translated_text: Just as a face shines in a mirror free from impurity,
so in the intellect-principle purified by <s>Śiva</s>'s descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>), the one whose nature is radiance shines forth. // 9 //

body.text: darpaṇe mālinyarahite yathā nirviśeṣarūpādiguṇagaṇayuktaṃ mukhaṃ cakāsti / na sa deśo 'sti yaṃ vinivṛttamala ādarśo na svīkurute / samale darpaṇe tu mukhamananyātiśayamapi dhyāmalatvādvaiparītyena prakāśate / nāpi malinastadīyānguṇānsvīkartumalam / pratyuta tannyastamukhaḥ pumānmukhamanyathaiva dhyāmalatvādyupetamavalokya svātmano lajjāmāvahati vikṛtaṃ madvadanamiti / tathaiva

children.translated_text: of <s>Śiva</s>,
of the self — that which is called grace (<s>anugraha</s>),
the <s>śakti</s> (power),
of that [power],
the descent (<s>pāta</s>) —

when by the spreading of its rays the reflective mirror [of intellect] has been cleansed, purified through the eradication of the latent impressions of the <s>āṇava</s> (innate), <s>māyīya</s> (illusory), and <s>kārma</s> (karmic) impurities, then in certain subjects who are in their final birth,
<s>bhā</s>
(radiance),
<s>rūpa</s>
(the nature of which is [radiance]) —
the one whose nature is radiance (<s>bhārūpa</s>),

children.text: svātmā yāvatsarvajñatvādiguṇagaṇayuktastāvānapyavabhāsate yena kecanaiva te svātmasvarūpaprathanātsaṃsāramadhyapatitā api muktakalpāḥ sātiśayāśca / keṣāñcideva parameśvaratirodhānaśaktyāṇavamāyīyakārmamalasamācchādite buddhitattve bhārūpo 'pyātmā mālinyādbhāto 'pyabhātakalpo yena te sāṃsārikāḥ paśava ityabhidhīyante 'nye 'pyubhayaśaktiyogātpramātāra ārurukṣava iti / itthaṃ tīvramandamandatarādibhedena śaktipātavaicitryaṃ sarvatrāpyūhyam / atra na māyāntaḥpātiniyatiśaktisamutthamaśvamedhādikaṃ japadhyānādi vānyadyatkiñcitkarma mocanaheturātmanastasya hi māyātaḥ samuttīrṇatvādbhedapradhānaṃ vastu tatsādhanāya na prakalpate / yadgītam
children.translated_text: the Self, endowed with an array of qualities such as omniscience and the like, shines forth to that extent — whereby certain [beings] alone, through the manifestation of their own essential nature, even though fallen in the midst of <s>saṃsāra</s>, are as if liberated and surpass [others]. In the intellect-principle of certain others, concealed by the Lord's power of concealment (<s>tirodhāna</s>) — the <s>āṇava</s>, <s>māyīya</s>, and <s>kārma</s> impurities — the Self, though of the nature of radiance (<s>bhārūpa</s>), due to impurity appears though present as if unmanifest — whereby they are called <s>paśus</s> (bound souls), worldly beings. Still other subjects, through the conjunction of both powers, are aspirants (<s>ārurukṣu</s>). In this way, the variety of <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power) through distinctions of intense, mild, milder, and so forth, should be inferred everywhere. Here, neither the <s>Aśvamedha</s> and other [rituals] arising from the power of <s>niyati</s> within <s>Māyā</s>, nor <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), nor any other action whatsoever is the cause of the self's liberation — for since He has transcended <s>Māyā</s>, a thing predominantly characterized by duality cannot serve as the means to accomplish that. As it has been sung:

body.translated_text: Just as a face, endowed with an array of qualities such as form and the like in their undifferentiated state, shines in a mirror free from impurity — there is no region that a stainless mirror does not receive — so in an impure mirror, the face, though unsurpassed, appears dimly and distortedly due to the dullness. Nor is the impure [mirror] able to receive its qualities. Rather, a person whose face is placed in it, seeing the face as otherwise — accompanied by dullness and the like — brings shame upon himself: 'My face is distorted!' In the same way,

body.text: nāhaṃ vedairna tapasā na dānena na cejyayā /
body.translated_text: 'Not by the <s>Vedas</s>, not by austerity, not by gifts, not by sacrifice,

body.text: iti / tasmādekamevātra parameśvarānugrahaḥ kāraṇamakṛtrimaṃ bhavyabuddhīnām / yaduktam
body.translated_text: ...' Therefore, the sole cause here is the grace of the Supreme Lord, the unconditioned [cause] for those of awakened intellect. As has been stated:

children.translated_text: 'In the aspect of the Lord's descent of power, the intellect, which reveals His absolute freedom,
touched by the creative power, depends on nothing whatsoever.'

body.text: iti / paśupramātṝṇāṃ tu parameśvaratirodhānaśaktiḥ saṃsaraṇahetureva yenaite svasvarūpāprathanācchubhāśubhakarmaniratāḥ sukhaduḥkhādibhogabhājaḥ punaḥ punarasminsaṃsaranti / tasmātpramātṝṇāṃ sādhāraṇe 'pi svātmani prakāśāprakāśarūpe anugrahatirodhānaśaktī dve eva te mokṣabandhapravibhāgahetū / yaduktam
body.translated_text: But for the <s>paśu</s> (bound) subjects, the Supreme Lord's power of concealment (<s>tirodhāna</s>) is the very cause of transmigration — whereby these [beings], due to the non-manifestation of their own essential nature, engaged in auspicious and inauspicious deeds, experiencing pleasure, pain, and the like, transmigrate again and again in this [world]. Therefore, though the Self is common to all subjects, consisting of manifestation and non-manifestation, the two powers of grace (<s>anugraha</s>) and concealment (<s>tirodhāna</s>) alone are the causes of the division into liberation and bondage. As has been stated:

children.translated_text: 'A certain power of the one of infinite powers binds the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower/soul), unobstructed, with the net of worldly bonds;

children.text: jñānāsinā ca vinikṛtya guṇānaśeṣānanyā karotyabhimukhaṃ puruṣaṃ vimuktau //
children.translated_text: and another, having cut away all the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) with the sword of knowledge, makes the soul face toward liberation.'

body.text: evamidaṃ sarvamāgamānubhavayuktiyuktaṃ pratipādya yatprākśaktyādyaṇḍacatuṣṭayaṃ pratipāditaṃ tadantarālavarti samutpattikrameṇa ṣaṭtriṃśattattvātmakaṃ jagadyallagnaṃ bhāti tatprathamataḥ kāraṇakāraṇaṃ paramaśivasvarūpaṃ kārikādvayenāha
body.translated_text: Having thus established all this, supported by scripture, experience, and reasoning — regarding the fourfold sphere from <s>Śakti</s> onwards that was previously expounded — the universe consisting of thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles) in the order of emanation, which shines as attached to [that sphere], and first of all, the cause of all causes, the essential nature of Supreme <s>Śiva</s> — [the author] states in two <s>kārikās</s>:

children.translated_text: Whose nature is radiance, who is complete, who is the Great Bliss through repose in the Self,
pervaded by will, knowledge, and action, filled with infinite powers — // 10 //
Devoid of all <s>vikalpas</s> (mental constructs), pure, peaceful, free from dissolution and origination —
in that Supreme Principle, the universe consisting of thirty-six [<s>tattvas</s>] shines forth. // 11 //
That which
is of such a nature —
the supreme,

children.text: pūrṇaṃ śivatattvaṃ tatra śivādidharāparyantaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ viśvaṃ viśrāntaṃ satprakāśate tadabhinnameva cakāsadyuktyopapadyata iti yāvat / nanu tanyate sarvaṃ tanvādi yatra tattattvaṃ tananādvā tadāpralayaṃ tasya bhāva iti vā tattvamityevamapi tattvavyapadeśo 'yaṃ jāḍyāpādakaḥ kathaṃ cidrūpe bhagavati paramaśive syāducyate / upadeśyajanāpekṣayā yāvatā śabdena pratipādyate tāvatā tatra tattvavyapadeśo na vastutaḥ / kīdṛśaṃ tatparaṃ tattvam /
children.translated_text: complete <s>Śiva</s>-principle — in that, the entire universe to be described, from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth, rests and shines forth; it gleams as non-different from it — this is established by reasoning. Now, '<s>tattva</s>' [means] that in which everything is extended (<s>tanyate</s>), or [its] state (<s>bhāva</s>) until dissolution through extension (<s>tanana</s>) — even by such etymological designation of <s>tattva</s>, this implies inertness; how could it apply to the Blessed Supreme <s>Śiva</s> whose nature is consciousness? [The author] replies: With respect to those who are to be instructed, whatever word is used for exposition, by that the designation '<s>tattva</s>' applies there — but not in reality. What is this Supreme Principle like?
<s>Bhā</s>
(radiance) —
<s>rūpa</s>
(form/nature) of which is [radiance] — its nature is the great radiance; this is the meaning. Further,
complete (<s>paripūrṇa</s>) —

children.text: nirākāṅkṣam / nirākāṅkṣamapi sphaṭikamaṇidarpaṇādi jaḍaṃ vastu bhavatītyāha
children.translated_text: without any want. But even a crystal gem, a mirror, or the like, though without want, is an inert thing — therefore [the author] says:
'Through repose in the Self, [it is] the Great Bliss' —

children.text: iti / svasminsvabhāve 'khaṇḍāhantācamatkārarase viśramānmahānānandaḥ parā nirvṛtiryasyeti / tadevaṃ paramāhlādakasphurattāsāratvātprakāśyasphaṭikāderjaḍādvailakṣaṇyamuktaṃ bhavati / ata evāha
children.translated_text: the one whose great bliss — supreme delight — consists in resting in one's own nature, in the savor of undivided I-consciousness wonder. Thus, because its essence is the most blissful scintillation, its dissimilarity from the inert, such as a crystal and other illuminable [objects], is stated. Hence [the author] further says:
'Pervaded by will, knowledge, and action' —

children.text: iti / icchājñānakriyāśaktisvabhāvameva na punaḥ śāntabrahmavādināmiva śaktivirahitaṃ jaḍakalpam / anyacca
children.translated_text: its nature is the powers of will (<s>icchā</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>); not like the [Supreme] of the advocates of the quiescent <s>Brahman</s>, devoid of power and virtually inert. And further:
'Filled with infinite powers' —
this [means]:
infinite,
innumerable — the powers that constitute name and form, such as pot, cloth, and the like,
the <s>śaktis</s> (powers),
which are the offshoots of the powers of will, knowledge, and action — the powers <s>Brāhmī</s> and the rest, arising from the aggregate of sounds — by those,
on all sides,
from every direction,
[it is] complete —

children.text: vyāptaṃ tata evollasantyastatraiva śāmyantīti / evaṃ parāvāgrūpaṃ bhagavati svātantryamuktaṃ syāt / nanu vāgrūpaṃ cetparaṃ tattvaṃ tarhi kālpanikaṃ śabdasaṃbhinnatvātkathaṃ śuddhaprakāśavapuṣi kalpanāyoga ityāśayenāha
children.translated_text: pervaded; from that very [source] they flash forth, and in that very [source] they subside. Thus the absolute freedom of the Blessed One, consisting of the supreme and the immanent Speech, is stated. Now, if the Supreme Principle has the form of Speech, then it would be imaginary, being intermixed with words — how could there be a conjunction of imagination in that which has the form of pure radiance? With this intention [the author] says:
'Devoid of all <s>vikalpas</s> (mental constructs)' —

children.text: iti / parapramātari yo 'yaṃ parāhantācamatkāraḥ sa vāgrūpo 'pi nirvikalpaḥ / vikalpo hyanyāpohalakṣaṇo dvayaṃ ghaṭāghaṭarūpamākṣipannaghaṭādvyavacchinnaṃ ghaṭaṃ niścinoti / prakāśasya punaḥ parāhantācamatkārasārasyāpi nāprakāśarūpaḥ prakāśādanyaḥ pratipakṣatayā vidyate yadvyavacchedāttasya vikalparūpatā syāt / vyavacchedyo hyartho 'prakāśātmā prakāśavapuṣi prakāśate cettarhi
children.translated_text: the supreme I-consciousness wonder in the supreme subject, though having the form of Speech, is free from <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction). For <s>vikalpa</s>, characterized by mutual exclusion, involves a duality — grasping the form of pot and non-pot, it ascertains the pot as excluded from non-pot. But for radiance, whose essence is the supreme I-consciousness wonder, there exists no counter-entity that is non-radiance, different from radiance, by the exclusion of which it would assume the nature of <s>vikalpa</s>. For the object that is to be excluded, being of non-luminous nature — if it appears in radiance,

body.translated_text: 'Through being apprehended in the form of that very consciousness, by the recognition of identity [with it]' —

body.text: ityādinyāyena yo 'pyarthaḥ prakāśasvabhāvatāṃ yātaḥ sansa kathaṃ svātmanastasyaiva vyavacchedakaḥ syādyena vikalparūpatāṃ tatra samāvahet / atha pratipakṣatayā na prakāśata iti kathamihāprakāśamānaḥ padārthaḥ pratipakṣarūpo 'stīti paricchettumapi śakyeteti yatkiñcidetatsyāt / yataḥ

children.translated_text: from all
[<s>vikalpas</s>] whose nature is exclusion,
[the Supreme Principle] is devoid —
the Supreme Principle is of an uncircumscribed nature. Hence [the author] further says:
'Pure' (<s>śuddha</s>) —

children.text: iti vimalaṃ vikalpamayyā aśuddhimaṣyā abhāvāt / tathā
children.translated_text: spotless, because of the absence of the impure ink of <s>vikalpa</s>. Likewise:
'Peaceful' (<s>śānta</s>) —
because of the absence of agitation arising from the subject-object [duality], resting in its own nature through the equilibrium of powers — not like a piece of stone. And further:
'Free from dissolution and origination' (<s>layodayavihīna</s>) —
this [means]:

body.translated_text: by this principle, whatever object has assumed the nature of radiance, how could it, being identical with [radiance], be the excluder of its own self, so as to bring about the nature of <s>vikalpa</s> there? If, on the other hand, it does not appear as a counter-entity, then how could an entity that is unmanifest here be determined as having the form of a counter-entity? — all this would be meaningless. For:
'This Self, once having shone forth,' —

body.text: iti kṛtvā sanātana eva / ato bhūtabhaviṣyadvartamānavapuḥ kālastatra na kramate yataḥ kālasya tata eva samullāsa iti samutpattivināśabahiṣkṛte paratattve 'bhyupagate viśvasya viśvatvamupapannamiti pratipāditaṃ syāt // 11 //
body.translated_text: is therefore eternal. Hence time, whose form is past, future, and present, does not advance there, because time itself flashes forth from that very [source]. Thus, when the Supreme Principle is accepted as being beyond origination and destruction, the universality of the universe is established — this is what has been demonstrated. // 11 //

body.text: nanvevaṃvidhe paratattve jagadbhātīti yatpratipāditaṃ tatkathametatsyādyāvatā paratattvāpekṣayā na kiñcidbhedena bhātuṃ pragalbheta / tato bhinnaṃ cejjagadbhāsate tadādvayavādakhaṇḍanābhinnaṃ cejjagatprakāśata iti kathaṃ vācoyuktiriti dṛṣṭāntadvāreṇa tadbhedābhedarūpaṃ tattvamupadarśayannetatsamarthanāyāha
body.translated_text: Objection: It has been demonstrated that the universe shines in such a Supreme Principle — but how could this be, inasmuch as nothing could presume to shine as differentiated with respect to the Supreme Principle? If the universe shines as different [from it], then the position of non-duality would be destroyed; if the universe shines as non-different [from it], then how is the expression [of multiplicity] justified? — Through an illustration, showing the principle as consisting of both difference and non-difference, [the author] states this in order to establish it:

children.translated_text: Just as in the surface of a mirror, a city, village, and the like appear as variegated yet undivided,

children.text: bhāti vibhāgenaiva ca parasparaṃ darpaṇādapi ca // 12 //
children.translated_text: and yet [they appear] as mutually distinct and also distinct from the mirror itself — // 12 //
so too from the most stainless consciousness of the Supreme <s>Bhairava</s>, though void of division,

children.text: anyonyaṃ ca tato 'pi ca vibhaktamābhāti jagadetat // 13 //
children.translated_text: this universe appears as mutually distinct and as distinct from That as well. // 13 //
variegated (<s>citra</s>),
manifold in its distinctive characteristics,
undivided (<s>avibhāgi</s>) —
being undivided from the mirror,
it shines —
it presents its inner form in identity with that [mirror]; though shining in non-difference there, it [also] shines
'as mutually distinct' —

children.text: ityanyonyasvālakṣaṇyena ghaṭātpaṭo bhinnaḥ paṭātghaṭa iti vibhaktatayā sphurati / tadantargatā hi bhāvā eva pṛthaktvena parāmṛśyante na punastaṃ darpaṇaṃ tyaktvā pṛthakkiñcidupalabhyate kintu darpaṇasāmarasyena sthitamapi sarvato bhinnaṃ jagatpratīyate / evamapi ghaṭādipratibimbena darpaṇastarhyantarhitaḥ syādityetannetyāha
children.translated_text: that is, through the distinctive characteristics of each — the pot is different from the cloth, the cloth from the pot — it appears as differentiated. For the entities contained within it are apprehended separately, yet nothing is obtained separately apart from that mirror; rather, though everything rests in identity with the mirror, the universe is perceived as distinct from every side. Yet, [one may object:] then the mirror would be concealed by the reflections of pot and the like — this is not so, [the author] says:
'And also from the mirror' —

children.text: iti / na kevalaṃ svayaṃ bhāvā darpaṇāntargatā api bhinnāḥ prakāśante yāvaddarpaṇādapi vyatiricyante yato darpaṇastattatpratibimbamayo 'pi tebhyaḥ pratibimbebhyaḥ samuttīrṇasvarūpatayā cakāsti na punastanmayaḥ saṃpadyate yena ca na darpaṇa iti pratītaḥ syāt / sarvasya punastattatpratibimbagrahaṇe 'pi darpaṇo 'yamityabādhitā pratipattiḥ / nāpi ghaṭādirdarpaṇaṃ viśinaṣṭi yenāyaṃ ghaṭadarpaṇo 'yaṃ paṭadarpaṇa iti svasvarūpatāhāniratra jāyate / deśakṛtaḥ kālakṛto vā bhedo na tatra svabhāvavipralopāya bhavati / tasmāttattatpratibimbasahiṣṇuḥ sansvātmani darpaṇo darpaṇa eveti na kācitpratibimbavādakṣatiḥ / athocyate bhrāntireṣā yaduta darpaṇe hastīti parāmṛśyate na tu punardarpaṇe sa kaścidvidyate tathātvenārthakriyāvirahādbhrāntyaivaiṣa niścaya iti / etāvatā pratibimbavādena dṛṣṭāntastāvatsiddhaḥ / bhrāntestu svarūpaṃ samanantaraṃ nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: Thus — not only do the objects themselves appear as distinct within the mirror, but they also transcend the mirror, because the mirror, even though consisting of those various reflections, shines forth as having a nature that rises above those reflections — it does not become identical with them, so that one would fail to perceive it as a mirror. Rather, even while grasping all those reflections, the cognition 'this is a mirror' remains uncontradicted. Nor does a pot or the like obscure the mirror such that one would say 'this is a pot-mirror' or 'this is a cloth-mirror' — the loss of its own nature does not occur here. A difference based on space or time does not there cause the destruction of its essential nature. Therefore, the mirror, while accommodating all those reflections, remains a mirror in its own self — thus there is no damage to the reflection doctrine. Now if one objects: 'This is an error — namely, that one apprehends an elephant in the mirror; but no such thing exists in the mirror as such, and since there is no capacity for real action, this cognition is merely an error' — by this much, the reflection doctrine has established the analogy. The nature of error itself will be examined immediately after.
Likewise (<s>tadvat</s>),
in the same way, by the analogy of reflections in a mirror, a city, and the like,
from the utterly pure supreme <s>Bhairava</s>-consciousness (<s>bodha</s>),
from that light (<s>prakāśa</s>) in which temporality has been supremely dissolved, overflowing with full bliss (<s>pūrṇānanda</s>),
the world (<s>jagat</s>),
the universe,
though devoid of [real] differentiation,

children.text: darpaṇapratibimbavattataḥ prakāśādavibhaktamapi parasparaṃ ca vibhaktatvena grāhyagrāhakāpekṣayā nānārūpaṃ prathate
children.translated_text: like a reflection in a mirror — though undivided from that light, yet appearing as divided from each other, manifests in diverse forms with respect to the grasped and the grasper —
and furthermore from that [consciousness],
thus appearing as if emerged even from consciousness —
it shines forth,

children.text:
yato bodhastadrūpatayāpi prathamānastataḥ samuttīrṇaḥ prathate yathā pratibimbebhyo darpaṇaḥ
/ evamapi viśvabhāvapratibimbasahiṣṇuḥ prakāśo viśvabhāvebhyaḥ samuttīrṇaḥ sarvasyānubhavitṛtayā svasvarūpeṇa prathate / bhāvagato 'pi deśakālākārabhedaḥ kevalamatra prakāśate darpaṇavanna punaḥ svaṃ rūpaṃ saṃbhinatti / ata evaikānekasvarūpo 'pi bodha eka eva bodhābhyupagatacitrajñānavat / kintu darpaṇaprakāśātsacamatkārasya citprakāśasyeyānviśeṣo yaddarpaṇe svacchatāmātrasanāthe bhinnaṃ bāhyameva nagarādi pratibimbatvenābhimataṃ bhāti na tu svanirmitamato darpaṇe 'yaṃ hastīti yo niścayaḥ sa bhrāntaḥ syātprakāśaḥ punaḥ svacamatkārasāraḥ svecchayā svātmabhittāvabhedena parāmṛśansvasaṃvidupādānameva viśvamābhāsayati / viśvasyābhāsanameva nirmātṛtvaṃ bhagavata iti parāmarśa eva prakāśasya jaḍāddarpaṇaprakāśādervailakṣaṇyāpādakaṃ mukhyaṃ rūpamiti / etadeva granthakṛtā vivṛtivimarśinyāmuktam
children.translated_text:
because consciousness, even while manifesting as having the nature of that [universe], shines forth as transcending it — just as a mirror [transcends] its reflections.
Even so, the light (<s>prakāśa</s>), while accommodating the reflections of all states of being, shines forth by its own essential nature as the experiencer of everything, transcending all states of being. The differentiation of space, time, and form, though present within the realm of objects, merely appears there, as in a mirror, and does not fragment its own nature. Therefore, consciousness (<s>bodha</s>), though of the nature of both unity and multiplicity, is one alone — like the variegated knowledge contained within accepted consciousness. However, this is the distinction between the light of consciousness (<s>cit-prakāśa</s>), which is replete with self-awareness (<s>camatkāra</s>), and the light of a [mere] mirror: in a mirror, which possesses only transparency, it is the external city and the like, as separate, that appears as reflection — the mirror does not create it; therefore the judgment 'this is an elephant in the mirror' would be erroneous. But the light [of consciousness], whose essence is self-awareness, fashioning by its own will upon the canvas of its own self, without differentiation, manifests the universe as nothing but the material of its own awareness. The very manifestation of the universe is the creative agency of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Thus <s>parāmarśa</s> (reflective awareness) itself is the primary nature that distinguishes the light [of consciousness] from the inert light of a mirror. This very thing has been stated by the author of the text in the <s>Vivṛtivimarśinī</s>:

body.translated_text: Just as in the clear interior of a mirror, everything — cities, villages, towns, ramparts, towers, plains, rivers, streams, fires, trees, mountains, animals, birds, women, men, and the like — appears in the form of reflections,

children.translated_text: 'Within the Self, the entire universe shines forth, just as a variegated painting [appears] within a mirror.',

children.text: bodhaḥ punarnijavimarśanasārayuktyā viśvaṃ parāmṛśati no makurastathā tu //
children.translated_text: 'But consciousness, by the power of its own reflective self-awareness (<s>vimarśana</s>), reflectively apprehends the universe — a mirror, however, does not do so.'

body.text: iti / itthaṃ parameśvarāpekṣayā svāṅganirmite bhāvarāśau na kācidbhedabhrāntirmāyāpramātrapekṣayā tu yo 'yaṃ bhedāvabhāsa eṣā pūrṇatvākhyātirūpā bhrāntiḥ pūrṇasyādvayātmano rūpasyākhyānamaprathā pūrṇaṃ na bhāsate kintvapūrṇaṃ dvayarūpaṃ bhāsate bheda eva pratīyata iti yāvat / tasmānniravadyo 'yaṃ pratibimbavādaḥ // 13 //
body.translated_text: Thus, from the perspective of the Supreme Lord, in the mass of objects created as His own limbs, there is no erroneous differentiation. But from the perspective of the <s>māyā</s>-subject, this appearance of differentiation is an error of the nature of non-manifestation of fullness (<s>pūrṇatvākhyāti</s>) — meaning the non-manifestation, the non-appearance, of the full, non-dual nature. The full [reality] does not appear; rather, what appears is incomplete, dual in form — only differentiation is apprehended. Therefore this reflection doctrine is faultless. // 13 //

body.text: itthaṃ paratattvasvarūpanirūpaṇapūrvaṃ prakāśābhedena jagataḥ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvātmakasya sthitiṃ vidhāya punarapyetasya samutpattikrameṇa pratitattvaṃ svarūpaṃ kārikābhiḥ pratipādayati
body.translated_text: Having thus established the nature of the Supreme Principle and the existence of the universe — consisting of thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles) — as non-different from the light, he now sets forth the nature of each <s>tattva</s> in the order of emanation through the following verses:

children.translated_text: He manifests, in differentiated form, the realm of five powers as the state of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Vidyā</s>. // 14 //
[Commentary:]

body.text: yo 'yaṃ paramaśivaḥ paratattvanirūpaṇayā samanantarapratipāditasvarūpaḥ svasvarūparūpā yāḥ śaktayaścinnirvṛtīcchājñānakriyākhyāḥ pañcānantaśaktivrātahetubhūtāstāsāmeva

children.translated_text: five powers,
in differentiated form, through exclusion from what they are not, this
state of <s>tattvas</s>,
delimited to the number five,
he manifests —
he makes evident through their distinctive characteristics — this is the meaning. What is the nature of this [state]? He says:
<s>Śiva</s>

children.text: ityādi / śivaśca śaktiśca sadāśivaśca teṣāṃ bhāvo yasyāḥ sā tathoktā tāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. '<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s>' — that which has these as its nature is so described; and
<s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Vidyā</s> —

children.text: prakṛtiryasyāṃ sā tatheti / atra pratitattvaṃ svarūpaṃ pradarśyate / tathā hi sarvapramātṝṇāmantaḥ pūrṇāhantācamatkāramayaṃ sarvatattvottīrṇaṃ mahāprakāśavapuryaccaitanyametadeva śivatattvam / atra tattvanirūpaṇamupadeśyajanāpekṣayeti / tasyaiva bhagavataścidrūpasyānandarūpā viśvaṃ bhavāmīti parāmṛśato viśvabhāvasvabhāvamayī saṃvideva kiñciducchūnatārūpā sarvabhāvānāṃ bījabhūmiriyaṃ śaktyavasthā / eṣaiva viśvagatasṛṣṭisaṃhāropacārātkṛśapūrṇobhayarūpāpyekaiva sarvarahasyanayeṣu gīyate / punarapyatraiva viśvasamutpattibījabhūmau mahāśūnyātiśūnyākhyāyāṃ maheśasyāhamidamityabhedena pūrṇāhantāmayo yaścamatkāro jñānaprādhānyātkriyābhāgasyāhantāviśrānteḥ seyaṃ sadāśivadaśā / atra mantramaheśvarāḥ pramātārastiṣṭhanti / tathātraivāhamidamityabhedenāhantedantayoḥ samadhṛtatulāpuṭanyāyena yaḥ svātmacamatkāraḥ saiṣā tasyeśvarāvasthā / atrāpi mantreśvarāḥ pramātāraḥ / atrāpīdantāprādhānyenāhantāguṇīkāreṇa yo 'hamahamidamidamityevaṃrūpaścamatkāraḥ sadyojātabālasyeva śiro 'ṅgulīnirdeśya etadeva bodhasāratvādbhagavataḥ śuddhavidyātattvam / atra vidyeśvaraiḥ saha saptakoṭyastu mantrāṇāṃ vācakatayānugrahasvabhāvātpaśūnuddhartuṃ vācyānmantramaheśvaramantreśvarānpratyavatiṣṭhante / atra vidyātattve vidyeśvarapramātṝṇāṃ bodharūpatvāviśeṣe 'pi yā bhedaprathā sā māyāśaktikṛtaivetyāgameṣu gīyate
children.translated_text: that of which these are the basis is so described. Here the nature of each <s>tattva</s> is shown. That is to say: within all subjects (<s>pramātṛs</s>), that great light which is the innermost full I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhantā</s>), replete with self-awareness (<s>camatkāra</s>), transcending all <s>tattvas</s>, this consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) — this itself is the <s>Śiva-tattva</s>. The exposition of <s>tattvas</s> here is from the standpoint of the student to be instructed. The bliss-nature of that very <s>Bhagavān</s>, whose essence is consciousness — the awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) which, while reflectively apprehending 'I shall become the universe,' is of the nature of all states of being, slightly more expanded — this state, the seed-ground of all existents, is the <s>Śakti</s> stage. This very [state], by the figurative usage of emission and absorption occurring throughout the universe, is sung of in all the secret doctrines as one alone, though of the threefold appearance of contracted, full, and both. Furthermore, in this very seed-ground of universal emanation, called the great void and the supra-void — that self-awareness (<s>camatkāra</s>) of the Great Lord, consisting of the full I-consciousness as 'I am this' in non-differentiation — since knowledge predominates and the action-aspect rests in the I-consciousness — this is the <s>Sadāśiva</s> stage. Here the <s>Mantramaheśvaras</s> abide as subjects. Likewise, here again, the self-awareness that arises as 'I am this' in non-differentiation, with I-ness and this-ness held in equal balance like the pans of a scale — this is His <s>Īśvara</s> stage. Here too the <s>Mantreśvaras</s> are the subjects. And here again, with this-ness predominating and I-ness becoming subordinate, that self-awareness of the form 'I... I... this... this...' — like a newborn child pointing to its head and fingers — since this is the essence of consciousness, this is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>Śuddhavidyā-tattva</s> (Pure Knowledge principle). Here, together with the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>, the seven crores of <s>Mantras</s>, being of the nature of grace through their capacity as signifiers, stand in relation to their signified <s>Mantramaheśvaras</s> and <s>Mantreśvaras</s>, in order to uplift the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>). Here in the <s>Vidyā-tattva</s>, although there is no difference in the consciousness-nature of the <s>Vidyeśvara</s> subjects, the manifestation of differentiation that exists is declared in the <s>Āgamas</s> to be produced by the <s>Māyā</s>-power:

body.translated_text: This Supreme <s>Śiva</s>, whose nature has just been set forth through the exposition of the Supreme Principle — His own powers, which are of His own essential nature, designated as <s>Cit</s> (consciousness), <s>Ānanda</s> (bliss), <s>Icchā</s> (will), <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), and <s>Kriyā</s> (action), which are the causes of infinite hosts of powers — of these very

body.text:
māyopari mahāmāyā ... /
iti / yena tatrasthā mantrā mahāmāyānupraveśādaṇava ityucyante / māyātattvopari śuddhavidyādhaśca vijñānākalāḥ pramātāra āṇavamalabhājanam / evamekamevedaṃ śivasvarūpaṃ turyātītamapi turyarūpatayā tattvapañcakatayā gīyate / tasmādeka evaiṣa svatantraḥ kartā prakāśate yasyāhamidamiti sadāśiveśvarabhūmau yaḥ prakāśa etadeva śuddhavedanarūpaṃ karaṇaṃ vakṣyamāṇo māyātattvādidharāntastattvasargaśca kāryamityeva kartṛkaraṇakriyārūpa eka eva svātmamaheśvarākhyaḥ paramapramātā vijṛmbhate // 14 //
body.translated_text: 'Above <s>Māyā</s> is <s>Mahāmāyā</s>...' Thus the <s>Mantras</s> dwelling there, due to the entrance of <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, are called <s>aṇavas</s> (atomic). Above the <s>Māyā-tattva</s> and below <s>Śuddhavidyā</s>, the <s>Vijñānākalas</s> are the subjects, possessing the <s>āṇava-mala</s> (impurity of finitude). Thus this one <s>Śiva</s>-nature, though beyond the fourth state (<s>turyātīta</s>), is described as the fourth state (<s>turya</s>) in the form of five <s>tattvas</s>. Therefore this one independent agent alone shines forth — the light that appears as 'I am this' at the <s>Sadāśiva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> levels, this very [light] in its nature as pure experience is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), and the forthcoming creation of <s>tattvas</s> from <s>Māyā</s> down to earth is the effect — thus, as agent, instrument, and action, the one Supreme Subject called the Lord of his own Self unfolds. // 14 //
He states the nature of the <s>Māyā-tattva</s>:

children.translated_text: The supreme absolute freedom of the Great Lord, which accomplishes the impossible —
this is the divine <s>Māyā-śakti</s>, the self-concealment of <s>Śiva</s>. // 15 //
The supreme
— not dependent on anything else —
that which is
the Supreme Lord's
absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>),
His capacity to create the universe — this itself is
the power called <s>Māyā</s>,

children.text: tasya śaktimataḥ / mīyate paricchidyate dharāntaḥ pramātṛprameyaprapañco yayā sā māyā viśvamohakatayā vā māyā / eṣā devasya krīḍāśīlasya saṃbandhinīti kṛtvā
children.translated_text: belonging to Him who possesses power. That by which the entire expanse of subjects and objects, extending down to earth, is measured and delimited — that is <s>Māyā</s>; or, as that which deludes the universe, it is <s>Māyā</s>. Since she belongs to the Lord (<s>Deva</s>) who delights in play, she is called
<s>Devī</s> (the Goddess),

children.text: na punarbrahmavādināmiva vyatiriktā kācinmāyopapadyata iti / kīdṛśaṃ tatsvātantryam
children.translated_text: and is not, as for the Brahmanists, some separate, extraneous <s>Māyā</s> that could be posited. What is the nature of that freedom?
It accomplishes the impossible (<s>durghaṭasaṃpādana</s>),
that is — that which is difficult to accomplish, meaning
the difficult-to-accomplish
effect, in the form of subjects and objects —
its accomplishment,
the bringing about and the means of bringing about. This very <s>Māyā</s>, for [<s>Śiva</s>] who has by his own will assumed the state of a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), is
