the self-concealment of <s>Śiva</s>,
the triad of impurities (<s>malas</s>) known as <s>āṇava</s> and others, which constitute the concealment of one's own nature. // 15 //

body.text: vakṣyamāṇe ca prādhānike sukhādirūpe bhinne bhogye yadbhoktṛrūpaṃ puṃstattvaṃ tatsvarūpamāha
body.translated_text: He states the nature of <s>Puṃs-tattva</s> (the Puruṣa principle), which is the enjoyer-form corresponding to the forthcoming differentiated enjoyable reality (<s>bhogya</s>) having the form of pleasure and the like, whose basis is <s>Prakṛti</s>:

children.translated_text: Due to being seized by <s>Māyā</s>, consciousness becomes impure — it becomes a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>); // bound by <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Kalā</s>, and <s>Niyati</s>, and by <s>Rāga</s> and <s>Avidyā</s>. // 16 //
[Commentary:]
<s>Māyā</s> —
due to the dependence of being seized [by her], though [the soul] by nature possesses omniscience and omnipotence,
consciousness (<s>bodha</s>),

children.text: sarvajñatvādiguṇāpahastanenākhyātirūpamāṇavaṃ malamāpanno yena ghaṭākāśavatpūrṇasvarūpāccidākāśādavacchedya parimitīkṛtaḥ saṃstadeva puṃstattvamucyate / ato māyāyāḥ pālyaḥ pāśyaśceti
children.translated_text: through the removal of qualities such as omniscience — having acquired the <s>āṇava-mala</s> (impurity of finitude), which is in the nature of non-manifestation — by which, like the space within a pot [cut off] from the full essential nature of the space of consciousness, [consciousness] is delimited and made finite — that very [delimited consciousness] is called the <s>Puṃs-tattva</s>. Therefore, being protected and bound by <s>Māyā</s>, it is
a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>),
a vessel for the bonds (<s>pāśas</s>) whose nature is the threefold impurity — <s>āṇava</s>, <s>māyīya</s>, and <s>kārmika</s>. And furthermore,
<s>Kāla</s> (Time) and <s>Kalā</s> (Limited Agency),
whose natures will be described, together with
<s>Kāla</s> and the rest,
interwoven through and through, thoroughly
bound,
tightly fastened — thus the <s>Puṃs-tattva</s> is enveloped by the group of six <s>tattvas</s>. // 16 //

body.translated_text: He states the nature of the <s>tattvas</s> from <s>Kāla</s> onward in the order of their enveloping [of the soul]:

children.translated_text: 'Only now,' 'only this,' 'only this much,' 'I know entirely' — // the six-fold sheath (<s>kañcukaṣaṭka</s>), together with <s>Māyā</s>, is said to be the innermost [covering] of the atomic [soul]. // 17 //

Thus, although consciousness is independent, having been reduced to atomic status by its own <s>Māyā</s>, even so its powers of knowledge and action become contracted — for this bound soul these are called <s>Vidyā</s> (limited knowledge) and <s>Kalā</s> (limited agency). Just as when a king has confiscated one's entire property, a small amount of wealth is given out of compassion for survival, even so for consciousness that has been reduced to atomic status, whose omniscience and other [qualities] have been taken away, a small measure of agency is reinforced as the purpose of limited knowledge. And since knowledge predominates, the connection of <s>Kāla</s> and the rest with 'knows' has been shown.

body.text: itthaṃ svatantro 'pi bodhaḥ svamāyayā yathāṇutvaṃ prāptastathaiva tadīye jñānakriyāśaktī saṃkucite asya paśurūpasya vidyākale ityucyete / yathā rājñāpahṛtasarvasvasyānukampayā jīvanārthaṃ kiñciddhanaṃ stokaṃ dīyate tathaivāṇutvamāpannasya bodhasyāpahṛtasarvajñatvādeḥ kiñcitkartṛtāparamārthaṃ jñatvamupodbalyata iti jñatvasyaiva prādhānyātkālādīnāṃ jānātinānvayo darśitaḥ /

children.translated_text: This six-fold sheath (<s>kañcukaṣaṭka</s>),
together with <s>Māyā</s> of the nature described,
of the atomic [soul] (<s>aṇu</s>),
of the <s>Puruṣa</s> whose omniscience and other [qualities] have been removed by the <s>āṇava-mala</s> — concealing his own nature, like tarnish on gold —
the innermost,
that which is one's own, is declared. Of what nature is it? He says:
'Only now' (<s>adhunā</s>)
and so forth.
'Only now I know' —

children.text: iti so 'ṇurvartamānatayedaṃ prāṅmayā jñātaṃ jānāmi jñāsyāmītyevamapi kṛtaṃ karomi kariṣye veti jñānakriyāsvarūpeṇa bhāvānapi tathā kalayannavacchinatti cetyeṣo 'sya kālaḥ / tathā
children.translated_text: thus that atomic [soul] says, in the present tense, 'This was known by me before,' 'I know,' 'I shall know' — and also 'I have done,' 'I do,' 'I shall do' — he delimits objects too in the form of knowledge and action; and this is his <s>Kāla</s> (Time [tattva]). Likewise,
'only this much' (<s>kiñcideva</s>) —

children.text: ityavacchinnameva karoti sarvaṃ kartuṃ nālaṃ ghaṭamātrakaraṇāya prabhavati na paṭādāvityetadasyāṇoḥ kalātattvam /
children.translated_text: he acts upon only a delimited [object]; he is not able to do everything — he is capable of making only a pot, not a cloth and so on — this is the <s>Kalā-tattva</s> (Limited Agency) of this atomic [soul].
'only this' (<s>idameva</s>) —

children.text: iti niyatātkāranānniyataṃ kāryaṃ yadarthayate yathā vahnereva dhūmo 'śvamedhādikarmaṇa eva svargādiphalaṃ na sarvasmādityevaṃ niyamena svasaṃkalpakṛtakarmaprabandhasamutthapuṇyāpuṇyairātmā niyamyate yena tadasya niyatitattvam / tathā
children.translated_text: from a fixed cause, a fixed effect is what one seeks — as smoke comes only from fire, as the fruit of heaven comes only from the <s>Aśvamedha</s> and such rituals, not from everything — thus by the rule of determinacy, the self is constrained by the merit and demerit arising from the series of actions created by one's own volition; that is his <s>Niyati-tattva</s> (Determinacy). Likewise,
'entirely' (<s>sarvātmanā</s>) —

children.text: iti yeyamapūrṇammanyatā sarvaṃ mamedamupayujyate bhūyāsaṃ mā kadācinna bhūvamityetatpaśo rāgatattvam / buddhidharmo yo rāgaḥ sa ekatra kutrāpi kāntālakṣaṇe 'rthe 'nyadapohyātra me rāga ityabhiṣvaṅgamātraṃ na sarvākāṅkṣāmayasya rāgatattvasya samānaḥ / tathā
children.translated_text: this sense of incompleteness: 'all this should be useful to me,' 'may I always exist,' 'may I never cease to exist' — this is the <s>Rāga-tattva</s> (Attachment) of the bound soul. The attachment that is a property of <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is directed at one particular beloved object while excluding others — 'my attachment is here alone' — it is merely clinging, and is not equivalent to the <s>Rāga-tattva</s> which consists of the desire for everything. Likewise,
'I know' —

children.text: iti kiñcideva purovarti ghaṭādikaṃ na punardūravyavahitaṃ vastviti vidyātattvam / śuddhavidyāpekṣayā kārikāyāmavidyeti kathitaṃ na punarvedanābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>vidyā</s>-principle means that only something immediately present, such as a pot, [is known], but not a thing that is distant or obstructed. It is called <s>avidyā</s> in the verse in contrast to <s>śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge), not because there is an absence of cognition.
Together with <s>māyā</s>,
this group of six <s>kañcukas</s> (coverings), characterized by the manifestation of duality, belongs to the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). // 17 //

body.translated_text: [Commentary:]
He now explains how this group of six <s>kañcukas</s> is intimately connected with the <s>aṇu</s> (individual soul):

children.translated_text: Like a husk enveloping a grain of rice, though separate it appears as non-separate;
but that [husk] attains purification through the orientation toward the path of <s>Śiva</s> by means of <s>yoga</s>. // 18 //
though the husk is separate,
just as
it is non-separately enveloping the grain of rice —

children.text: ityabhedena taṇḍulāntaścotaṃ bhāsate nipuṇairapi yatnataḥ prakṣipyamāṇaṃ taṇḍulasyāntaraṅgatvānna pṛthagavatiṣṭhate tathaitanmāyādikañcukamaṇostaṇḍulasthānīyasyāntaraṅgatvātkambukasthānīyaṃ vyatiriktamapyavyatiriktatayā pūrṇasaṃvitsvarūpamācchādya sthitamiti śeṣaḥ / evamapi durnivāraṃ kathaṃ tadvilīyata ityāha
children.translated_text: thus it appears as non-different, embedded within the rice grain; even when carefully cast aside by the skilled, it does not stand apart due to its intimate connection with the grain. In the same way, this covering of <s>māyā</s> and the rest, occupying the place of the husk, though distinct from the <s>aṇu</s> who occupies the place of the grain, remains as if non-distinct, concealing the true nature of full <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness) — this is the remainder [of the meaning]. Even so, since it is so difficult to remove, how is it dissolved? He says:
It attains —
and so on.
The particle 'tu' (but)
[indicates] a distinction: there is no other means for this.
Of <s>Śiva</s>,
that is, of one's own self, <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), that which is
the path —

children.text: paramādvayacidānandaikaghano 'smi mamaivedaṃ viśvaṃ svaśaktivijṛmbhaṇamātramiti yā svātmasvarūpavibhūtipratyavamarśarūpā saraṇiḥ
children.translated_text: the way whose nature is the reflective awareness of one's own essential glory, [thinking]: 'I am nothing but the supreme non-dual consciousness-bliss; this entire universe is mine alone, a mere efflorescence of my own power' —
orientation toward that,
steadfast absorption in contemplating that with firmness — that itself is
<s>yoga</s> —
the connection of the <s>aṇu</s> (individual soul) with its own self as its own essential nature, in its complete form. By that,
that —
the covering of the aforementioned nature, thoroughly
attains purification —

children.text: svayameva niḥśeṣeṇa vilayaṃ sevate / etaduktaṃ syādyadā parameśvaraśaktipātaviśuddhahṛdayaḥ paśurbhavati tadāhameva maheśvara iti svātmajñānāvirbhāvātsvayameva paśutvāpādakaṃ kañcukāvaraṇaṃ vilīyate na punaratra svātmajñānaṃ vihāya māyīyaṃ kiñcinniyatiśaktisamutthaṃ karma pragalbhata iti // 18 //
children.translated_text: of its own accord it undergoes complete dissolution. What has been said amounts to this: when the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) becomes one whose heart has been purified by the descent of the power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), then, through the arising of self-knowledge — 'I myself am <s>Maheśvara</s>' — the covering of <s>kañcukas</s> that had brought about the state of bondage dissolves of its own accord. It is not the case that, setting aside self-knowledge, some <s>māyīya</s> (illusory) action arising from the power of <s>niyati</s> (limitation) becomes efficacious here. // 18 //

body.translated_text: In actual reality,

Since such an <s>aṇu</s> (individual soul), being an experiencer, must have objects of experience, he now sets forth the creation of principles (<s>tattvas</s>) pertaining to <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature):

children.translated_text: Pleasure, pain, and delusion alone, and ascertainment, volition, and self-attribution —
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), and then the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>): <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>manas</s> (mind), and <s>ahaṅkṛti</s> (ego-sense), in succession. // 19 //
of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion —

children.text: sāmānyaṃ rūpamaṅgāṅgibhāvo yatra nopalabhyate sā mūlakāraṇam
children.translated_text: whose general form is such that the relation of principal and subordinate parts is not apprehended therein — that is the root cause,
<s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).
After <s>prakṛti</s>, he states the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) which is an effect:
Ascertainment —
and so on.
Ascertainment (<s>niścaya</s>)
[means] 'this is of such a nature' —
volition (<s>saṃkalpana</s>)
[means] deliberation (<s>manana</s>),
self-attribution (<s>abhimāna</s>)
[means] 'mine' — in this order:
<s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>manas</s> (mind), and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) —
the triad of this nature
[constitutes] the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>).

children.text: aṅgāṅgibhāvena guṇānāṃ kāryaṃ bhūtendriyādyapekṣayā ca kāraṇamiti // 19 //
children.translated_text: As an effect of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) in the relation of principal and subordinate, and as a cause in relation to the gross elements, sense organs, and the rest. // 19 //

body.translated_text: Of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, that which is
He states the outer instruments:

children.text: śrotraṃ tvagakṣi rasanā ghrāṇaṃ buddhīndriyāṇi śabdādau /
children.translated_text: Hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell are the organs of knowledge (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>), [operating] in the domain of sound and the rest;
speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are the organs of action (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>). // 20 //
sound and the rest —
the five sense organs predominating in knowledge, [operating] in [their respective] objects,
[are] hearing and the rest (<s>śrotrādi</s>),
and five organs predominating in action
[are] speech and the rest (<s>vāgādi</s>).

children.text: / vacanādānaviharaṇavisargānandātmakāḥ karmendriyāṇāṃ viṣayāḥ / ityubhayathā ca śṛṇomi kathayāmītyahaṅkārānugamādahaṅkārakāryāṇi // 20 //
children.translated_text: The objects of the organs of action are: speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure. And in both cases, since [the experience] 'I hear,' 'I speak' is always accompanied by the ego-sense, [these organs] are effects of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego). // 20 //

body.translated_text: In the forthcoming [discussion of]
He describes the nature of their objects, beginning with sound:

children.text: eṣāṃ grāhyo viṣayaḥ sūkṣmaḥ pravibhāgavarjito yaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: That object of theirs which is to be grasped, which is subtle and devoid of differentiation —

children.text: tanmātrapañcakaṃ tacchabdaḥ sparśo maho raso gandhaḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: that is the fivefold group of <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements): sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. // 21 //
that which is of these —
of the sense organs —
the object,
the range [of operation],
would be —
of what kind is it?
Devoid of differentiation —
that is, excluded from particularity, of a general nature,
subtle —
whatever object that may be,
that itself is sound and the rest
in their general form —
[called] <s>tanmātra</s> (subtle element).
The generality of sound is the sound-<s>tanmātra</s>; similarly the others. Because object and subject are mutually dependent, this too, like the sense organs,
the fivefold group of <s>tanmātras</s>,
is indeed a product of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego). // 21 //

body.translated_text: To be accepted as that which is to be known and acted upon,
He states that through the mutual intermixture of the objects, the gross elements such as earth are the effect:

children.translated_text: Through the combination of these [tanmātras], the gross object attains the state of the five elements (<s>bhūtapañcaka</s>) —

children.text: abhyeti nabhaḥ pavanastejaḥ salilaṃ ca pṛthvī ca // 22 //
children.translated_text: space (<s>nabhas</s>), wind (<s>pavana</s>), fire (<s>tejas</s>), water (<s>salila</s>), and earth (<s>pṛthvī</s>). // 22 //
Through the combination of these —
the particular [gross object] arising from the capacity of mutual friction [among the tanmātras] —
the gross object,

children.text: sa eva bhūtarūpatāṃ yāti / tathā hi śabdatanmātrācchabdaviśeṣo nabho jāyate śabdasparśābhyāṃ pavano rūpasaṃyuktābhyāmetābhyāṃ tejaścaibhyo rasayuktebhyaścāpo gandhasaṃyuktebhyaśca pṛthvīti pañca mahābhūtāni kāryaṃ kāraṇānuguṇam iti kṛtvaikottaraguṇānīti / evameṣā prakṛtiḥ kāryakāraṇātmā puruṣasya parameśvarasyecchayā bhogyatayā pravṛtteti ṣaṭtriṃśattattvātmakaṃ jagadvibhajya pratitattvaṃ nirūpitam // 22 //
children.translated_text: that itself assumes the form of [gross] elements. Thus: from the sound-<s>tanmātra</s> arises space (<s>nabhas</s>), characterized by the particular quality of sound; from sound and touch arises wind (<s>pavana</s>); from these two conjoined with form arises fire (<s>tejas</s>); from these conjoined with taste arises water (<s>āpas</s>); and from these conjoined with smell arises earth (<s>pṛthvī</s>) — thus the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) are effects conforming to their causes, each having one more quality than the preceding. Thus this <s>prakṛti</s>, consisting of cause and effect, has been set in operation as the object of experience for the <s>puruṣa</s> (soul) by the will of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), and the world consisting of thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles) has been analyzed and explained principle by principle. // 22 //

body.translated_text: He states the covering nature of <s>prakṛti</s> with respect to the <s>puruṣa</s>, as in the case of the coverings of <s>māyā</s> and the <s>kañcukas</s>:

children.translated_text: Like a husk covering a grain of rice, the creation beginning with <s>prakṛti</s> envelops
this [creation] extending down to earth, [envelops] consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) in the form of a body. // 23 //
This too —
the creation pertaining to <s>prakṛti</s> (<s>prādhānika</s>),
the creation,
extending down to earth,
the grain of rice —
just as
the husk,
the outer covering of grain,
covers —
conceals, so too consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), which is already enveloped by the covering of <s>māyā</s> and the <s>kañcukas</s> — which occupy the place of the inner husk (<s>kambuka</s>) —
consciousness,
is once again, by that which occupies the place of the outer husk (<s>tuṣa</s>),
in the form of a body,

children.text: etatsamāvṛṇute tatpratiprākāratayā sthagayati / atreme pramātāraḥ kalābhirindriyamātrābhirviśeṣāntābhirdehasvabhāvāḥ sakalā ityucyante viśeṣavarjitā videhāḥ pralayākalā iti ca / evaṃ śivādisakalāntapramātṛsaptakasanāthaṃ rudrakṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitaṃ jagaditi // 23 //
children.translated_text: enveloped by this [prākṛtic creation], which conceals it as a wall set before it. Hence these knowers (<s>pramātṛs</s>) — endowed with <s>kalās</s> (powers of limited action), sense organs, [and tattvas] down to the <s>viśeṣas</s> (particularities), whose nature is that of a body — are called <s>sakalas</s> (those possessing all parts). Those devoid of <s>viśeṣas</s> are [called] <s>videhas</s> (bodiless) and <s>pralayākalas</s> (devoid of parts at dissolution). Thus the world, presided over by <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (the field-knower), is furnished with the seven [types of] knowers from <s>Śiva</s> down to <s>sakala</s>. // 23 //

body.translated_text: He states the nature of the three coverings as supreme, subtle, and gross:

children.text: paramāvaraṇaṃ mala iha sūkṣmaṃ māyādikañcukaṃ sthūlam /
children.translated_text: The supreme covering is <s>mala</s> (impurity); here the subtle [covering] is the group of <s>kañcukas</s> beginning with <s>māyā</s>; the gross [covering]
is the external one in the form of the body. The <s>ātman</s> (Self) is indeed enveloped by these three sheaths (<s>kośatraya</s>). // 24 //
<s>mala</s> (impurity),
the innermost [covering], like tarnish on gold,
supreme —
[means] most intimate,
a covering,
a concealment — because it abides in identity [with the Self].
Beginning with <s>māyā</s>,
the group of six <s>kañcukas</s> ending with <s>vidyā</s>,
[is] subtle —

children.text: ātmana āvaraṇaṃ taṇḍulasya kambukamivāvaraṇaṃ pṛṣṭhapātitvenāste yena bhedamayī jñatvakartṛtvādiprathā prathata ityeṣa māyīyo malaḥ / etadapekṣayā
children.translated_text: a covering of the <s>ātman</s>, like the husk (<s>kambuka</s>) covering rice, which remains as something cast upon the surface, by means of which the manifestation of differentiated knowership, agentship, and the like expands — this is the <s>māyīya</s> (pertaining to <s>māyā</s>) <s>mala</s> (impurity). In comparison to this,
the external [covering],
occupying the place of the outer husk (<s>tuṣa</s>), the covering pertaining to <s>prakṛti</s>, characterized by the existence of a body,
[is] gross,

children.text: tvaṅmāṃsādirūpatvādeṣa tṛtīyaḥ kārmo malo yena pramātā śubhāśubhakarmasaṃcayabhājanaṃ bhavati / evamanena parasūkṣmasthūlarūpeṇa
children.translated_text: because it consists of skin, flesh, and the like. This is the third <s>mala</s>, the <s>kārma</s> (pertaining to <s>karma</s>), by which the knower (<s>pramātā</s>) becomes a receptacle for the accumulation of meritorious and unmeritorious actions. Thus, by means of this threefold [covering] — supreme, subtle, and gross —
enveloped by the three sheaths (<s>kośatraya</s>),
though inherently expansive, [the Self is] contracted like the space within a pot,
the <s>ātman</s> (Self)
is called an <s>aṇu</s> (atomic soul) or a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). // 24 //

body.translated_text: The <s>āṇava</s> [mala] of consciousness is precisely the non-recognition of one's own essential nature — the ignorance regarding one's true being —
He says that due to this connection [with the three sheaths], the Self appears as if afflicted:

children.translated_text: Though the Self's own nature is one, due to the conjunction with the darkness of ignorance,
one apprehends it with the variegation of manifold [distinctions of] object (<s>grāhya</s>) and subject (<s>grāhaka</s>). // 25 //
though one,
though of a non-dual nature,
one's own —
innate, not obtained from another,
the nature of the Self,

children.text: caitanyamātmasattālakṣaṇaṃ svarūpaṃ pramātṛpramāṇaprameyanānāracanāprapañcena jānātyabhedaviparītena bhedenābhimanyata iti yāvat / yathā rekhātimiropahataḥ puruṣa ekamapi candraṃ paśyandvau candrāvimau nabhasi sta iti paricchindamṝÉllokamapi darśayati dvau candrāvimau paśyeti / vastuvṛttenaika evāsau candra iti timiravaśāttathā bhāsate yenodvegalakṣaṇāmānandalakṣaṇāṃ vārthakriyāṃ sa taimirikaḥ prāpnoti / tathaivājñānatimiraprāptabhedaprathaḥ sarvaṃ svātmano 'bhinnamapi bhedena vyavaharanbhinnaṃ karmaphalamarthayate yena bhūyobhūyaḥ svarganirayādibhogabhāgbhavati / ataścājñānasya timireṇa rūpaṇā viparītābhāsanāt // 25 //
children.translated_text: the essential nature characterized by the being of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) — [one] knows it through the manifold elaboration of the distinctions of knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>); that is to say, one falsely identifies it through differentiation, which is the opposite of non-duality. Just as a person afflicted by the eye-disease of double vision (<s>timira</s>), seeing even a single moon, determines 'there are two moons in the sky' and makes others see [the same], [saying] 'look, these two moons' — in actual reality it is one and the same moon, but due to the eye-disease it appears thus, whereby the afflicted person experiences an activity characterized by either distress or [false] delight. In the same way, one whose manifestation of duality has been acquired through the eye-disease of ignorance, treating everything as different though it is non-different from one's own Self, pursues the differentiated fruits of action, whereby one becomes again and again a partaker of the experiences of heaven, hell, and the like. Therefore, the metaphor of ignorance as an eye-disease is apt, since it causes an inverted appearance. // 25 //

body.translated_text: This <s>ātman</s>, bound by the three sheaths, due to the connection with the darkness of self-non-recognition —
He illustrates the non-duality of the Self by means of an analogy:

children.translated_text: Just as juice, treacle, raw sugar, molasses, refined sugar, and the rest are nothing but sugarcane juice,
so too all the different states are [modifications] of the Supreme Self, <s>Śaṃbhu</s> (the Auspicious One). // 26 //
Juice and the rest —
the varieties of sugarcane [products] —
just as
one
single sugarcane juice
[is the reality] in all [these products], since sweetness pervades them all, in the very same way waking and the other [states] —
the different states —
which have the form of the manifold display of object (<s>grāhya</s>) and subject (<s>grāhaka</s>) —
all —
the particular [modifications],
of the Supreme Self —
whose nature is one's own essential being,
of <s>Śaṃbhu</s> —

children.text: caitanyamaheśvarasyaiva / yataḥ sa eva bhagavānsarvasya svātmabhūtaḥ svasvātantryāttāṃ tāmapi bhūmikāṃ samāpannastathā grāhyagrāhakādyavasthāviśiṣṭaḥ prathate yathekṣuraso na punaḥ svātmanastasmādbhinnaṃ kiñcidastīti sa eka eva sarvāvasthāsu saṃvidanugamāt / itthaṃ sarvatraikarūpatādarśanātpramātā sarvadṛśvā bhavati / yathāha śrīśaṃbhubhaṭṭārakaḥ
children.translated_text: belong to the Great Lord of consciousness (<s>caitanya-Maheśvara</s>) alone. For that <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed Lord), who is the very Self of all, having by His own absolute freedom assumed each and every level [of manifestation], manifests as qualified by the various states of object, subject, and the rest — like sugarcane juice. Nothing whatsoever exists as different from Him, from His own Self; He alone is one in all states, because consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>) pervades [them all]. Thus, by seeing the unity of form everywhere, the knower (<s>pramātā</s>) becomes the seer of all. As the revered <s>Śaṃbhu-bhaṭṭāraka</s> has said:

children.text: eko bhāvaḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvaḥ sarve bhāvā ekabhāvasvabhāvāḥ /
children.translated_text: One reality is the nature of all realities; all realities are of the nature of one reality.

children.text: eko bhāvastattvato yena dṛṣṭaḥ sarve bhāvāstattvatastena dṛṣṭāḥ //
children.translated_text: One who has truly seen that one reality has truly seen all realities.

body.translated_text: And in the <s>Bhagavadgītā</s> as well:

children.translated_text: That knowledge by which one sees in all beings a single, imperishable reality,
undivided among the divided — know that knowledge to be <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of <s>sattva</s>).

body.text: tīrthāntaraparikalpitastu bhedaḥ saṃvṛtyarthamabhyupagato 'pi na satyabhūmāvavakalpata ityāha
body.translated_text: But the differentiation postulated by rival schools (<s>tīrthāntara</s>), even though provisionally accepted for the sake of conventional discourse (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), is not established on the plane of ultimate truth — he says:

children.translated_text: <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness), the Inner Controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), <s>virāj</s> (cosmic body), and [entities] ending in body, universal, and individual —
all this is merely conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>); in ultimate reality they do not exist at all. // 27 //
<s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness) —

children.text: iti bodhamātrameva kevalamanupādhi nāmarūparahitamapyanādivāsanāprabodhavaicitryasāmarthyānnīlasukhādirūpaṃ bāhyarūpatayā nānā prakāśata iti vijñānavādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: thus, the <s>Vijñānavādins</s> (proponents of the consciousness-only doctrine) [hold that] consciousness alone, bare, without substratum, devoid of name and form, yet by the power of the variety of the awakening of beginningless impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), manifests in diverse forms such as blue, pleasure, and so forth, as if external.

body.translated_text: 'All this is indeed the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Spirit) alone...'
'There is no multiplicity here whatsoever...'

children.translated_text: the Inner Controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) —

children.text: sarvasyeti paraṃ brahmaivānādyavidyāvaśādbhedena prakāśata iti brahmavādinaḥ / atrobhayatrāpi vedanasya svātantryaṃ jīvitabhūtaṃ viśvanirmāṇaheturiti na cetitam /
children.translated_text: [they hold that] the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone, being the inner controller of all, appears as differentiated due to beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — thus say the <s>Brahmavādins</s> (proponents of <s>Brahman</s>). In both these [schools], however, it has not been recognized that the autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) of consciousness — which is its very life — is the cause of the creation of the universe.

body.translated_text: By this reasoning,

children.translated_text: <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) —

children.text: brahmavādinastu yathāprāṇanameva viśvamāgūrya vartate nahi prāṇanādṛte 'nyatkiñcidbrahmaṇo rūpamiti savimarśaṃ śabdabrahmetyāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>Brahmavādins</s> who [emphasize] <s>prāṇa</s>, however, [maintain] that the universe exists as having been gathered up through the very act of breathing; that there is no other form of <s>Brahman</s> apart from breathing — [this Brahman], they say, is the 'word-<s>Brahman</s>' (<s>śabdabrahman</s>), endowed with reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>).

body.translated_text: Others —

children.translated_text: the <s>virāj</s>-body —
that is, the cosmic (<s>vairāja</s>) [form] of <s>Brahman</s> is also ultimately real. As it is said:

body.translated_text: Yet others have maintained that

children.translated_text: He whose mouth is <s>Agni</s> (fire), whose head is heaven, whose navel is space, whose feet are the earth,
whose eye is the sun, whose ears are the directions — homage to Him, the Soul of the world (<s>lokātman</s>).

body.translated_text: And so on in this manner.

children.translated_text: <s>Jāti</s> (universal) —

children.text: iti mahāsattāsāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ sarvaguṇāśrayaṃ vastu paramārthasaditi vaiśeṣikādayo bruvate /
children.translated_text: thus the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others declare that the entity characterized by the great universal of existence (<s>mahāsattā-sāmānya</s>), the substratum of all qualities, is ultimately real.
<s>piṇḍas</s> (individuals/particulars) —

children.text: iti vyaktaya eva paramārthasatyo nahi sāmānyaṃ nāma kiñcidekamanekaguṇāśrayaṃ prakāśate nāpyupapadyate veti vyaktīnāmeva vyavahāraḥ parisamāptaḥ kiṃ sāmānyeneti nānāvṛttivikalpaiḥ sāmānyaṃ vivadamānā vyaktayo nānuyantyanyadanuyāyi na bhāsata ityevamādi bahu bruvanto jātirna paramārtha iti pratipannā ityeva
children.translated_text: that is, only the particulars (<s>vyaktis</s>) are ultimately real; for no single universal, serving as the substratum of many qualities, is ever perceived nor is it even logically tenable — thus the activity of particulars alone is complete in itself; what need is there of a universal? Those who, by means of various arguments concerning inherence (<s>vṛtti</s>), dispute the universal, [say]: 'particulars do not follow [something else]; what is dependent on another does not manifest' — speaking much in this manner, they maintain that the universal is not ultimately real. Thus —
[these views range] from <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) at the beginning to <s>piṇḍa</s> (the particular) at the end.
Of which distinctions, those are thus described.
This is merely conventional (<s>vyavahāra</s>).

children.text: ityasminsvātantryavāde prakāśamānasya vastuno 'napahnavanīyatvādete bhedāḥ saṃvṛtisatyatvena prakāśante
children.translated_text: In this doctrine of absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), since the reality that manifests cannot be denied, these distinctions appear as having merely conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>),
but in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārtha</s>), they do not exist at all.

children.text: iti na punaḥ satattvatayaite bhedāstīrthāntaraparikalpitabhedā vidyamānā eva / tasmādeka eva paramaprakāśaparamārthaḥ svatantraścaitanyamaheśvara itthamitthaṃ cakāsti yato 'nyasyaitadvyatiriktasyāprakāśarūpasya prakāśamānatābhāvāt / yaduktam
children.translated_text: Thus, it is not the case that these distinctions — the distinctions imagined by other schools (<s>tīrthāntara</s>) — exist as ultimately real. Therefore, the one supreme light, the ultimate reality, the independent (<s>svatantra</s>) consciousness-lord (<s>Caitanya-Maheśvara</s>), shines forth in this and that manner, since nothing other than Him — being of the nature of non-luminosity — can manifest. As it has been said:

body.translated_text: Others [say] —

children.translated_text: Those devoted to the practices of [various] systems, having conjectured reality through their own reasoning, whatever they declare —

children.translated_text: All that is indeed Your reality; there is nothing else. The dispute among the learned is merely about names.

body.translated_text: Thus ends [verse] 27.

children.text: na kenacidvicārayituṃ pāryata iti yāvat / yathā vastuvṛttena rajjuḥ paridṛśyamānā dīrghatvakuṇḍalinīrūpatvabhramātsarpo 'yamityadhyavasātṝṇāṃ rajjudravye 'pyasadarthapratibhāso 'yaṃ sarpādhyavasāyaḥ sadarthapratibhāsādbhayaṃ maraṇāvasāyaṃ vidadhāti / anubhavasiddhamapyetatsthāṇuṃ bhūtamiti matvā svayaṃ bhīṣaṇīyaṃ vākāraṃ samullikhya bhrāntāḥ santo hṛdbhaṅganāśaṃ ke nāma na yātā iti vibhrama evāpūrṇatvaprathane heturiti // 28 //
children.translated_text: cannot be investigated by anyone, this is the meaning. Just as a rope, when actually perceived, due to the error of its elongated and coiled form, is determined as "this is a snake" — in the rope-substance, this appearance of an unreal object, namely the determination of a snake, produces from the appearance of a [seemingly] real object a fear extending up to death. This too is established by experience: having perceived a post as a ghost and having themselves conjured up a terrifying cry, those who are deluded — who indeed has not gone to destruction through heart-failure? Thus error alone is the cause of the manifestation of incompleteness. [End of verse 28]

body.translated_text: He applies this to the matter at hand.

<s>varṇa</s>, <s>āśrama</s>, and so forth — though unreal in the Self, they arise through the force of error. [Verse 29]

children.text: grahaṇāttapaḥpūjavratānīti sarvaṃ kalpanāmātrasāraṃ vibhramavijṛmbhitameva māyāśaktyā dehādyātmatayābhimanyate / etatsarvaṃ bhrānteḥ prabhavati yayānavaratasvarganarakajanmamaraṇaprabandhabhājaḥ paśavo na punaḥ paramārthataḥ svātmano 'navacchinnacidānandaikaghanasya dharmādharmādikaṃ kiñcidvidyata iti // 29 //
children.translated_text: by the word 'and so forth,' austerities, worship, vows, and the like — all this, whose essence is mere mental construction (<s>kalpanā</s>), is nothing but the efflorescence of error. Through the power of <s>Māyā</s>, it is wrongly identified as the Self in the form of body and the like. All this arises from error, by which bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) partake in the unceasing chain of heaven, hell, birth, and death. But in ultimate reality, for the Self — which is an undivided mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>) — there exists no <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, or anything of the sort. [End of verse 29]

body.translated_text: Thus, just as a rope, though ultimately real, when erroneously apprehended as a snake, produces the practical effects associated with a snake — in exactly the same way, in the minds of those who identify the Self with the body,
Having thus examined the power of error in causing the appearance of unreal objects, he now states its origin.

Therefore, the true nature — that 'I alone, whose essence is consciousness (<s>cit</s>), manifest in the form of subject and object' — does not shine forth; only unreal distinction appears. Since the true manifestation does not occur, error is characterized as darkness. [End of verse 30]

body.translated_text: Since manifestation is otherwise inexplicable, in those [entities] that have become embodiments of luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>),
Teaching that the misidentification of the non-Self as Self is preceded by the misidentification of the Self as non-Self, he declares the thoroughly delusory nature of error.

children.translated_text: the apprehension of identity where there is no identity — this is the greatest cruelty. If there were cruelty merely in the misidentification of the Self [with objects in general], let it also apply to blue, pleasure, and other things, or let it not occur anywhere at all. But that in a particular inert [entity] — the body and the like, which are like a clod of earth — there is the anointing with the essence of I-ness as Self, while elsewhere, in blue, pleasure, and such, there is the establishment of non-Self-hood and otherness — this alone is complete <s>saṃsāra</s>, worthy of lamentation, for the torment of dualities (<s>dvandva</s>), brought on by misidentification, drags the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>). As stated in the <s>Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa</s> by the <s>yoginī</s> <s>Madālasā</s>:

body.translated_text: First, in entities that are in truth one consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>), the imposition of inertness filled with difference has been accomplished by the darkness of non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>) — that entities non-different from one's own Self appear as different from it — this itself is like darkness,

Just as [those who think] 'I am thin,' 'I am fat,' 'I am handsome,' 'I am learned' — children, women, the ignorant, and farmers — by their own mental constructions (<s>vikalpa</s>) have thus accepted the body alone as the Self, [while] some who consider themselves discerning [say]:

body.translated_text: Every knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), whose consciousness has been concealed by non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>), by the fetters of mental constructions (<s>vikalpa</s>) arising from himself, though [the Self is] all-pervading,

body.text: dehastāvadihaiva pralīyate kuto 'syātmatvamato yaḥ kṣudhitaḥ pipāsitaḥ so 'hamiti prāṇātmamāninaśca vivecakaṃmanyatarāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'The body dissolves right here [at death] — how can it be the Self?' Therefore those who identify the Self with <s>prāṇa</s>, [thinking] 'I am hungry, I am thirsty, that is me' — they consider themselves even more discerning.

body.text: dehaprāṇau jaḍau loṣṭādivatkuto 'nayorātmabhāvastataḥ sukhyahaṃ duḥkhyahamiti yaḥ sukhaduḥkhādi cetate sa ātmeti puryaṣṭakābhimānino mīmāṃsakādayo 'pi vivecakatamāśca /
body.translated_text: Body and <s>prāṇa</s> are inert like a clod of earth — how can they be the Self? Therefore, 'I am happy, I am suffering' — he who cognizes pleasure, pain, and the like, he is the Self — thus the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> and others who identify with the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) consider themselves the most discerning of all.

body.text: etatsukhaduḥkhādyapi buddhidharmaḥ kathamātmatayā vaktuṃ śakyastato dehaprāṇadhīvikalpānāṃ yatrābhāvaḥ sa ātmeti śūnyābhimāninaḥ / evaṃ yatkiñcididaṃ bhāti tannāhamityaprathārūpaṃ śūnyameva sarvāpohanasvabhāvamātmeti nabhaḥśabdenoktaḥ / tadapi śūnyaṃ yadā samādhānāvasare vedyīkurvata etadapi śūnyaṃ vayaṃ na bhavāmastadā śūnyāntaramātmatvena vidadhānā neti neti brahmavādyabhyupagatatattacchūnyaparityāgena tāṃ tāṃ śūnyātmatāṃ parigṛhṇantīti nabhaḥprapañcaḥ kārikāyāṃ nirūpitaḥ / itthaṃ saṃvitsvarūpāparyavasānācchūnyātmamānino yoginaḥ suṣuptaguhānimagnā jaḍātmāno bhrāntā evātmānaṃ saṃvitsvarūpamapi jāḍyenānubadhnanti /

And thus the <s>Bauddhas</s> [say]:

body.translated_text: But even these pleasures, pains, and so forth are properties of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — how can they be spoken of as the Self? Therefore, where there is an absence of the mental constructions of body, <s>prāṇa</s>, and intellect — that is the Self: thus [think] those who identify with the void (<s>śūnya</s>). In this way, whatever appears — 'that I am not' — the void, whose nature is the negation of everything, of the form of non-manifestation, is the Self: this is indicated by the word 'void' (<s>nabhas</s>). But when that void too, at the time of meditative absorption, is made into an object of knowledge, [they think] 'we are not even this void,' and then, positing yet another void as the Self — those who profess '<s>neti neti</s>' ('not this, not this') as <s>Brahman</s>, by abandoning each successive void, grasp each successive void-selfhood — this is what is meant by 'the expanse of voids' (<s>nabhaḥ-prapañca</s>) in the verse. Thus, since they do not arrive at the essential nature of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>), the yogins who identify with the void, plunged into the cave of deep sleep (<s>suṣupta</s>), their selves being inert, are indeed deluded — they bind the Self, which is of the nature of consciousness, with inertness.

children.translated_text: When there is a real Self, the notion of 'other' arises; from the distinction of self and other arise appropriation and hatred;
Bound to these two, all faults arise.

body.translated_text: Thus they declare. [End of verse 32]

body.text: kathameṣa durnivāro mahāmoho dehādipramātṛtāsamutthaḥ pralīyata iti bhagavatsvātantryamevātra heturityāha
body.translated_text: How does this irremediable great delusion, arising from the identification of the body and the like as the subject, dissolve? The blessed Lord's own absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) alone is the cause — this he states.

children.translated_text: Through the means of manifesting the splendor of one's own knowledge, one unwraps one's own Self;
thus <s>Paramaśiva</s> extends the wondrous play of bondage and liberation. [Verse 33]
"Of one's own" —
of the Self, which is characterized by consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), that which is
"knowledge" —
the realization of one's own absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>); of that,
"splendor" (<s>vibhava</s>) —

children.text: dehādyabhimānavigalanena yaccitsvarūpe parāhantācamatkārarūpasya svasvātantryasya sphītatvaṃ cidānandaikaghanaḥ svatantro 'smīti tasya bodhasvātantryasvarūpasya vibhavasya
children.translated_text: through the dissolution of the misidentification with body and the like, the expansion of one's own sovereignty — which is of the nature of the wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) of supreme I-consciousness (<s>parāhantā</s>) — in the essence of consciousness; 'I am an undivided mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>), I am free' — of that splendor, which is the essential nature of awakening and freedom,
