"the means" (<s>yoga</s>) —
through such a process of cultivation, the firmness of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) that arises in the Self — by this means,
"through the means of manifesting the splendor of one's own knowledge, one's own Self" —
not something obtained from elsewhere, whose nature is consciousness —
"unwraps" —

children.text: dehaprāṇapuryaṣṭakaśūnyaparāmarśanānigaḍairyo veṣṭita āsīttameva caitanyasvarūpaḥ svatantro 'smīti vimarśanena punarapi bhagavānevodveṣṭanaṃ vigataveṣṭanaṃ kuruta iti / evamakhyātibalādāgataṃ svātmano dehādyāvaraṇaṃ tatpunarapi khyātibalādvinaśyatīti svavikalpakalpita iyāndoṣa iti śrīmadgranthakṛtā tantrasāre nirūpitam
children.translated_text: the one who was wrapped by the fetters of identification with body, <s>prāṇa</s>, subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), and void — that very one, being of the nature of consciousness, through the reflective awareness that 'I am free' — once again it is the Blessed Lord Himself who performs the unwrapping, the removal of wrapping. Thus the covering of the Self by body and the like, which came about through the force of non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>), is again destroyed through the force of recognition (<s>khyāti</s>). That this fault of such magnitude is fabricated by one's own mental constructions has been established by the blessed author in the <s>Tantrasāra</s>:

children.text: yo niścayaḥ paśujanasya jaḍo 'smi karmasaṃpāśito 'smi malino 'smi parerito 'smi /
children.translated_text: The conviction of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) — 'I am inert, I am fettered by <s>karma</s>, I am impure, I am impelled by another' —
by the method of obtaining a different, firm conviction, one instantly becomes the Lord, whose body is the universe, whose Self is consciousness.

body.text: iti / kimiti badhnāti muñcati ca bhagavānityāha

children.translated_text: "Thus bondage" —
and so forth.
"Thus" —
by the previously explained method, the Blessed Lord, who is free (<s>svatantra</s>),
<s>Paramaśiva</s> —

children.text: pūrṇacidānandaikaghanalakṣaṇaḥ svarūpagopanasatattvakrīḍāśīlatvādakhyātyavabhāsanapūrvaṃ svātmānameva dehādipramātṛtāpannaṃ vidhāya svarūpaṃ pracchādya ca bandhaṃ vidadhāti tathaiva punaḥ svecchātaḥ svātmajñānaprakāśakrameṇa dehādipramātṛtābandhaṃ nivārya sa eva taṃ svātmānaṃ mocayatītyubhayathā
children.translated_text: whose essential characteristic is undivided fullness of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>), because His nature is to play the game of concealing His own true nature, having first manifested non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>) and having made His own Self assume the condition of a subject identified with body and the like, concealing His true nature, He effects bondage; and then again, of His own will, through the process of illuminating self-knowledge, having removed the bondage of identification with body and the like as subject, He Himself liberates that very Self — thus in both ways
a play variegated with bondage and liberation,
a wonder whose nature is <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation),
a play,
a sport,
he extends,

children.text: vistārayatyekākī na ramāmyahamiti / svabhāva evaiṣa devasya yattāṃ tāmapyavasthāmāpannaḥ svarūparūpaḥ sansarvatrānubhavitṛtayā prathata ityetadeva svātantryam // 33 //
children.translated_text: expands — thinking 'I do not delight in being alone.' This is the very nature of the Lord: that even having assumed this or that condition, while remaining in his own true form, he manifests everywhere as the experiencer of all — this alone is his absolute freedom. (33)

body.translated_text: Thus. Why does the Blessed Lord bind and release? He says:

body.text: na kevalametadyāvadaparaḥ kaścidavasthāviśeṣaḥ svasminrūpe viśrānta evāvabhāsyate bhagavatetyāha
body.translated_text: Not only this, but another particular state also appears as resting in his own nature, in the Blessed One — thus he says:

children.translated_text: "Creation, maintenance, dissolution, waking, dream, and deep sleep — these shine in that"

children.text: bhānti turīye dhāmani tathāpi tairnāvṛtaṃ bhāti // 34 //
children.translated_text: "<s>turīya</s> (fourth) state; and yet it shines unobscured by them. (34)"

body.text: viśvāpekṣayā ye sargādayo māyāpramātṛgatāśca ye jāgradādayo 'vasthāviśeṣāsta ubhayathaitasminbhagavatyānandaghane

children.translated_text: <s>turīya</s> (fourth) state,
the fourth station, which is the fullness of <s>aham</s> (I-consciousness) —
they shine,

children.text: tadviśrāntāḥ santaḥ svarūpasattāṃ kalpitapramātrapekṣayā bāhyatayā labhante / parameśvarabhittau yanna prakāśate tadbāhyatayāpi na prakāśate 'taḥ
children.translated_text: resting in that, they obtain their true existence externally from the perspective of a constructed subject. Whatever does not shine forth on the canvas of the Supreme Lord does not shine forth externally either. Therefore:

body.translated_text: The creation and other cosmic processes with respect to the universe, and the waking and other particular states pertaining to the <s>māyā</s>-level subject — both types shine in this Blessed One, who is a mass of bliss, in the
"The fourth should be poured into the three, like oil."

body.text: iti sarvāsvavasthāsu turīyaṃ rūpamanusyūtatvena sthitamiti paramārthaḥ / etāvatā tatra taiḥ svarūpamācchāditaṃ syānna vetyāha

children.translated_text: "And yet it shines unobscured by them."

children.text: iti / itthamapi taiḥ svarūpasattārthamāvṛtamapi tebhyaḥ samuttīrṇatayā sarvānubhavitṛtayā sarvatrāvabhāsata eva na punastadāvaraṇena pūrṇasvarūpatāṃ tatra tirodhatta iti śivadhāma sarvāvasthāsvapi sadaiva paripūrṇam // 34 //
children.translated_text: Even so, although concealed by them for the purpose of their own existence, yet because it transcends them, as the experiencer of all, it appears everywhere — its full true nature is not concealed there by their covering. Thus the abode of <s>Śiva</s> is eternally complete in all states. (34)

body.translated_text: The ultimate truth is that the <s>turīya</s> form stands as pervading all states with unbroken continuity. By this much, does it follow that its true nature is concealed by them or not? He says:

body.text: vedāntabhāṣābhirjāgradādīnāṃ trayāṇāṃ svarūpaṃ vyavaharaṃstadanusyūtamapi tataḥ paraṃ turīyamāvedayati
body.translated_text: Using the terminology of <s>Vedānta</s>, describing the nature of the three states of waking and so forth, he reveals the <s>turīya</s> that pervades them yet is beyond them:

children.translated_text: "Waking is <s>Viśva</s> because of difference; dream is <s>Tejas</s> because of the greatness of luminosity;"
"<s>Prājña</s> is the state of deep sleep because of its being a mass of knowledge; beyond that is <s>turya</s> (the fourth). (35)"
is <s>Viśva</s>,
the <s>Vairāja</s> form of <s>Brahman</s>. Why?
Because of difference —

children.text: śabdādiviṣayapañcakasya bāhyatayā parameśvarasṛṣṭasyaiva sarvapramātṝṇāṃ cakṣurādīndriyapravṛtterityekasyaiva brahmaṇo viṣayaviṣayibhāvena sthitasya nānendriyajñānavaicitryam / ata eva śivasūtreṣu
children.translated_text: since the five objects such as sound and so forth, externally created by the Supreme Lord, engage the sense organs such as the eye of all subjects — it is the variety of sense-knowledge of one single <s>Brahman</s> standing in the relation of object and subject. For this very reason, in the <s>Śivasūtras</s>:

body.translated_text: The waking state itself
"Knowledge is waking."

body.text: iti / eṣā brahmaṇo virāḍavasthā gīyate / yacchrutiḥ
body.translated_text: This is celebrated as the <s>Virāṭ</s> state of <s>Brahman</s>. As <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) says:

children.text: yo viśvacakṣuruta viśvatomukho viśvatohasta uta viśvataspāt /
children.translated_text: "He who has eyes everywhere, faces everywhere, hands everywhere, feet everywhere —
with two arms he forges, with two thighs; the one God, generating heaven and earth."
dream
is the <s>Tejas</s> state of <s>Brahman</s>. Why? He says:
"Because of the greatness of luminosity."

children.text: iti / svapne bahiṣkaraṇāni śabdādau viṣaye tāvanna pragalbhante nāpi tatra bāhyaṃ śabdādikaṃ nāma kiñcitparamārthasadvidyate nāpi bāhyatayādhyavasāyasyāvidyādi kiñcidbhinnamabhinnaṃ vā kāraṇāntaramupalabhyate yuktyā vicāryamāṇaṃ vopapadyate 'tha ca svapne sarvaṃ prakāśate 'ta idamarthabalādāyātaṃ yatsa eva bhagavānsvasvabhāvo devastattatpramātṛtāṃ samāviṣṭaḥ svapnāyamānaḥ svātmānameva prakāśasvātantryādgṛhanagarāṭṭālādyanekapramātṛvaicitryarūpatayā pravibhajya pratipramātṛ svapne 'sādhāraṇameva viśvaṃ prakāśayatyeveti brahmaṇaḥ svātantryaṃ svapna eva brahmavādibhirabhyupagatam / yato vedānteṣvidamuktam
children.translated_text: In dream, the external sense organs do not function with regard to objects such as sound; nor does any external object such as sound truly exist there in ultimate reality; nor is any cause — whether different or non-different, such as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the like — perceived by which the external ascertainment could be accounted for, nor does it hold up when examined by reasoning. And yet everything shines forth in dream. Therefore, this follows from the force of the matter itself: that very Blessed One, the Lord, whose nature is his own Self, having entered this or that state of being a subject, dreaming, by the autonomy of his own luminosity, divides his own Self into the manifold forms of various subjects such as houses, cities, palaces, and so forth, and for each individual subject manifests in dream a universe that is entirely unique. Thus the autonomy of <s>Brahman</s> is acknowledged by the proponents of <s>Brahman</s> in dream itself. Since in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts it is stated:

body.translated_text: Likewise,

children.translated_text: "Having divided himself by himself, having created beings of various kinds,
the Lord of all, who is the Self of all, shines forth as the enjoyer in dream."

body.text: iti prakāśamāhātmyamevātra heturataḥ svapno brahmaṇastejo 'vastheti / tathā

children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> is the state of deep sleep.
The
state of deep sleep
(<s>suṣupti</s>) of all subjects, that is
<s>Prājña</s>

children.text: iti brahmaṇaḥ prājñāvastheti / yataḥ sarvapramātṝṇāṃ grāhyagrāhakaprapañcavilayānmahāśūnyatvarūpe grāhyādivilaye saṃskāraśeṣe suṣupte viśvasya bījabhūtasya brahmaṇa eva prajñā brahma prajñātṛtayāntaratamamavaśiṣyata iti yāvat / sarvasya pramāturnīlasukhādiviśvavaicitryaprathāyāḥ saiṣā saṃskārabhūmistataḥ prabuddhasya prāganubhūtavadvyavahāradarśanādanyathā yadyasyāṃ bhūmau sthiraṃ prajñātṛsvabhāvaṃ sarvakroḍīkāreṇa brahma na prākāśiṣyata kutastata utthitasya pramātuḥ prāganubhūtavastunastathaiva tadityanubhūtacaratvena smṛtirudapatsyata nāpi sukhamahamasvāpsaṃ duḥkhamahamasvāpsaṃ gāḍhamūḍho 'hamāsamityanubhavaḥ prādurabhaviṣyaditi / tathā ca bhaṭṭadivākaravatsaḥ
children.translated_text: — the <s>Prājña</s> state of <s>Brahman</s>. Since in the deep sleep of all subjects, with the dissolution of the entire expanse of grasped and grasper, in that state which is of the nature of a great void, where the grasped and so forth have dissolved and only <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) remain, the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) of <s>Brahman</s> — who is the seed of the universe — remains as the innermost in the capacity of the knower. This is the ground of <s>saṃskāras</s> for the manifestation of the entire variety of the universe — blue, pleasure, and so forth — for every subject; because upon awakening from it, one's behavior is seen to be just as if previously experienced. Otherwise, if <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is the knower, had not shone forth in that ground firmly and by encompassing everything, then for a subject arising from it, the memory of previously experienced objects as 'it was indeed thus' functioning as though experienced would not arise; nor would the experience 'I slept happily,' 'I slept painfully,' 'I was deeply confused' have arisen. And as <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> <s>Divākaravatsa</s> says:

body.translated_text: The greatness of luminosity alone is the reason here; therefore dream is the <s>Tejas</s> state of <s>Brahman</s>. Likewise,

children.translated_text: "If all experienced inner objects, well-protected by being made one's own,
were not present, then there could never be what is called memory, whose nature is the non-theft of known objects."

body.text: iti / itthaṃ suṣuptaṃ cinmayameva brahmaṇaḥ prājñāvastheti gīyate / kutaḥ

children.translated_text: "Because of being a mass of knowledge."

children.text: iti / suṣuptaturyayoḥ sādhāraṇo 'yaṃ heturityubhayatra yojyam / eṣā suṣuptabhūmiḥ
children.translated_text: This reason is common to both deep sleep and <s>turīya</s>, so it should be applied to both. This ground of deep sleep
is a mass of knowledge,

children.text: prakāśamūrtiḥ kevalaṃ viśvapralayasaṃskāreṇa dhyāmalā satī śuddhacinmayī na bhavatīti / yaduktaṃ spandaśāstre
children.translated_text: whose form is luminosity, but being darkened by the <s>saṃskāra</s> of universal dissolution, it is not purely of the nature of consciousness. As stated in the <s>Spandaśāstra</s>:

body.translated_text: Thus deep sleep, being of the nature of consciousness, is celebrated as the <s>Prājña</s> state of <s>Brahman</s>. Why?

children.translated_text: "United with the supreme power, whose nature is the knower and the known,
the all-pervading Lord shines in the two states; but elsewhere he is merely consciousness."
"beyond that is <s>turya</s> (the fourth)."
Beyond that deep sleep,
another,

children.text: anyanniḥśeṣapāśavavāsanāsaṃskāraparikṣayācchuddhapūrṇānandamayaṃ brahmaṇasturīyaṃ rūpamanuguṇaṃ nāma / yadatra nāmānvarthaṃ na kiñcidupapadyate 'to vyākhyātasyāvasthātrayasya viśrāmabhūtaṃ sarvāntaratamatvenānusyūtamiti catuḥsaṃkhyāpūraṇena
children.translated_text: the <s>turīya</s> form of <s>Brahman</s> — pure, complete, consisting of bliss, due to the complete exhaustion of the <s>vāsanās</s> (latent tendencies) and <s>saṃskāras</s> of all bonds — is accordingly named. Here no etymological meaning of the name is applicable; therefore, since it is the resting place of the previously explained triad of states, pervading them as the innermost of all, by the filling of the number four,
<s>turya</s> (the fourth)

children.text: iti pūraṇapratyayena saṃkhyāvyapadeśo 'tra kṛtaḥ kathamavasthātrayasyānusyūtamapi tataḥ parametadityāha
children.translated_text: — the ordinal suffix indicates a numerical designation here. How can it pervade the three states and yet be beyond them? He says:
"Because of being a mass of knowledge."

children.text: iti / yato jāgradādayo 'vasthāḥ sarvā bhedapravaṇatvātpramātṝṇāmajñānamayyasturīyaṃ grāhyagrāhakakṣobhapralayasaṃskāraparikṣayājjñānaghanaprakāśānandamūrtyatastadantaḥsthamapi tābhyo 'vasthābhyaścinmayatayā samuttīrṇatvāt
children.translated_text: Since all the states of waking and so forth, being inclined toward difference, are of the nature of ignorance for the subjects, while <s>turīya</s>, through the complete exhaustion of the agitation and dissolution and <s>saṃskāras</s> of the grasped and the grasper, is a mass of knowledge-luminosity-bliss in form — therefore, although situated within those states, because it transcends them through its nature of pure consciousness,
it is something other,

children.text: anyaditi / evamavasthāvicitraṃ paramādvayasvabhāvaṃ svatantraṃ brahmaiva pūrṇaṃ vijṛmbhate // 35 //
children.translated_text: beyond. Thus the autonomous <s>Brahman</s> alone manifests in its fullness, variegated by states yet of the nature of supreme non-duality. (35)

body.translated_text: Likewise,

body.text: evamapi śuddhasya paramātmanaḥ sarvapramātranusyūtatvena sthitatvādavaśyaṃ pramātṛgaṇagatamakhyātimālinyamāyātīti yattanneti dṛṣṭāntenāvedayati /
body.translated_text: Even so, since the pure Supreme Self stands pervading all subjects, surely the impurity of non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>) pertaining to the host of subjects would affect him — that this is not so, he reveals through an illustration:

children.translated_text: "Just as the vault of the sky is not made impure by clouds, smoke, and dust,"
"so too the Supreme Person is untouched by the modifications of <s>māyā</s>. (36)"
Just as

children.text: meghadhūmadhūlīpuñjairākāśasthairapyākāśapṛṣṭhamamalinaṃ svabhāvato na malinaṃ vidhīyate nāpi nityatāvaitatyakhaṇḍanāṃ vā nīyate kevalaṃ darpaṇapratibimbavattattadavasthāvicitraṃ gaganaṃ gaganameva sarvadā tathātvena pratyabhijñānāt /
children.translated_text: by masses of clouds, smoke, and dust, even though situated in the sky, the surface of the sky, which is inherently spotless, is not made impure, nor is it brought to a loss of its eternity or indivisibility — it simply remains the sky at all times, being recognized as such, merely variegated by this or that condition, like a reflection in a mirror.
So too,
in exactly the same way,
by the modifications of <s>māyā</s>,

by the transformations arising from non-recognition, pertaining to various subjects, consisting of manifold wondrous states such as birth, death, and so forth, even though situated in the Blessed One, the Blessed One is not
touched —
his true nature is not taken away by them, because he is the
Supreme Person (<s>Paraḥ Puruṣaḥ</s>)

children.text: iti sarvapuruṣāṇāṃ jīvānāmādya ullāso viśrāntisthānaṃ ceti sarvānubhavitṛtayā sadā sphuratīti paraśabdena nirdiṣṭaḥ / tasmānna svasamutthairaprakāśarūpairmāyāvikārairaindrajālikavadbhagavataḥ kācitkhaṇḍaneti parameṣṭhinā nareśvaraviveke 'pyuktam
children.translated_text: — the first efflorescence and resting place of all <s>puruṣas</s> (souls), of all living beings — and because he always pulsates as the experiencer of all, he is designated by the word 'supreme.' Therefore, by the modifications of <s>māyā</s> which are of the nature of non-luminosity, self-produced, the Blessed One is not at all diminished, like a magician. As <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> also said in the <s>Nareśvaraviveka</s>:
"Even though the existence of objects is regulated in the living being controlled by <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the subtle body,

children.text: jīve niruddhā tatrāpi paramātmani sā sthitā //
children.translated_text: even there it abides in the Supreme Self."

body.translated_text: "How could there be control by <s>prāṇa</s> for that which is of the nature of the Self itself?"

But if the <s>puruṣas</s>, whose ultimate reality is one consciousness alone, are subject to the variety of states such as distinct pleasure, pain, delusion, birth, death, and so forth — how can this be? He presents an illustration:

children.translated_text: "When the space in one pot is pervaded by dust, the other spaces do not become"
"impure. So too these living beings, subject to the distinctions of pleasure and pain. (37)"
when one
pot-space is covered by a mass of dust,
the other
pot-spaces, though spotless, because there is no difference in their being space,
do not become impure,
covered by dust.

children.text: / vimalaṃ vyāpakaṃ nityamapi hi gaganaṃ yādṛśaṃ ghaṭasaṃkocasaṃkucitaṃ bhavettādṛśameva tasyaiva ghaṭasya tadbhavati na punaḥ sarvāṇi ghaṭapaṭādyākāśāni kṛṣṇāgurudhūpitāni mṛgamadādhivāsitāni viṭhiragandhīni vaikākāśasvarūpatvātsaṃkīryante svagataghaṭādikṛtavicchedātpratyutaikatrāpi gagane vāstave sthite ghaṭādayaḥ svagatabhittisaṃkocaniyantritāḥ santo nānāgaganavaicitryaṃ prathayanti / itthaṃ ghaṭakṛtaḥ saṃkoca eva gaganatayā tathā viśiṣyate tathātvenārthakriyākāritvānna punaḥ gaganasyaitatkiñcidghaṭagataṃ mālinyādi svarūpatirodhānāya bhavati nāpi parasparaṃ ghaṭādyavacchinnānāṃ gaganānāṃ vyāmiśraṇeti /
children.translated_text: For space, though pure, all-pervading, and eternal, of whatever nature it is when contracted by the contraction of a pot, it becomes of that nature for that pot alone. But all pot-spaces, cloth-spaces, and so forth are not contaminated by being fumigated with black aloe incense, or scented with musk, or having foul odors — because of their being of the very nature of space, they are not mixed. Rather, due to the delimitation caused by the walls and so forth within each particular space, even when space exists as one reality, the pots and so forth, being regulated by the contraction of their own walls, manifest the variety of many spaces. Thus the contraction caused by the pot alone is differentiated as space in such a way that it functions accordingly; but for space itself, this impurity and so forth pertaining to the pot does not serve to conceal its true nature, nor is there intermingling of spaces delimited by pots and so forth.
So too,
in exactly the same way, these
living beings (<s>jīvas</s>),

children.text: puruṣā ekacinmātraparamārthā api pārameśvaryā māyāśaktyāṇavamāyīyaprākṛtakośatrayāveṣṭanena pūrṇaṃ vyāpi cidānandaikaghanaṃ svarūpamapahastya parimitīkṛtā yenaikacaitanyātmāno 'pi svagatakośatrayavicchedadaurātmyātparasparaṃ bhinnāśceti ghaṭapaṭādyākāśavat / itthaṃ māyīyakośakṛto viccheda eva jīvatayā vyavahriyate na punaḥ parameśvare 'navacchinnacidānandaikaghane jīvāḥ puruṣā ātmāno 'ṇava iti darśanāntaradṛṣṭaḥ kaścidvyavahāraḥ / evamāṇavādikośāvacchinnā jīvā anādivicitrakarmamalavāsanādhivāsitanānādehā nānāśayā nānāpuṇyapāpasvarganarakasukhaduḥkhajanmamaraṇādidvandvabhedabhājaśca santo nānyonyaṃ saṃkīryante yathā nānādravyādhivāsitāni ghaṭādyavacchinnāni ghaṭākāśānīti sūpapannamekacinmātraparamārthā api svavicchedādanyonyabhedajuṣaśceti // 37 //
children.translated_text: <s>puruṣas</s> (souls), though their ultimate reality is one consciousness alone, by the <s>māyā</s> power belonging to the Supreme Lord — through being enveloped by the threefold sheath of <s>āṇava</s> (pertaining to the individual), <s>māyīya</s> (pertaining to <s>māyā</s>), and <s>prākṛta</s> (pertaining to <s>prakṛti</s>) — have their complete, all-pervading nature, which is a compact mass of consciousness and bliss, pushed aside, and are made limited. Thus, even though of one consciousness-Self, due to the misfortune of being delimited by their own threefold sheath, they are mutually different — like the spaces in pots, cloths, and so forth. Thus the delimitation caused by the <s>māyīya</s> sheath alone is conventionally designated as being a <s>jīva</s>; but the Supreme Lord, who is an undelimited compact mass of consciousness and bliss, is not subject to the conventional usage seen in other philosophical systems — that <s>jīvas</s>, <s>puruṣas</s>, selves, <s>aṇus</s> (atoms of consciousness) are different. Thus the <s>jīvas</s>, delimited by the <s>āṇava</s> and other sheaths, scented by the <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) of beginningless and varied <s>karmic</s> impurity, having various bodies, various dispositions, and being subject to the duality-distinctions of varied merit and demerit, heaven and hell, pleasure and pain, birth and death — do not intermingle with one another, just as pot-spaces delimited by pots and scented by various substances do not. Thus it is well-established that though their ultimate reality is one consciousness alone, due to their own delimitation they are subject to mutual difference. (37)

body.translated_text: Just as

body.text: itthaṃ jīvamaṇḍalagatā avasthāviśeṣā ye te kevalaṃ bhagavatyupacaryante na punastattvataste 'tra kecidityāha
body.translated_text: Thus the particular states pertaining to the circle of living beings are merely attributed to the Blessed One figuratively, but in reality they do not pertain to him at all — he says:

children.text: śānte śānta ivāyaṃ hṛṣṭe hṛṣṭo vimohavati mūḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "When things are at peace, he appears peaceful; when joyful, joyful; when deluded, confused."

children.text: tattvagaṇe sati bhagavānna punaḥ paramārthataḥ sa tathā // 38 //
children.translated_text: "When the host of <s>tattvas</s> (reality-principles) exists, the Blessed One appears so, but in ultimate reality he is not so. (38)"
When the host of <s>tattvas</s>,
the group of sense organs,
is at peace,
when it has ceased, the Supreme Self situated in that is
as if peaceful,
considered as if destroyed. Likewise when that is
joyful,

children.text: sāhlāde sati sa tathaivopacaryate paraṃ tamomaye mūḍhe mohavāniti yathā sthāvarayonau
children.translated_text: in a state of delight, he is figuratively spoken of in the same way; and when it is dominated by darkness and confused, he is said to be subject to delusion, as in the case of immovable beings (plants).
"But in ultimate reality,"
in the true state of affairs,
he,
the Supreme Lord,
is not so —

children.text: tena prakāreṇa bhavati / sarvo hi jaḍabhāga utpādyaḥ saṃhāryo vā bhavati na punarnitye bhagavati bodhasvabhāve māyādikañcukagate vināśotpattī syātāmiti bhagavānsadā samaḥ // 38 //
children.translated_text: in that manner. For every inert portion is subject to production and destruction; but in the eternal Blessed One, whose nature is consciousness, wrapped in the coverings beginning with <s>Māyā</s>, there can be no destruction or production — thus the Blessed One is always the same. // 38 //

body.text: samutpattikrameṇāgatā bhrāntiḥ punarjñaptikrameṇa sutarāṃ samunmūlitā bhavatītyatra svātmana eva svātantryamityāha
body.translated_text: The delusion that arrived in the order of emanation is, conversely, most thoroughly uprooted in the order of realization — regarding this, [the author] states that the absolute freedom belongs to the Self itself:

children.translated_text: Having first dispelled the appearance of self-nature in what is non-self,
the Supreme Self destroys the delusion of non-self-nature in the Self. // 39 //
In the non-self —
in the body and the like, characterized as insentient — the [appearance] 'I am thin, I am stout,' and so on — that which is
the appearance of self-nature [in the non-self],
the apprehension of the non-self as the self,
that —
in that [context],
first —
from the very beginning,
having dispelled [it] —

children.text: ahaṃ cidānandaikaghano 'navacchinnasvabhāvaḥ svatantraścetyakṛtrimāhantāsphuraṇayā kṛtrimadehādipramātṛtāmapahṛtyātmaiva vigalitadehabandhaḥ paramātmatāṃ yātaḥ san
children.translated_text: through the spontaneous flash of the authentic I-consciousness — 'I am a solid mass of consciousness and bliss, of unrestricted nature, and free' — having thereby removed the artificial subjectivity of the body and the like, the Self itself, its bondage to the body having dissolved, having attained the state of the Supreme Self,
in the Self —
in this shining universal reality whose nature is radiance, which is, as it were, one's own limb, the
delusion —
the spread of difference generated by the false identification with the body and the like as the subject — that [delusion]
[the Supreme Self] destroys —

children.text: ahamevaiko viśvātmanā sphurāmītyevaṃ cūrṇīkaroti / idamatra tātparyaṃ yāvadanātmani dehādāvātmābhimāno na galitastāvatsvātmaprathārūpe 'pi jagati bhedaprathāmoho na vilīyate 'taścānātmanyātmābhimānabhramavināśādātmanyanātmābhimānabhrāntiṃ paramātmaiva svātmamaheśvaro bhagavāneva vināśayati nānyasyātra sāmarthyam // 39 //
children.translated_text: [thinking] 'I alone flash forth as the totality,' He thus pulverizes it. The essential purport here is: as long as the false identification with the body and the like as the self has not dissolved, so long does the delusion of differentiated manifestation not dissolve, even though the universe has the nature of self-manifestation. Therefore, from the destruction of the delusion of false identification of the self in the non-self (body etc.), the Supreme Self — the Lord of one's own Self, the Blessed One Himself — destroys the delusion of non-self-identification in the Self. No other has the capacity for this. // 39 //

body.text: evaṃ bhrāntidvayāpasāraṇātparameśvarībhūtasya yogino na kiñcitkāryamavaśiṣyata ityāha
body.translated_text: Thus, for the <s>yogin</s> who has become the Supreme Lord through the removal of the twofold delusion, nothing remains to be done — [the author] states:

children.translated_text: For one who has accomplished the complete uprooting of the pair of delusions in this way,
the supreme <s>yogin</s> never has any preoccupation with any other thing to be done. // 40 //
'In this way' —
by the method expounded in the meaning of the <s>kārikā</s>, [namely] the tearing out of the sprout of the twofold delusion,
'for one who has accomplished [the goal]' —
because of the full recognition of one's own absolute freedom, through the splitting asunder of all contraction,
'accomplished' —
attained
is the goal —

children.text: puruṣārthalābho yena tasya prakṛṣṭayogayuktasya na kadācit
children.translated_text: the attainment of the supreme human goal for the one who is established in the highest <s>yoga</s> — never
any other thing to be done —
any remaining duty in the form of pilgrimage, visiting sacred places, initiation, <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), exposition, listening, and the like —
preoccupation —
not even a mental engagement exists [for such a one].

body.translated_text: 'This indeed is the supreme <s>dharma</s>: that one sees the Self through <s>yoga</s>' —

body.text: iti hi svātmayogasya prādhānyamatastatprāptyā nānyatra pariśramaḥ pūrṇayoginaḥ / yaduktam
body.translated_text: for the primacy belongs to self-<s>yoga</s>; hence, upon its attainment, the accomplished <s>yogin</s> has no exertion elsewhere. As has been stated:

children.translated_text: 'When your intellect shall cross beyond the thicket of delusion,

children.text: tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca //
children.translated_text: then you shall attain to disgust with what has been heard and what is yet to be heard.'

body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Gītā</s>. // 40 //

body.text: saṃprati pṛthivyādimāyāntasya bhedāvabhāsabhājo viśvasya bhedābhedamayaśāktabhūmikāveśena pūrṇaprakāśānandaghanaśāṃbhavapadasamāpattyā bhedavilāyanena tadabhedamayatāprāptimabhidhāya tataḥ śāṃbhavātpadātsaṃpūrṇasudhāmbhodhikalpānmahāpravāhadeśīyaśāktaprasarollāsapramukhaṃ tattattaraṅgabhaṅgirūpatāmabhidadhatsvānubhavasiddhaṃ mahāmantravīryasāraṃ samastabhedavilāyanaparamādvayodayaṃ naraśaktiśivasāmarasyātmakaṃ parasaṃviddhṛdayaṃ krameṇonmīlayiṣyanviśvasyāgamikāṇḍatrayātmatāsaṃkalanayuktyaikīkāraṃ tāvadāha
body.translated_text: Now, having demonstrated — through the perspective of reabsorption (<s>saṃhāra</s>) — how the universe of differentiated appearance, from earth to <s>Māyā</s>, which has the nature of the human level, attains identity with the undifferentiated mass of consciousness that is <s>Śiva</s>, through ascent to the <s>Śākta</s> level which consists of both difference and non-difference, and through the dissolution of difference therein — [the author], intending to reveal the heart of supreme consciousness (<s>parasaṃvid</s>), consisting of the identity of <s>nara</s> (human), <s>śakti</s> (power), and <s>śiva</s>, which is the supreme non-duality dissolving all difference, the essence of the great <s>mantra</s>'s potency, established through self-experience, [and which arises] beginning with the expansion of the <s>Śākta</s> level as a great flood from the <s>Śāmbhava</s> level — full like the ocean of nectar — in the form of various wave-crests, will gradually unfold [this teaching]. First, [the author] states the unification through the rationale that the universe has the nature of the three sections of scripture:

children.translated_text: Earth, <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), and <s>Māyā</s> — this triad, which has fallen into the state of the knowable,
through the power of the contemplation of non-duality, becomes a mere residue of pure Being. // 41 //
'has fallen into the state of the knowable' —
has entered the domain of cognition.

body.translated_text: The threefold [universe], consisting of the earthly, natural (<s>prākṛta</s>), and <s>Māyīya</s> spheres — gross, subtle, and transcendent in form —

children.translated_text: 'Knowledge shines outwardly and inwardly in the form of each respective [object];
apart from knowledge there is no existence of an object — therefore the universe has the nature of knowledge.'
'For entities are never made objects by anyone apart from knowledge;
knowledge has assumed their identity — from this it is ascertained.'
the contemplation of non-duality (<s>advaitabhāvana</s>) —
by the power of that, by its intensification,
a mere residue of pure Being —
consisting solely of being, which is of the nature of luminous manifestation,
[it] becomes.
'Hi' [indicates]
the reason. // 41 //

body.translated_text: By the principle stated in the sacred <s>Kālikākrama</s>, that which is
This very [point] is substantiated with the intention of demonstrating the unreality of difference:

children.translated_text: Just as gold is seen when one abandons the differentiation of necklace, earring, and bracelet,
so too, when difference is abandoned, everything shines as pure Being alone. // 42 //

body.text: yathā kila sauvarṇaṃ raśanādyābharaṇaṃ suvarṇārthino raśanāviśeṣaparihāreṇa hemamātratayaivābhāti hemarajatakāṃsyatāmranāgādi tāvanmātrārthino loharūpatayā

children.translated_text: In the same way, everything —
for the <s>yogin</s> who, having abandoned the stain of <s>vikalpas</s> (mental constructs) such as acceptance and rejection, is established solely in the non-conceptual reflective awareness,

body.translated_text: Just as a golden ornament — a necklace and the like — for one who desires gold, when the particular distinction of necklace is set aside, shines as mere gold alone; [and similarly] for one who desires just that much — gold, silver, bronze, copper, lead, and the like — [everything appears] in the form of mere metal.
'its establishment follows from transformation in form and the like' —

children.translated_text: when difference is abandoned,
when [it] is [abandoned],
pure Being alone —
consisting solely of being,
shines forth.

body.translated_text: according to the method stated by the venerable <s>Bhaṭṭa Śrī Kallaṭa</s>,

body.text: tadiyataḥ sarvasya saṃkocāvabhāsaparityāgādāgamaprasiddhyā nararūpasya śāktarūpopārohaṃ mantrasaṃpradāyaṃ kaṭākṣayannabhidadhāti
body.translated_text: Since, through the abandonment of the contracted appearance of everything, and in accord with the scriptural tradition, [the author] glances at the <s>mantra</s> tradition regarding the ascent of the human form to the <s>Śākta</s> form — [the author] states:

children.text: tadbrahma paraṃ śuddhaṃ śāntamabhedātmakaṃ samaṃ sakalam /
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahman</s> — supreme, pure, peaceful, whose nature is non-difference, equal, complete,
immortal, true — reposes in <s>Śakti</s>, whose nature is radiance. // 43 //
That —
this entirety, whose nature is pure Being, because of its vastness,
[is called] <s>Brahman</s>.
As the knowers of the culmination of the <s>Śruti</s> declare:

body.translated_text: 'In the beginning, dear one, this was Being alone.'

children.translated_text: [it is] supreme (<s>para</s>).
Because there is nothing to be rejected or accepted,
[it is] pure (<s>śuddha</s>).
Because of the subsidence of separateness,
[it is] peaceful (<s>śānta</s>).
For this very reason,
[it is] of the nature of non-difference (<s>abhedātmaka</s>).
Because there is no superiority or inferiority,
[it is] equal (<s>sama</s>).

body.translated_text: Because of its completeness,
'Even a portion of <s>Brahman</s> has the nature of all things, is unsurpassed, and is beyond conceptual construction.'

children.translated_text: [it is] complete (<s>sakala</s>).
For this very reason,
[it is] immortal (<s>amṛta</s>) —
imperishable.

body.translated_text: Having thus established,

children.text: satyāsatyau tu yau bhāgau pratibhāvaṃ vyavasthitau /
children.translated_text: 'The two portions, real and unreal, are established corresponding to each manifestation;

children.text: satyaṃ yattatra sā jātirasatyā vyaktayaḥ sthitāḥ //
children.translated_text: that which is real therein is the universal (<s>jāti</s>); the particulars (<s>vyakti</s>) stand as unreal.'

body.text: yadādau ca yadante ca yanmadhye tasya satyatā /
body.translated_text: 'That which [exists] at the beginning, at the end, and in the middle — therein lies its reality.'

children.translated_text: [it is] true (<s>satya</s>).
This very entirety, whose nature is pure Being,
'in <s>Śakti</s> whose nature is radiance' —
in the supreme <s>Śakti</s>, whose nature is the equilibrium of the powers of will (<s>icchā</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>), it reposes —

body.translated_text: According to the method established by the venerable <s>Bhartṛhari</s>,
'The determination of objects rests in consciousness' —
by this principle, it becomes one with that. And further,

children.translated_text: 'Peaceful' (<s>śānta</s>) —
that which follows after the <s>ś</s>-sound in the cerebral form, and beyond that, that which is
'Immortal' (<s>amṛta</s>) —
consisting of the <s>amṛta</s>-<s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable of immortality),
'<s>Brahman</s>' —
consisting of pure Being, from contact with the level called <s>Sadākhya</s> (the level of pure Being),
'Pure' (<s>śuddha</s>) —
for this very reason, through the equalization of everything — 'I am all this' —
'Equal' and 'Complete' (<s>sama</s>, <s>sakala</s>) —
and further, from the dissolution of [the sense of] 'otherness,'
'True' (<s>satya</s>).
As the Blessed One has taught:

body.translated_text: [considering also:]
'The third <s>Brahman</s>, O beautiful-hipped one ...'

body.text: iti śrītriṃśikāyām / tadidamamṛtībhāvāvamṛṣṭaṃ sadāśivapadopārūḍhametadviśvātmakaṃ brahma prāguktāyāṃ śaktau viśrāmyati // 43 //
body.translated_text: thus in the sacred <s>Triṃśikā</s>. This very [<s>Brahman</s>], tasted as having become immortal, having ascended to the level of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, this <s>Brahman</s> which is the totality of the universe, reposes in the <s>Śakti</s> described earlier. // 43 //

body.text: kriyājñānecchāmukhena paraśaktau yanna viśrāmyati tanna kiñcidityāha
body.translated_text: That which does not repose in the supreme <s>Śakti</s> through will, knowledge, and action is nothing whatsoever — [the author] states:

children.text: iṣyata iti vedyata iti saṃpādyata iti ca bhāsvarūpeṇa /
children.translated_text: 'It is desired,' 'it is known,' 'it is accomplished' — [whatever shines] in the form of radiance;
that which is not apprehended [thus] attains the status of a sky-flower (i.e., is non-existent). // 44 //
[it is] not apprehended,

that, devoid of both manifestation (<s>prakhyā</s>) and designation (<s>upākhyā</s>), is equal to a sky-flower. And by this, the potency of the trident-formed activity, operating above the <s>sadvṛtti</s> (activity of Being), is indicated. // 44 //

body.translated_text: Whatever thing, though existing in actuality in the external world, if through consciousness — radiant, consisting of the expansion of the supreme <s>Śakti</s> which is the equilibrium of the three powers of will, knowledge, and action —
Restating this absorption into the <s>Śākta</s> level and making manifest the state of identity with it through attainment of the <s>Śāmbhava</s> level, [the author] says:

children.translated_text: Through the means of encompassing the trident of powers, everything, into the Supreme Lord,
into [Him] named <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Reality, is emitted by the God of gods. // 45 //
everything —
this entirety, which because of its nature as pure Being has the Supreme Reality of <s>Brahman</s> as described,
through the means of encompassing the trident of powers —
by the established reasoning, through the method of attainment of the supreme <s>Śakti</s>,
into [Him] named <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Reality —
into the Supreme Lord, the undivided solid mass of consciousness and bliss, into one's own essential nature,
is emitted —
through the intensification of inward-turned reflective awareness, by absorption into That, it is brought to the state of identity with That.
'Of the gods' —
of all luminaries, from <s>Brahmā</s> to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and also of the sense organs,
'God' —

children.text: prabhuṇā paramaśivenaiva nahyatrānyasya kasyacitkartṛtvaṃ ghaṭate nāpyetadvyatirikto 'nyaḥ kaścitpramātāstyasyaiva ca bhagavatastattadbhūmikādhirohiṇastattadrudrakṣetrajñādipramātṛrūpatayā sphuraṇamiti
children.translated_text: the Lord, the Supreme <s>Śiva</s> Himself — for no other can function as an agent here, nor does any other subject exist apart from this [Supreme <s>Śiva</s>]; and it is this very Blessed One, ascending to various levels, who flashes forth in the form of various subjects such as <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Kṣetrajña</s>, and the like — hence
'God of gods' —
is a fitting expression. Thus the <s>visarga</s>-activity has been shown. // 45 //

body.translated_text: Thus indeed,

body.text: evamiyatā bhedātmano nararūpasya jagato bhedābhedātmakaśāktapadādhyāroheṇābhinnacidghanaśivasāmarasyāpattimupasaṃhāradṛśā pradarśyedānīṃ cidekaghanaḥ śiva eva śaktirūpatayollāsya narātmakaviśvarūpatayā sphurati na tu śivavyatiriktaṃ śaktinarayoḥ kimapi rūpaṃ śiva eva tvitthaṃ nijarasāśyānatayā sphuratīti prasarayuktiṃ mahāmantrasphāramayīṃ darśayati
body.translated_text: Having thus shown, by this extent, from the perspective of reabsorption, how the universe of the human form, whose nature is differentiated, attains identity with the undifferentiated solid mass of consciousness that is <s>Śiva</s>, through ascent to the <s>Śākta</s> level which consists of both difference and non-difference and through dissolution of difference — [the author] now demonstrates from the perspective of emanation that it is <s>Śiva</s> alone, as a solid mass of consciousness, who, having flashed forth as <s>Śakti</s>, manifests as the universe whose nature is the human [level] — and that <s>Śakti</s> and the human [levels] have no form apart from <s>Śiva</s>; rather, it is <s>Śiva</s> alone who thus flashes forth through the relish of His own nature — [the author] displays this reasoning of emanation, suffused with the expansion of the great <s>mantra</s>:

children.translated_text: And again, through the process of emanation of the five powers, outwardly too, that
variegated triple sphere is emitted, through the attainment of externality. // 46 //
that triple sphere, variegated —
consisting of various worlds and the like,
is emitted, through the attainment of externality —
through displaying one's own self as having the nature of external appearance.
'And again' —

children.text: ityanenaitaddarśayati yatparamaśiva eva svatantraḥ sadā svabhittau viśvaprapañcollāsanavilāpanakrīḍāṃ svātmānatiriktāmapyatiriktāmivādarśayannevamitthaṃ sthito na tu tadvyatiriktaṃ kimapyastīti // 46 //
children.translated_text: by this [word the author] shows that the Supreme <s>Śiva</s> alone, of absolute freedom, upon His own canvas always plays the game of flashing forth and dissolving the universal manifold — a game that, though non-different from Himself, He displays as if different — and He abides just thus; nothing else exists apart from Him. // 46 //

body.translated_text: The Supreme <s>Śiva</s>, whose nature is the equilibrium of the fivefold powers called consciousness (<s>cit</s>), bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), will (<s>icchā</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>) — through the method of unfolding the levels called <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Śuddhavidyā</s>, which consist of the predominant manifestation of the powers beginning with consciousness —

children.translated_text: is called '<s>Śiva</s>' —

children.text: iti vyapadiśyate sa katamaḥ kutra tiṣṭhati katamena vā pramāṇena prasiddha ityāśaṅkya sarveṣāṃ svātmaiva śivaḥ sarvatrādisiddhatayā sphuransargādīnvidadhātītyasmacchabdavācakaiḥ śabdaiḥ pratipādayati
children.translated_text: who is He, where does He abide, and by what means of knowledge is He established? Anticipating this doubt, [the author] demonstrates through words signified by the word 'I' (<s>aham</s>) that the Self of everyone is <s>Śiva</s>, who, shining forth as primordially established in all, performs emanation and the like:

body.translated_text: Thus, the Blessed One, whose nature is the play of flashing forth and dissolving the universe — He who

children.translated_text: Thus, driving the mechanism of the wheel of powers through the play of <s>yoga</s>, the God —
I myself, of pure nature, established in the position of the leader of the great wheel of powers — // 47 //

children.text: mayyeva bhāti viśvaṃ darpaṇa iva nirmale ghaṭādīni /
children.translated_text: In me alone the universe shines, like pots and the like in a clear mirror.
From me alone everything emanates, like the variegated [imagery] of a dream from one who is asleep. // 48 //
I myself am of the nature of the universe, like the body whose nature is hands, feet, and the like.
In everything I alone flash forth among entities, like the nature of radiance [in all things]. // 49 //
The seer, the hearer, the smeller — though devoid of body and senses, though a non-agent —
I alone compose the wondrous doctrines of <s>Siddhānta</s>, <s>Āgama</s>, and logical reasoning. // 50 //

body.text: iti vyākhyātena prakāreṇa cidādiśaktipañcakākṣipto 'nanto yaḥ śaktisamūhastadeva

children.translated_text: mechanism [of the wheel of powers], driving [it] through the play [of <s>yoga</s>] —
revolving it through the sport of immersion and emergence in emanation and the like, by the principle of the waterwheel mechanism — 'I alone' — thus,
the God —
of all living beings,
'I' (<s>aham</s>) —

children.text: ityanāhato nādātmā parāhantācamatkārasāraḥ svātmaparāmarśaḥ sa eva sarvasyānapahnavanīyo 'yaṃ svātmaiva
children.translated_text: the unstruck sound (<s>anāhata nāda</s>), whose essence is the savor of the supreme I-consciousness wonder, the self-reflective awareness — that alone is the undeniable Self of everyone — this very Self,
[is] the God —

children.text: krīḍanaśīlaḥ sphuratīti / anena svasvarūpaniṣṭha eva śiva iti pratipāditam / tathā śuddharūpa iti kalpanātikrāntagocaraḥ / anyacca
children.translated_text: He who is playful by nature shines forth. By this it is established that <s>Śiva</s> is established in His own essential nature. Likewise, 'of pure form' means one whose domain transcends conceptual construction. And further,
of the <s>śaktis</s> (powers) —
that which bestows autonomy in the activities of grasping and relinquishing sense-objects upon the <s>karaṇadevatās</s> (deities of the sense-faculties) — that
position of the great <s>cakranāyaka</s> (lord of the wheel [of powers]) —
in that he abides;
he is established in that.

children.text: / yataḥ karaṇaśaktīnāṃ caitanyaviśrāntiṃ vinā svarūpasattā na vidyate 'taḥ śaktimantameva svarūpāsādanāyānavarataṃ bhajanta ityanena sarvapramātṛhṛdayādhiṣṭhātṛtvādbhagavato niyatabhuvanādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ parihṛtam / tathā yadidaṃ kiñcidviśvatayābhimataṃ tatsarvamādarśapratibimbanyāyena
children.translated_text: Since the sense-faculties' powers have no existence of their own without reposing in consciousness, they ceaselessly worship the possessor of power alone in order to attain their own nature — by this, since the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord) is the presiding lord of the hearts of all cognizers, the notion that He presides over only specific worlds is rejected. Likewise, whatever exists that is considered as the universe, all that, by the principle of reflections in a mirror,
'shines in Me alone' —
it manifests as reposing in Me, whose nature has been explained; it shines forth having the I-consciousness as its essence — that is the meaning. Likewise,
'from Me' —

children.text: iti pūrṇādahamiti rūpātsvātmanaḥ sakalaṃ niḥśeṣamidaṃ viśvam
children.translated_text: from the self, whose form is the perfect 'I,' this entire universe without remainder
'issues forth' —
it shines forth as if projected, from the perspective of the cognizer. How? He says:
'like the diversity of a dream from a sleeping person' —

children.text: iti yathā nidritātpramātuḥ svapnāvasthāyāṃ bāhyapadārthābhāve 'pi puraprākāradevagṛhādi nānāścaryaṃ svapnapadārthavaicitryamavidyādiparikalpitakāraṇāntarābhāvātsvasaṃvidupādānameva prasarati tathaiva tīrthāntaraniyamitakāraṇāntarānupapatteranavacchinnacidānandaikaghanādahamiti rūpādviśvamiti / tathā
children.translated_text: Just as from a sleeping cognizer, in the dream state, even in the absence of external objects, a diverse wonder of dream-objects — cities, ramparts, temples, and so forth — issues forth, having one's own consciousness as its material cause alone, since there is no other cause constructed by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the like; similarly, because another cause posited by rival schools is untenable, the universe [issues forth] from the self whose form is 'I' — an undivided mass of consciousness and bliss. Likewise,
'I alone am the form of the universe' —

children.text:
ityādi / ahamityeva yaḥ pūrṇaścaitanyaparāmarśa eṣa evāsmi nānādehādipramātṛtāsamāpanno viśvarūpa āgopālabālāṅganādiṣvantarabhedena sphuraṇādviśvāni mamaiva rūpāṇīti yāvat / ka iva karacaraṇādisvabhāvo deha iva yathā sāmānyena sarveṣāmeko dehaḥ karacaraṇādisvabhāvaḥ pratipramātṛ svālakṣaṇyena nānārūpastathaivaikaścaitanyalakṣaṇaḥ padārthaḥ sarvāvāsatvādviśvarūpa
iti / tathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. That which is the perfect reflective awareness of consciousness as 'I' — that alone am I, having assumed the nature of diverse cognizers such as various bodies and the like — of the form of the universe; since I shine forth with internal differentiation in cowherd boys, women, etc. — that is, all forms are mine. Like what? Like one having the nature of hands, feet, etc. — like the body: just as in general there is one body for all, having the nature of hands, feet, etc., yet for each individual cognizer it has different forms through its own particular characteristics — similarly, the one reality whose nature is consciousness, being the abode of all, is of the form of the universe. Likewise,
'in everything' —
in this [reality] having the form of the cognizer, the means of cognition, and the object of cognition,
'I alone shine forth' —
because everything is illuminated through being experienced by one's own Self. How?
'like the nature of light in things' —
Just as in diverse objects,
'the nature of light' —

children.text: atiśayena dyotanaśīlaṃ vastu dedīpyate tathaiva jaḍe 'smiñjagatyekaścidrūpo 'hamiti / ataśca
children.translated_text: a luminous substance that by nature intensely shines — so too in this inert world, I alone am of the nature of consciousness. And therefore,
'the seer' —
and so forth.
'even without body and sense-organs' —

children.text: cinmūrtatvādahameva paśyāmi śṛṇomi jighrāmi rasayāmi spṛśāmīti sarvatra pūrṇāhantāviśrānteḥ kṛtakṛtyatā / dehendriyavargo hi paśyāmītyādi manyate paraṃ svāpādyavasthāsu draṣṭṛtvādyabhāvāttasmāddehendriyādivargasamullāsakastadvarjito 'pi cidānandaikaghanaḥ sarvabhūtahṛdayāntaracārī viṣayopabhogabhoktāsmacchabdavācyaḥ paraḥ puruṣa eva / tathā ca śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: because my very form is consciousness, I alone see, hear, smell, taste, and touch — thus, because everywhere there is repose in the perfect I-consciousness, the state of having accomplished what is to be accomplished [is attained]. The aggregate of body and senses indeed thinks 'I see' and so forth; but since in states such as deep sleep etc. there is no seeing, etc., therefore the one who, even without the aggregate of body, senses, etc., being a solid mass of consciousness and bliss alone, moves within the hearts of all beings, is the experiencer of the enjoyment of sense-objects — He who is denoted by the word 'I,' the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) indeed. Thus the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) states:

body.translated_text: In the manner explained, the infinite assembly of powers projected by the fivefold powers beginning with consciousness — that very

children.text: apāṇipādo javano grahītā paśyatyacakṣuḥ sa śṛṇotyakarṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Without hands or feet, He is swift and a grasper; He sees without eyes; He hears without ears;

children.text: sa vetti vedyaṃ na ca tasyāsti vettā tamāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam //
children.translated_text: He knows all that is to be known, but none knows Him — they call Him the foremost, the great <s>Puruṣa</s>.'

body.text: iti / tathākartāpi siddhāntāgama ityādi svayamavidhātāpi devamunimanuṣyādyāśayāviṣṭaḥ saṃkṣepavistāravivakṣayāntaḥpratibhāsvarūpo 'haṃ siddhāntādīnnānāścaryānkaromi na punarjaḍānāṃ loṣṭasthānīyānāṃ dehendriyāṇāṃ tatkaraṇaṃ śakyamiti tattadvyavadhānenāhameva sarvapramāṇanirmāteti / anena parāhantāsvarūpasya svātmamaheśvarasya sattāyāṃ na pramāṇopayoga upapadyata upayujyate vetyuktaṃ syāt / evamanapahnavanīyaḥ

children.text: ityevamanubhavitṛtayā sarveṣāṃ svātmaiva śivaḥ sarvatrāvasthitaḥ sarvapramāṇeṣvādisiddha iti // 47 // 48 // 49 // 50 //
children.translated_text: thus, through being experienced by all as their very Self, <s>Śiva</s> Himself is established everywhere, primordially established in all means of knowledge. // 47 // 48 // 49 // 50 //

body.translated_text: Likewise, 'even though not an agent — <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), <s>āgama</s> (scripture)' and so forth. Even though not Himself a creator, having entered into the dispositions of gods, sages, humans, and others, with the intention of being brief or extensive, having the nature of internal manifestation as 'I,' I produce <s>siddhāntas</s> and other marvelous [works]; but inert things like clods of earth — the body and senses — cannot do that; therefore, through the instrumentality of those [body and senses], I alone am the creator of all means of knowledge. By this, it is stated that when the existence of the great Lord as one's own Self, having the nature of the supreme I-consciousness, is established, the application of means of knowledge is neither needed nor applicable. Thus, undeniable is

body.text: tadevaṃ vyākhyātena krameṇa sarvo mamāyaṃ vibhava iti dārḍhyena svātmānaṃ pratyavamṛśanparabrahmasvarūpo yogī bhavatītyāha
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>yogī</s> (practitioner) who, in the manner explained, firmly reflects upon his own Self [thinking] 'all this splendor is mine,' becomes of the nature of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — he says:

children.text: itthaṃ dvaitavikalpe galite pravilaṅghya mohanīṃ māyām /
children.translated_text: [Verse:] Thus, when the conceptual construction of duality has dissolved, having transcended the deluding <s>Māyā</s>, one would merge in <s>Brahman</s> like water in water, like milk in milk. // 51 //

children.text: salile salilaṃ kṣīre kṣīramiva brahmaṇi layī syāt // 51 //
children.translated_text: In this manner, through the practice of cultivating the sense of 'I' in everything,
when the manifestation of difference has melted away,
'having transcended the deluding <s>Māyā</s>' —

children.text: anātmanyātmābhimānarūpāmakhyātiṃ bhedaprathāhetumahameva viśvātmeti saṃkocāpasaraṇena samutsṛjya jñānī
children.translated_text: having cast off <s>akhyāti</s> (non-recognition), which has the form of self-identification with the non-self, the cause of the manifestation of difference — through the withdrawal of contraction, [thinking] 'I alone am the Self of the universe,' the knower
'in <s>Brahman</s>' —
in one's own essential nature, which is expansive by nature, full, a solid mass of consciousness and bliss,
'would merge' —
through the dissolution of contraction, one would attain identity with <s>Brahman</s>. Like what? He says:
'in water' —
and so forth. Just as
'water' —

children.text: uddhṛtaṃ nānāghaṭādibhirjalaṃ kṣīraṃ vā vividhaśāvaleyabāhuleyādyanekagosahasrasaṃbhinnaṃ punarapi ghaṭaśāvaleyādikṛtabhedasaṃkocaparikṣayāt
children.translated_text: water drawn out by various pots and the like, or milk differentiated by various breeds of cows — thousands of them — again, through the complete destruction of the contraction of difference imposed by pots, breeds, etc.,
'water in water' —
having entered,
'milk in milk' —

children.text: vetyekameva tadvastu na tatra bhedaḥ sphurati tathaiva dehaprāṇapuryaṣṭakaśūnyātmakapratyavamarśabhaṅgādbrahmaiva saṃpadyate / yathāha bhaṭṭadivākaravatsaḥ
children.translated_text: becomes that one thing alone, and no difference shines forth there — similarly, through the dissolution of the reflective awareness of the body, vital breath, <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body), and the void, one becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself. As <s>Bhaṭṭa Divākaravatsa</s> has said:

body.translated_text: 'when the conceptual construction of duality has dissolved' —

children.translated_text: 'When the island of body-based cognition is shattered, having reached oneness in the pure ocean of awareness,
not turning back the aggregate of senses within, you, the Self of the universe, shine forth eternally, alone.'

body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Kakṣyāstotra</s>. // 51 //

body.text: evaṃ brahmasattāmadhirūḍhasya yogino dvandvābhibhavo 'pi brahmamaya eva na svarūpavipralopāya pragalbhata ityāha
body.translated_text: Thus, even the conquest of the pairs of opposites by the <s>yogī</s> who has ascended to the reality of <s>Brahman</s> is itself of the nature of <s>Brahman</s> and does not serve to undermine his essential nature — he says:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] Thus, when the aggregate of principles has attained the state of being <s>Śiva</s> through contemplation, what grief is there? What delusion? — for one who beholds everything as <s>Brahman</s>. // 52 //

children.text: kaḥ śokaḥ ko mohaḥ sarvaṃ brahmāvalokayataḥ // 52 //
children.translated_text: In the manner thus determined,
the host of elements, sense-objects, and sense-organs — for the <s>yogī</s> whose bondage of the sheaths has dissolved,
'through contemplation' —
through the firm conviction that 'all this is one's own consciousness,'
'the state of being <s>Śiva</s>' —
having been attained, having reached the state of supreme non-duality, the conquests of the pairs of opposites indicated by grief and delusion —
'everything' —
this host of principles —
'<s>Brahman</s>' —

children.text: paśyato 'sya na kecanaiva te brahmamayatvātsarve svarūparūpā iti na khedāya prabhavanti // 52 //
children.translated_text: for one who sees [thus], they are none at all; because they are of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, they are all of the nature of one's own Self, and hence they do not have the power to cause distress. // 52 //

body.translated_text: 'the aggregate of principles' —

body.text: nanu paramādvayarūpasyāpi jñānino 'vaśyaṃ sthite śarīre 'pi taddhetukaśubhāśubhakarmaphalasaṃcayaḥ kimiti na syāditi pariharati
body.translated_text: But even for the knower who is of the nature of supreme non-duality, while the body still remains, why should there not be an accumulation of the fruits of good and bad <s>karmas</s> caused by it? — this he resolves:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] The fruit of <s>karma</s>, whether good or bad, arises solely from association with false knowledge; for the fault of association is perilous — like the association with a thief even for one who is not a thief. // 53 //
'arises solely from association with false knowledge' —

children.text: prādurbhavatyahaṃ śarīrīdamaśvamedhādi mamopāyatayāstviti yadanātmanyātmābhimānalakṣaṇaṃ vaiparītyena jñānaṃ tena yo 'bhiṣvaṅgastasmādeva paśoḥ śubhāśubhakarmaphalasaṃcayo yenānavaratādhivāsitaḥ saṃsārakleśabhājanaṃ bhavati / nanu brahmātmakasyāpi pramātuḥ kimityetāvatā paśutvamāyātītyatrārthāntaramupakṣipati
children.translated_text: it comes into being from the identification 'I am an embodied being; this <s>Aśvamedha</s> etc. belongs to me as a means' — that knowledge which has the character of false self-identification with the non-self, the attachment that comes from that — it is from that alone that the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) has the accumulation of the fruits of good and bad <s>karmas</s>, by which, being constantly permeated, it becomes a vessel for the afflictions of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). But how does the cognizer who is of the nature of <s>Brahman</s> come to the state of a bound soul merely by this? — introducing another point, he says:
'perilous indeed' —
and so forth. Because
'the fault of association' —

children.text: sarvathāviṣahyo yathāsādhuyogo 'tyantasādhorapi svagatadoṣasamarpaṇaṃ kurute tathaiva śuddhasyāpi pramāturakhyātijanito mohayogaḥ paśutvamāpādya śubhāśubhakarmasaṃbandhaṃ dadāti // 53 //
children.translated_text: is utterly unbearable in every way; just as association with a non-virtuous person causes even an extremely virtuous person to receive the faults belonging to the other, similarly, the delusory association born of <s>akhyāti</s> (non-recognition), even for a pure cognizer, brings about the state of a bound soul and gives rise to the connection with good and bad <s>karmas</s>. // 53 //

body.translated_text: Even the accumulation of the fruits of meritorious and sinful <s>karmas</s> such as the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), <s>Brahmahatyā</s> (killing of a Brahmin), and the like,

body.text: janmamaraṇādyapi na brahmarūpasya yogino 'pi tu māyāpramātṝṇāmevetyāha
body.translated_text: Birth, death, and the like do not belong to the <s>yogī</s> whose nature is <s>Brahman</s>, but only to those cognizers who are under <s>Māyā</s> — he says:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] Those deluded ones who in this world worship <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) consisting of worldly conventions, bound by the bolt of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> (merit and demerit),
they undergo birth and death. // 54 //

body.text: ye pramātāro dehātmamānino bhūtvā phalakāmanākaluṣitā lokācārarūpāṃ puṇyāpuṇyamayīm

children.translated_text: '<s>avidyā</s>' (ignorance) —
the <s>Māyā</s> in the form of the manifestation of difference, in the world, as a means for attaining the fruits of heaven, hell, etc.,
'those deluded ones' —

children.text: ajñāḥ puṇyāpuṇyanigaḍabaddhāstatphalopabhogāya punaḥ punarjāyante mriyante cetyanavaratasaṃsārakleśabhājo bhavanti na punaḥ prakṣīṇamohāvaraṇo vigalitadharmādharmabandho brahmasvabhāvo yogī jāyate mriyate veti // 54 //
children.translated_text: those ignorant ones, bound by the fetters of merit and demerit, are born and die again and again for the sake of experiencing those fruits — thus they become vessels for the ceaseless afflictions of <s>saṃsāra</s>. But the <s>yogī</s> whose nature is <s>Brahman</s>, whose veil of delusion has been destroyed, whose bondage of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> has dissolved — he is neither born nor dies. // 54 //

body.translated_text: Those cognizers who, having become identified with the body, sullied by the desire for results, serve the <s>Māyā</s> consisting of merit and demerit in the form of worldly conduct,
Thus, even <s>karmas</s> accumulated through <s>avidyā</s> are destroyed through the very arising of knowledge and not otherwise — he says:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] But even <s>karma</s> consisting of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, accumulated during the time of ignorance, perishes through the power of the radiance of knowledge, like cotton long accumulated. // 55 //
'During the time of ignorance' —
at the time when there is the false identification as a fabricated cognizer, <s>karma</s> in the form of merit and demerit,
'<s>karma</s>' —
that which, through desire for corresponding fruits,
'has been accumulated' —
has been accepted — that
'through the power of the radiance of knowledge' —
through the power of the radiance of supreme knowledge,
'perishes' —

children.text: ahameva paraṃ brahmeti kṛtrimapramātṛtādāhasamarthaṃ vijñānaṃ tasya yā paunaḥpunyena pratyavamarśanātprabhā tatsāmarthyāttadadarśanaṃ yāti / kimivetyāha
children.translated_text: The knowledge 'I alone am the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' is capable of burning up the fabricated cognizer-identity; its radiance — through repeated reflective awareness — by the power of that, [<s>karma</s>] is annihilated. Like what? He says:
'like cotton long accumulated' —

children.text: yathā cirasaṃcitaṃ tūlaṃ haṃsaroma vahnipradīptivaśājjhaṭityeva bhasmasādyāti tathaiva sarvaḥ karmaphalapracayo vijñānavahnisāmarthyātkṣaṇamadhye pralayamupagacchatīti / gītāsu
children.translated_text: Just as cotton long accumulated — swan-down — is instantly reduced to ashes by the power of fire's radiance, similarly the entire accumulation of the fruits of <s>karma</s>, through the power of the fire of knowledge, undergoes dissolution in a moment. In the <s>Gītā</s>:
'Just as a blazing fire reduces firewood to ashes, O <s>Arjuna</s>,
so the fire of knowledge reduces all <s>karmas</s> to ashes.'

body.text: na kevalaṃ prākkṛtaṃ karma jñānaprasādādupalīyate yāvadidānīntanamapi karma jñāneddhayā dṛṣṭyā na phalopabhogāya paryavasyatītyāha
body.translated_text: Not only is previously performed <s>karma</s> dissolved through the grace of knowledge, but even present <s>karma</s>, through the vision empowered by knowledge, does not culminate in the experience of its fruit — he says:

children.text: jñānaprāptau kṛtamapi na phalāya tato 'sya janma katham /
children.translated_text: [Verse:] When knowledge has been attained, even <s>karma</s> performed [now] does not [lead to] fruit; how then could there be birth for him? Freed from the bond of birth, the sun of <s>Śiva</s> shines with its own rays. // 56 //
'even [<s>karma</s>] performed' —
whether good, bad, or otherwise,
'<s>karma</s>' —

children.text: kṛtrimapramātṛtābhimānābhāvānnānuguṇaphaladānāya pragalbhata iti karmaphalābhāvāttadupabhogayogyasya janmanaḥ kena prakāreṇa sattā syānna bhavedyoginaḥ punarjanmetyarthaḥ / nanu sa piṇḍapātātpunarna jāyate cettarhi kīdṛśaḥ syādityāha
children.translated_text: does not become bold enough to yield corresponding fruits, because there is no identification as a fabricated cognizer; therefore, in the absence of the fruit of <s>karma</s>, by what means could there be existence of a birth fit for experiencing that [fruit]? — the <s>yogī</s> would not have another birth — that is the meaning. But if after [receiving] alms-food he is no longer born, what would he be like? He says:
'freed from birth' —

children.text: ityādi / gato janmarūpasya bandhasya yogaḥ saṃbandho yasya sa evamiti prakṣīṇamohāvaraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: and so forth. He whose connection with bondage in the form of birth has departed — thus, whose veil of delusion has been destroyed,
'with his own rays' —
with the multitude of rays of consciousness, he,
'the sun of <s>Śiva</s>-nature, shines' —

children.text: sphurati na punastīrthāntaraparikalpito 'sya mokṣaḥ kutracitprāptiriti kevalaṃ māyādikañcukakṛtasaṃkocavināśātsvaśaktivikasvaratāmāpadyata iti // 56 //
children.translated_text: shines forth; but the <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) constructed by rival schools — as an arrival somewhere — is not his; rather, merely through the destruction of the contraction imposed by <s>Māyā</s> and the other sheaths, he attains the unfoldment of his own powers. // 56 //

body.translated_text: When the reflective awareness of the great Lord as one's own Self has fully matured,
On this very point, he states the reasoning:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] Just as a seed freed from husk, bran, and chaff does not produce a sprout, so too the Self, freed from <s>āṇava</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>kārma</s> [impurities], does not [produce] the sprout of worldly existence. // 57 //
Just as a rice-seed separated from the bran, husk, and chaff,
due to the absence of the essential causal complex consisting of bran etc. inherent to seeds, even though placed amid soil, water, and heat,
'does not' —
become a cause for the effect characterized as the production of a sprout;
'similarly' —
from the <s>āṇava</s> [impurity], which stands in the place of bran,
'<s>āṇava</s>' —

children.text: malena tuṣasthānīyena māyāmalena kiṃśārukasthānīyena kārmamalena ca
children.translated_text: from the <s>āṇava mala</s> (impurity of finitude), from the <s>māyā mala</s> (impurity of illusion) which stands in the place of husk, and from the <s>kārma mala</s> (impurity of action) which stands in the place of chaff,
'freed' —
separated,
'the Self' —
consciousness, due to the absence of the causal complex in the form of the three <s>malas</s> (impurities), does not again [produce]
'the sprout of worldly existence' —

children.text: saṃsāraprarohaṃ vidadhāti kevalaṃ viśvagatanānāpadārthasārthaprādurbhāvavināśavaicitryaṃ svātmani parāmṛśanmaheśvara eva bhavati // 57 //
children.translated_text: produces the growth of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) — merely reflecting within His own Self the variegated appearance and disappearance of the multitude of diverse objects pervading the universe — He is none other than the Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>). // 57 //

body.text: evaṃ jñānāgnidagdhakañcukabījasya jñānino na kiñcicchaṅkāsthānaṃ heyopādeyaṃ vetyata āha
body.translated_text: Thus, for the knower whose seed-sheaths have been burned by the fire of knowledge, there is no ground for apprehension, nothing to be rejected or accepted — therefore he says:

children.text: ātmajño na kutaścana bibheti sarvaṃ hi tasya nijarūpam /
children.translated_text: The knower of the Self fears nothing whatsoever, for everything is his own nature; /

children.text: naiva ca śocati yasmātparamārthe nāśitā nāsti // 58 //
children.translated_text: nor does he grieve, because in ultimate reality there is no destruction. // 58 //
is the knower of the Self (<s>ātmajña</s>) —
one who knows the absolute freedom of the Great Lord who is his own Self — he
fears nothing whatsoever;

children.text: na sa kasmādapi rājñaḥ śatroḥ prāṇibhyo vā bhayamādatte / kuta etadityāha
children.translated_text: he does not take fright from anything — from a king, an enemy, or living beings. Why is this? He says:
for everything is his own nature —
because
for him,
the knower of the non-duality of the Great Lord who is his own Self,
everything —
this entire universe, the mass of objects —
of his own [Self],
of his own Self whose sole body is the great light (<s>mahāprakāśa</s>), is indeed
the form,

children.text: ākāraḥ sarvatra prakāśānugamāditi prakāśa eva svātantryātsvaparātmanā prakāśate 'ta eva bhayasthānaṃ loke yatkiñcitpratibhāti tattasya tathaiva svāṅgakalpameva kathaṃ bhayajanakaṃ syādyaduta svātmano vyatiriktaḥ padārtho bhayaheturbhavetkaḥ punaḥ sarvataḥ paripūrṇasyāvadhibhūto bhinno yamādirasti yasmājjñānyapahastitadehātmamānitvo 'pi bibhiyāditi sarvatra nijarūpopalabdheḥ saṃsārasthito 'pyekako vigalitasvaparavibhāgatayā niḥśaṅkaṃ vicaratyeva / yathoktaṃ parameṣṭhipādaiḥ
children.translated_text: the appearance — because light pervades everywhere, light itself, by its own freedom, shines as both self and other. Therefore, whatever appears in the world as a ground for fear — that, being like his own limb, how could it cause fear? For what object, separate from his own Self, could be a cause of fear? And for one who is completely full on all sides, what delimited, separate entity such as <s>Yama</s> (Death) and the like exists, from which the knower, even though freed from identification with the body as the Self, might fear? Thus, because his own nature is apprehended everywhere, even while dwelling in <s>saṃsāra</s>, he alone, with the distinction between self and other dissolved, wanders without any apprehension. As stated by the Supreme Lord [<s>Utpaladeva</s>]:

body.translated_text: He who

children.translated_text: 'He who sees this entire sphere of objects without conceptual construction, O Lord, as having your form — /
in a world completely filled with his own Self alone, whence could there be fear for him who is eternally happy?' //

body.translated_text: And the author of the treatise [<s>Ādiśeṣa</s>] also [says]:

children.translated_text: '"I am alone" — with this, a person in <s>saṃsāra</s> is afflicted by the emotion of terror and daring. /
'"I am alone" — who else is there for me? — thus established, he is freed from fear.' //
Nor does he grieve —
and so forth. Nor does the knower of the Self
grieve

children.text: yathā dhanadārādikaṃ mama naṣṭaṃ rikto 'smi vyādhinākrānto 'haṃ mriye vetyādi yato vyākhyātena krameṇa
children.translated_text: — thinking 'my wealth and wife and so on are lost,' 'I am destitute,' 'I am seized by illness,' 'I am dying,' and so on — because, in the manner explained,
in ultimate reality,
in the real substance whose nature is consciousness, in the inward-facing pure subject,
there is no destruction —

children.text: kṣayadharmitvaṃ na vidyate / sarvaṃ hyabhimānasāraṃ kāryatvena pratibhāsamānamidantāvācchinnamutpadyate kṣīyate ca na punaḥ saṃvinmayasyātmano 'hantāsārasyākṛtrimasya svatantrasya kāryonmukhaprayatnānupalabdheḥ / na caitāvatā svarūpavipralopaḥ syāditi vimṛśato yogino dehasthasyāpi taddhetukaḥ śokādyāvirbhāvaḥ svarūpācchādakatvena na bhavediti // 58 //
children.translated_text: there is no quality of perishability. For everything that appears as an effect, whose essence is [mere] identification, delimited by objectivity, arises and perishes — but for the Self, whose essence is consciousness, whose core is I-ness, which is natural and independent, no effort directed toward becoming an effect is found. And this does not result in the destruction of its own nature — thus, for the yogin who reflects in this way, even while embodied, the arising of grief and the like caused by the body would not occur as a concealment of his own nature. // 58 //

body.translated_text: And furthermore:
He now demonstrates that for this knower, through the firmness of his cultivation of the nature of the Great Lord who is his own Self, there is no defect such as a sense of incompleteness:

children.translated_text: From the treasure-house of the heart, exceedingly secret, wherein the wealth of supreme reality has sprouted — /
with the awareness 'I alone am all,' in the state of the Great Lord, what misfortune? for whom? // 59 //
Exceedingly secret —
concealed to the highest degree —
the heart itself is the treasure-house (<s>gañja</s>),
— the storehouse whose nature is the resting-place of all ultimate realities in their essential nature. In that [heart], he who has sprouted through supremely intense conviction —
the supreme reality (<s>paramārtha</s>),

children.text: sadgurūpadiṣṭaḥ svātmajñānasatattvaḥ sa eva sarvavibhūtihetutvādratnasaṃcaya iva
children.translated_text: the true knowledge of one's own Self as instructed by the true <s>Guru</s> — that itself, being the cause of all powers, is like a hoard of jewels —
a hoard of jewels.
By that reason,
'I alone' (<s>ahameva</s>) —
meaning 'I am all this' — the full [Self-awareness] that has manifested, characterized by resting in the supreme I-consciousness (<s>parāhantā</s>) —
the state of the Great Lord (<s>maheśvarabhāva</s>),
the self-luminous freedom of one's own Self even for an embodied being — when that is established,
what
— what wretched —
misfortune

children.text: daridrabhāvastadupalakṣito vā kaścitkṛtrimo vibhūtyādyatiśayaḥ syāt / ābhāsasārā hi sarve padārthā yadaivābhāsante tadaiva yoginaḥ svātmakalpāḥ santaḥ kathamutkarṣāpakarṣādau pragalbhanta iti na kiñciddaurgatyādikaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: — a state of poverty, or any artificial distinction of special powers and the like marked by it — could there be? For all objects are essentially appearances; the very moment they appear, for the yogin they are like his own limbs — how could they instigate any rise or fall? Thus there would be no misfortune or the like.
For whom? —

children.text: veti ko vāsyā durgateḥ samāśrayo dehādyātmābhimānino hyasyā durgateḥ samāśrayā bhavantu yataste vyatiriktasyaiṣaṇīyasya prāptyeśvarāstadapahārādriktā iti / yaḥ punarakṛtrimāhantāpratyavamarśaparamārtho jñānī sarvamasmītyavyatiriktenaiṣaṇīyena maheśvaraḥ sa kathaṃ vyatiriktaprāptyaprāptyabhāvāddaurgatyāderbhājanaṃ syādata eva gañjaśabdasya ratnasaṃcayaśabdasyeśvaraśabdasya ca hṛdayaprarūḍhaparamārtho mahānityakṛtrimārthavācakāni viśeṣaṇānyupapāditāni // 59 //
children.translated_text: meaning: and who would be the locus of this misfortune? Let those who identify the body and the like as the Self be the locus of this misfortune, for they, being masters of attaining desirable things that are separate [from themselves], become destitute when those are taken away. But the knower whose supreme reality is the reflective awareness of natural I-ness, who is the Great Lord by virtue of [the cognition] 'I am all,' with nothing desirable that is separate — how could he, in the absence of the attainment or non-attainment of anything separate, be a vessel for misfortune and the like? Therefore, the epithets 'treasure-house,' 'hoard of jewels,' and 'Lord' qualifying 'the supreme reality sprouted in the heart' are shown to express the great, eternal, and natural meaning. // 59 //

body.translated_text: Now he states the nature of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>):

children.text: mokṣasya naiva kiñciddhāmāsti na cāpi gamanamanyatra /
children.translated_text: Liberation has absolutely no abode, nor is there any going elsewhere; /
liberation is the splitting of the knot of ignorance, the manifestation of one's own powers. // 60 //
Of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>),
— of <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute aloneness), whose essence is the self-awareness (<s>camatkāra</s>) of the supreme I-consciousness —
an abode (<s>dhāma</s>),

children.text: vyatiriktaṃ sthānaṃ na vidyata eva deśakālākārāvacchedābhāvādata eva
children.translated_text: a separate place, does not exist at all, because there is no delimitation by space, time, or form; and therefore
nor going elsewhere —
