going,

children.text: layo mokṣo yathā bhedavādināṃ matenotkrāntyā cakrādhārādibhedanādūrdhvaṃ dvādaśānte laya eṣaiva muktiriti / yaduktam
children.translated_text: dissolution, is [not the nature of] liberation — as the dualists hold: that liberation consists in dissolution upward, through the <s>cakrādhāra</s> and other [centers], at the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger-breadths above the head), through ascent. As has been said:
'When <s>Śiva</s>'s being is all-pervading, what is the purpose of ascent? /

children.text: avyāpini pare tattve hyutkrāntyā kiṃ prayojanam //
children.translated_text: And if the Supreme Principle were not all-pervading, what would be the purpose of ascent?' //

body.text: iti / evaṃvidhāpyanye tīrthāntaraparikalpitā bahavo mokṣabhedāḥ santi te pratanyamānā granthagauravabhayamānayantīti neha pratanyanta iti sarvatra dvaitamalasya saṃbhavādamokṣe mokṣalipsā mokṣābhāsa eva / kiṃ punarmokṣalakṣaṇamityāha

children.translated_text: Ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) —
and so forth.
Ignorance —

children.text: akhyātijanita ātmanyanātmābhimānapūrvo 'nātmani dehādāvātmābhimānalakṣaṇo mohaḥ sa eva pūrṇasvarūpasaṃkocadāyitvādgranthiriva
children.translated_text: the delusion (<s>moha</s>) born of non-manifestation (<s>akhyāti</s>), preceded by the false identification of the non-Self as the Self — namely, the false identification of the body and the like, which are not the Self, as the Self — that itself, because it causes the contraction of the full essential nature, is like a knot —
the knot (<s>granthi</s>);
the bondage constituted by the identification of the body and the like as [the Self], through which one's own [nature], characterized by freedom and pervasiveness, is bound — of that [knot],
the splitting (<s>bhid</s>),
the breaking — the tearing apart of the knot characterized by identification with the body and the like, through the firmness of cultivation of one's own full Self-nature and freedom; by that cause,
by one's own powers (<s>svaśakti</s>),
by the qualities characterized as the freedom of one's own Self,
the manifestation (<s>abhivyaktatā</s>),
the blossoming of the powers of one's own Self — this itself is the unsurpassable
liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).

children.text: iti / ayamāśayo yathā sahajanityavyāpakatvādidharmayuktamākāśamapi ghaṭādibhittibandhasaṃkucitaṃ tata eva tadevāvyāpakatvādidharmayuktaṃ ghaṭākāśamityucyata ākāśādbhinnamiva prathate punarapi ghaṭādibhittikṛtasaṃkocabhaṅgāttadeva ghaṭādyākāśaṃ tadaiva vyāpakatvādidharmayuktaṃ syānna punastasya ghaṭādibhaṅgānnūtanaḥ kaściddharmāvirbhāva āyātīti / tathaiva dehādyabhimānakṛtasaṃkocasaṃkucitaṃ caitanyaṃ baddhamivetyucyate tadeva punaḥ svasvarūpajñānābhivyakterdehādipramātṛtābandhasaṃkṣayātsvaśaktivivekavikasvaraṃ muktamivetyabhimānamātrasārau parimitapramātrapekṣayā bandhamaukṣau na punaḥ paramārthe saṃvittattva evaṃ kiñcitsaṃbhavatīti / tasmānmuktau nūtanaṃ na kiñcitsādhyate nijameva svarūpaṃ prathate / etadeva viṣṇudharmeṣvapyuktam
children.translated_text: The purport is this: just as space, though possessing natural, eternal, pervasive, and other qualities, when contracted by the walls of a pot and the like — that very [space], endowed with non-pervasiveness and other qualities, is called 'pot-space' and appears as if different from [universal] space; but when the contraction caused by the walls of the pot and the like is broken, that very pot-space at that very moment becomes endowed with pervasiveness and other qualities — no new quality whatsoever arises from the breaking of the pot and the like. In the same way, consciousness, contracted by the contraction caused by identification with the body and the like, is said to be 'as if bound'; that very [consciousness], through the manifestation of knowledge of its own nature, through the destruction of the bondage of identification with the body and the like as the subject, blossoming with the discernment of its own powers, is 'as if liberated.' Thus bondage and liberation, being essentially mere conception, are relative to the limited subject — but in ultimate reality, in the consciousness-principle, nothing of this sort occurs. Therefore, in liberation nothing new is accomplished — one's own nature simply manifests. This very thing is stated in the <s>Viṣṇudharmas</s> also:

body.translated_text: There are many such varieties of liberation conceived by other schools — to elaborate on them would cause the fear of the text becoming unwieldy, so they are not elaborated here. Since in all of them the impurity of duality is possible, the desire for liberation in the absence of [true] liberation is merely an appearance of liberation. What then is the definition of liberation? He says:

children.translated_text: 'Just as by digging a well, the water is not created; /
what already exists is merely brought to manifestation — how could existence come from non-existence?' //

children.text: bhinne dṛtau yathā vāyurnaivānyaḥ saha vāyunā /
children.translated_text: 'Just as when a leather bag is torn, the air within is not other than the [outer] air; /
so too the Self, when the bonds of merit and demerit are exhausted, [unites] with <s>Brahman</s>.' //

body.text: evaṃ prakṣīṇājñānabandho jñānī parānugrahārthaṃ śarīramapi dhārayanmukta ityāvedayati
body.translated_text: Thus, the knower whose bondage of ignorance has been destroyed, even while maintaining the body for the sake of benefiting others, is announced as liberated:

children.translated_text: With the knot of ignorance split, with doubt gone, with error overcome, /
with merit and demerit exhausted — even while connected with the body, he is liberated. // 61 //
liberated (<s>mukta</s>),

children.text: vikasvaraśaktirbhavet / nanu vigrahayoga eva bandhaḥ kathaṃ tatsaṃbandhe 'pyasau muktaḥ syādityāha
children.translated_text: one whose powers have blossomed. But if the connection with the body is itself bondage, how can he be liberated while still connected with it? He says:
Split (<s>bhinna</s>) —

children.text: ityādi / bhinno vidārito 'jñānarūpo granthirapūrṇatvakhyātisamuttho dehādyabhimānarūpo bandho yena sa evam / tathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. One for whom the knot in the form of ignorance — the bondage in the form of identification with the body and the like, arising from the non-manifestation of fullness — has been split and torn apart — he is thus described. Likewise,
with doubt gone —
by this very reason, one whose doubts have been destroyed.
Overcome (<s>parākṛta</s>) —
vanquished, through the attainment of supreme non-dual knowledge,
is error (<s>bhrānti</s>) —

children.text: dvayarūpo bhramo yena sa tatheti / evaṃ pariśīlanena prakṣīṇāni puṇyāpuṇyāni vigalitasaṃskārāṇi dehātmamānitvābhāvāddharmādharmāṇi yasya sa evaṃvidha iti / anena
children.translated_text: the delusion of the form of duality — one for whom this is so is thus described. Thus, through [spiritual] cultivation, the merit and demerit whose impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) have dissolved — the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> that cease due to the absence of identification with the body as the Self — one for whom these have been exhausted is thus described. By this,
it is established that ignorance alone is bondage;

children.text: iti pratipāditam / tacca vigrahayoge 'pi yasya prakṣīṇaṃ sa tadaiva jīvanneva mukto na punaḥ śarīrayogo bandhastadapagamo muktiriti kiṃ tu dehapātātpūrṇo mokṣa iti // 61 //
children.translated_text: and when that [ignorance] is exhausted even while connected with the body, one is liberated while still alive (<s>jīvanmukta</s>) — not that the connection with the body is bondage and its removal is liberation; rather, complete liberation [follows] upon the fall of the body. // 61 //

body.translated_text: Even while connected with the body, due to the absence of identification with the body and the like through the discernment of knowledge of one's own Self, though still living, he is

body.text: jīvanmuktasya karmahetau śarīre sthite 'pi śarīrayātrāmātrārthaṃ jñāneddhaṃ kurvāṇasya karma na phalāya tasya bhavatītyatropapattimāha
body.translated_text: For the one liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>), even though the body — the cause of [past] <s>karma</s> — persists, the <s>karma</s> performed merely for the sustenance of the body, being kindled by knowledge, does not produce results — here he states the reasoning:

children.translated_text: Just as a seed burned by fire becomes incapable of sprouting, /
so too <s>karma</s> burned by the fire of knowledge does not give rise to birth. // 62 //

body.text: vahninirbhṛṣṭaṃ śālibījaṃ kṣitisalilātapamadhyavartyapi sāmagrīvaikalyādyathāṅkurādijanane 'śaktatāṃ yāti tathaiva

children.translated_text: [<s>karma</s>] burned by the fire of knowledge —
scorched by the blaze of supreme non-dual awareness —
<s>karma</s>,

children.text: yathāhamevetthaṃ viśvātmanā sphurāmītyevaṃrūpeṇa dehādyātmamānitvahānerheyopādeyabuddhiparityāgena yatkiñcicchubhāśubhaṃ karma kriyamāṇaṃ taddagdhavīryaṃ na punarjñāninaḥ piṇḍapātādanantaraṃ janmaphalapradam
children.translated_text: — since 'I alone shine forth thus as the universal Self' — through such [awareness], through the abandonment of the notion of things to be rejected and accepted consequent upon the loss of identification with the body and the like as the Self, whatever good or bad <s>karma</s> is being performed — that, its potency being burned, does not produce the fruit of [another] birth for the knower after the fall of the body —
it does not become

children.text: dehanirmāṇahetuḥ saṃpadyate dagdhaṃ bījamivāṅkure / tasmānna sarvāhaṃbhāvarūpāyāścitiśakteraphalābhisaṃdhānatayā kṛtaṃ karma bhūyo janma dātuṃ prabhavatīti // 62 //
children.translated_text: the cause of the construction of a body, like a burned seed [unable to produce] a sprout. Therefore, <s>karma</s> performed without attachment to results by the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>), whose nature is the universal I-ness, is unable to give another birth. // 62 //

body.translated_text: A rice seed roasted by fire, even though situated amidst earth, water, and sunlight, due to the deficiency of the requisite conditions, becomes incapable of producing a sprout and so on; in the same way,

body.text: evaṃ punarvikasvarāpi citiśaktiḥ kathaṅkāraṃ dehavatī syādityāha
body.translated_text: Thus, even though the power of consciousness has blossomed, how does it come to be embodied? He says:

children.translated_text: Due to limited understanding, through the impression of the future body suitable to [past] <s>karma</s>, /
the power of consciousness becomes contracted — upon the destruction of this body, it manifests accordingly. // 63 //
due to limited understanding —
the resolve, clouded by desire preceded by the impression of identification with the body and the like, born of non-manifestation, by which
<s>karma</s> [is performed] —

children.text: yathāhamaśvamedhena yakṣya ihāmutra ca sukhī bhūyāsaṃ mā kadācana duḥkhyahaṃ bhūyāsamamunā karmaṇā vaindraṃ padaṃ prāpnuyāmityevaṃ vāsanāviśiṣṭasya karturevamanuguṇaṃ karma tasya manovāsanālabdhaprarūḍheḥ karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: such as: 'By the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) I shall offer sacrifice and be happy in this world and the next,' 'May I never be unhappy,' 'By this <s>karma</s> may I attain the rank of <s>Indra</s>' — thus, for the agent endowed with such impressions, the <s>karma</s> corresponding to him, having sprouted through the impressions of the mind — of that <s>karma</s>,
suitable —
fit for experiencing the fruit corresponding to that [<s>karma</s>] —
the future body,

the body that will come into being in the future, when the entitlement to the body that is the experiencer of the fruit of <s>karma</s> already set in motion (<s>prārabdha</s>) is exhausted — of that [future body], the
impression (<s>bhāvanā</s>),

children.text: amunāśvamedhādikarmaṇā sāmrājyādyāpnuyāmityabhimatakarmaphalavāsanādhirūḍhistayā karmocitabhāvidehabhāvanayeyaṃ sarvataḥ pūrṇāpi citiśaktirāṇavamāyīyamalamūlena kārmamalenāghrātā

becomes contracted,
though all-pervading, like pot-space, delimited by the impression of the body that is the experiencer of the fruit corresponding to <s>karma</s> — having become so,
upon the destruction of this body, it manifests accordingly —
thus.
of this
commenced <s>karma</s> and its fruit, the body which is the enjoyer,
that body,
upon the exhaustion of its enjoyment, its
destruction,
death — upon the destruction of that body,
consciousness (<s>citi</s>)
with its arisen <s>karmic</s> impressions
becomes such

children.text: yenāśayena pūrvakarmaphalamupārjitaṃ tatkarmaphalabhoktā yo dehastadvatī saṃpadyate yadvaśāccitirapi svarganarakādibhogabhājanaṃ syāt / tasmāccharīrībhūtvā parimitaphalalaulyādyatkṛtaṃ karma tatphalabhoktṛ janma dātumavaśyaṃ prabhavati / yatpunaraśarīrībhūtvā sarvaṃ brahmāsmīti saṃvidrūpatayā kṛtaṃ tadvāsanāprarohānāsādanātkathaṃ vyāpinyāścitiśakterjanmane syāditi tātparyārthaḥ // 63 //
children.translated_text: that by whatever disposition the fruit of previous <s>karma</s> was earned, the body that is the enjoyer of that <s>karmic</s> fruit takes shape accordingly, and by its force consciousness too becomes a vessel for the enjoyment of heaven, hell, and so forth. Therefore, having become embodied, the <s>karma</s> performed out of greed for limited results necessarily has the power to grant a birth suited to enjoy its fruit. But that which is done without becoming embodied, in the form of consciousness as 'I am all, I am <s>Brahman</s>' — since it does not give rise to the sprouting of <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), how could it lead to a birth for the all-pervading power of consciousness? This is the purport. (63)

body.translated_text: Because

body.text: evamanātmatayā samucitaṃ karma saṃsaraṇāya pramāturbhavatīti cettarhyātmasvarūpaṃ vaktavyaṃ yena saṃsārī na syāditi pratipāditamapi śiṣyajanahṛdayaṅgamīkartuṃ punaḥ kathayati
body.translated_text: If thus <s>karma</s> performed with the sense of not-Self leads to <s>saṃsāra</s> for the subject, then the true nature of the Self should be stated, by which one would not be a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrant) — having already established this, he states it again to make it penetrate the hearts of the disciples:

children.translated_text: "If one should realize one's Self as stainless awareness, consisting of the knower and doer who transcends all,"
"all-pervading, whose form is the light that has no setting or rising, whose will is truth, (64)"
"free from the divisions of space, time, and form, eternal, imperishable, the Lord, utterly complete,"
"the sole agent of the manifestation and dissolution of the host of manifold powers, (65)"
"expert in the acts of creation and so forth, and of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> —"

children.text: kathamiva saṃsārī syādvitatasya kutaḥ kva vā saraṇam // 66 //
children.translated_text: "how could he be a transmigrant? For one who is all-pervading, whence and where could there be any wandering? (66)"
If indeed
a subject whose heart has been pierced by the descent of the supreme power (<s>śaktipāta</s>), having cast down the identification with the body and other limited subjectivity,
should realize his own Self as of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>,
should know it as a compact mass of consciousness and bliss — he, having recognized his own nature as the great Lord,
how could
— in what manner —
he be a transmigrant,

children.text: saṃsaraṇaśīlo bhavenna syāditi yāvadyataścidacidrūpapuryaṣṭakātmā kārmamalasaṃbandhena saṃsarati yaḥ punaścidekamūrtiḥ śivamayaḥ prakṣīṇāṇavādimalakañcukaḥ sa kathaṃ saṃsārīti tātparyam / nanu cidekamūrtiḥ syātsaṃsārī ca bhavediti kiṃ duṣyedityevamāśaṅkyāha
children.translated_text: be of the nature of one who wanders? He could not, inasmuch as one who has a Self consisting of the subtle body, which is of the nature of consciousness and non-consciousness, wanders through the connection with <s>karmic</s> impurity; but one whose sole form is consciousness, who is of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, whose <s>āṇava</s> and other impurities and limiting coverings have been exhausted — how could he be a transmigrant? This is the purport. But if he were of the sole form of consciousness, could he not still be a transmigrant? — anticipating this objection, he says:
"All-pervading"
and so forth.
"For one who is all-pervading" —
for a subject whose space, time, and form are undelimited, who is complete due to the exhaustion of the self-made <s>vāsanās</s> rooted in the identification with body and so forth,
"whence could there be wandering?"

children.text: sarvavyāpitvāttadatiriktaṃ kimasti yadvastvapekṣya tato viśliṣṭo 'nyatra bhinne saṃsaraṇaṃ gamanaṃ kuryādyato dehādipramātṛtābhimānāvacchinnasya kilāpādānādhikaraṇādikārakasaṃbhavo yaḥ punaścidekaghano brahmabhūto 'navacchinnadeśakālaḥ pramātā tasya saṃsaraṇe vācoyuktirapi na bhavediti / kīdṛśaṃ śivarūpamātmānaṃ vibudhyetetyāha
children.translated_text: Since he is all-pervading, what other thing exists apart from him, in dependence upon which, being separated from it, he could make a journey — a wandering — to somewhere else, to something different? For one delimited by the identification with body and other limited subjectivity, there is indeed the possibility of the grammatical cases of material cause, locus, and so forth; but for one who is a compact mass of consciousness, who has become <s>Brahman</s>, whose space and time are undelimited — for him, even the verbal expression of transmigration would not apply. What kind of <s>Śiva</s>-nature does he recognize in his Self? He says:
"Stainless awareness"

children.text: ityādi / apagata āṇavādimalapracayo yasya tamata eva vaimalyāt

awareness (<s>bodha</s>)
— pure consciousness. Likewise,

one whose will is
ultimate,
whose intentions

eternal (<s>dhruva</s>),
immutable,

the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>),

utterly complete (<s>suparipūrṇa</s>),
thoroughly without want. Then,
of the many

children.translated_text: abundant hosts of powers — arisen from the mass of words (<s>śabdarāśi</s>), presided over by <s>Brāhmī</s> and other powers, consisting of the hosts of powers of pots, cloths, and so forth — he is autonomous in the process of their dissolution and arising. And further,
"expert in the acts of creation and so forth"
— highly skilled,
a creator (<s>vedhasa</s>),

children.text:
vidhātāramityevamādiviśeṣaṇaiḥ
sarvataḥ paripūrṇaṃ svātmamaheśvaraṃ jānāno yatkiñcidapi kurvāṇo dagdhakarmabījo na punaḥ saṃsārabhāgjīvanneva vimukto bhavediti yāvat // 64 // 65 // 66 //
children.translated_text: a maker — one who, by such qualifications, knowing his own Self as the great Lord, complete in every respect, even while performing any action whatsoever, his seed of <s>karma</s> being burnt, would never again be subject to <s>saṃsāra</s>, but would be liberated even while living. (64) (65) (66)

body.text: evaṃ svātmapratyavamarśopapattyā jñāninā vigalitakarmaphalābhilāṣeṇa kṛtamapi karma na phalāyetyāvedayansvānubhavasiddhaṃ lokadṛṣṭāntamāha
body.translated_text: Thus, even the action performed by a <s>jñānin</s> (knower), whose desire for the fruit of action has dissolved through the practice of Self-recognition, does not lead to fruit — revealing this, he presents an example established by direct experience and seen in the world:

children.text: iti yuktibhirapi siddhaṃ yatkarma jñānino na saphalaṃ tat /
children.translated_text: "Thus it is established even by reasoning that the action of a knower is not fruitful."

children.text: na mamedamapi tu tasyeti dārḍhyato nahi phalaṃ loke // 67 //
children.translated_text: "'This is not mine, but his' — due to firmness in this conviction, there is no fruit in the world. (67)"

body.text: ahameva cidghanaḥ svatantraḥ sarvapramātrantaratamatvena sarvakarmakārī nāhaṃ vā kartā pārameśvarī svātantryaśaktiritthaṃ karotīti mama śuddhacaitanyarūpasyaitāvatā kimāyātam

children.translated_text: "by these reasonings,"

by the proofs consisting of the previously established true nature, for a subject who knows his own Self as thus explained — due to the absence of identification with body and so forth in both ways, and therefore being devoid of anything to be rejected or accepted —
"whatever action has been accomplished,"
even though completed and performed,
"is not fruitful,"

children.text: na tatphalena yujyate tasyātmajñāninaḥ pratipāditavadubhayathā kṛtrimatvābhāvātkṛtamapi karma kutra phalena yogaṃ kuryāddehādipramātṛtābhimānasvabhāvāśrayābhāvānna kutraciditi yāvat / kṛtasya karmaṇo yā pramātuḥ phalābhimānarūḍhireṣa evāśrayo jñāninastvabhimānābhāvātsvasminrūpa eva prakṣīṇaṃ karma na phalena saṃbadhyata iti / nanvabhimānādeva karma phalena yujyata iti kutra yathetyāha
children.translated_text: it does not join with its fruit for that Self-knower, as previously explained — in both ways, due to the absence of artificiality. Even action that has been performed — where could it join with its fruit? Due to the absence of a basis in the form of identification with body and other limited subjectivity — nowhere. The resting place for the fruit of performed action is the subject's firm identification with its result; but for a <s>jñānin</s>, due to the absence of identification, the <s>karma</s> consumed in his own true nature does not connect with its fruit. But if <s>karma</s> joins with fruit precisely through identification, then where is this seen? He says:
"'This is not mine, but'"
and so forth. This is seen and not unprecedented — for example:
"'This is not mine,'"
the sacrificial and other ritual action,
"'but his,'"
of some person of means, the sacrificer,
thus —
with this understanding, even sacrificial and other ritual action that has been performed,
in the world,

children.text:
mūlyārthitayā phalābhimānābhāvānna yatastatkarma pāralaukikena phalena yuktaṃ kalpate / tathā hi yajanti yājakā yajate yajamāna iti nyāyena yajatāmṛtvijāṃ yajñakarma svayaṃ kṛtavatāmapīdamaśvamedhādikaṃ yajñakarma nāsmākaṃ kiñcidapi tu dīkṣitasya puṇyavato vayaṃ kileha yajñakarmāṇi niyamitamūlyamātrārthino 'tra na kecanaiva yajamānaḥ punaramunā karmaṇā svargādiphalabhāgapīti teṣāṃ karmaphalābhimānābhāvānna svayaṃ kṛtamapi karma tadīyena svargādinā phalena yujyate yajamānastu tatra yajñakarma svayamakurvāṇa ṛtviṅnirvartyakarmamukhaprekṣyapi mamedamaśvamedhādikaṃ yajñakarma madīyena dhanenāmyṛtvijaḥ karmaṇi pravṛttā iti mamaiva svargādiphalaṃ dehapātādavaśyaṃbhāvītyakurvāṇasyāpi yathā samīhitakarmaphalābhimānadārḍhyāttattasya karma phalena yujyate / ata eva kartrabhiprāye kriyāphala iti dīkṣitātkarturyajate yajamāna ityātmanepadaṃ kartranabhiprāye tu parasmaipadaṃ yajanti yājakā iti / iyānmahimā durlaṅghyo vikalpasvātantryasya yatsvayaṃ kṛtamapi karma phalābhimānābhāvāttatphalena
na yujyate 'nyaiḥ kṛtamapi karma
children.translated_text: since there is no identification with the fruit due to being motivated only by wages, that action is not regarded as endowed with other-worldly fruit. For according to the principle 'the priests sacrifice, the sacrificer sacrifices,' even for the officiating priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) who have themselves performed the sacrificial action such as the horse-sacrifice and so forth — 'this sacrificial action is not at all ours, but belongs to the consecrated man of merit; we here in this sacrificial action desire only the stipulated wages, we have nothing further in it; rather, the sacrificer partakes of the fruit of heaven and so forth through this action' — since they have no identification with the fruit of the action, even action they themselves performed does not join with the fruit of heaven and so forth that belongs to him. But the sacrificer, even though he himself does not perform the sacrificial action, watching the action carried out by the priests with the thought 'this horse-sacrifice and other sacrificial action is mine; by my wealth the priests are engaged in the action; therefore the fruit of heaven and so forth will certainly be mine after death' — even though not performing the action himself, due to the firmness of identification with the desired fruit of the action, that action joins with its fruit for him. For this very reason, according to the rule 'the fruit of action belongs to the intended agent,' the middle voice (<s>ātmanepada</s>) 'the sacrificer sacrifices' is used from the consecrated agent; but for an unintended agent, the active voice (<s>parasmaipada</s>) 'the priests sacrifice' is used. Such is the insuperable glory of the freedom of conceptual thought: that even action performed by oneself, due to the absence of identification with the fruit, does not join with that fruit; while action performed by others,
"'this is mine'"

children.text: ityabhimānadārḍhyātphalayuktaṃ syāttasmādṛtvigvyāpāravatkriyamāṇaṃ yoginā karma phalābhimānābhāvānna tatsaphalaṃ bhavediti // 67 //
children.translated_text: — due to the firmness of identification, would be endowed with fruit. Therefore, just like the function of the officiating priests, the action performed by the <s>yogin</s>, due to the absence of identification with the fruit, would not be fruitful. (67)

body.translated_text: "I alone am the compact mass of consciousness, autonomous, the doer of all actions as the innermost of all subjects; or rather, I am not the doer — the supreme power of autonomy acts in this way. What has all this brought to me, whose form is pure consciousness?" —
Thus, the <s>jñānin</s> (knower), whose intellect has cast off the stain of distinguishing what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted in all actions, becomes illuminated — he says:

children.translated_text: "Thus, the awakened one, by the wind of contemplation, offering all conceptual thoughts"
"into the fire of the Self's light when it is ablaze, becomes one whose nature is light. (68)"
"Thus" —
by the previously explained method, the
contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>)

children.text: ahameva caitanyamaheśvaraḥ sarvātmanā sarvadaivaṃ sphurāmīti yātmani vimarśarūḍhiḥ saiva śanaiḥ prasarantī
children.translated_text: 'I alone am the great Lord of consciousness; in every way, at all times, I thus pulsate' — this firm reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) in the Self, itself gradually expanding, is the
wind (<s>samīraṇa</s>),
like a breeze — by that, the <s>jñānin</s>,
awakened,
like a fire covered by ashes and awakened by a breeze,
"all conceptual thoughts" —

children.text: paśurasmi karmabandhabaddho deharūpī mamedaṃ putradārādyamunā karmaṇā svargo nirayo vā bhaviṣyatītyādisarvāḥ kalpanā ahamevedaṃ sarvamiti parāmarśaśeṣībhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: 'I am a bound soul, I am fettered by <s>karmic</s> bondage, I am of the nature of a body, this son, wife, and so forth are mine, by this action heaven or hell will result' — all such conceptualizations, having become residues of the awareness 'I am indeed all this,'
"in the fire of the Self's light,"
in the fire of consciousness,
"when it is ablaze,"
in the essence of the wonder of supreme I-consciousness,
"offering,"
surrendering them through entry into the form of non-conceptual awareness, he
"becomes one whose nature is light" —

upon the exhaustion of the fuel of conceptual thoughts that are to be burnt, he becomes the fire of consciousness itself in the form of the burner — he remains as one body with the supreme subject. (68)

body.text: evaṃ vyākhyātena prakāreṇa yaḥ prakṛṣṭajñānayogābhyāsarataḥ sa śeṣavartanayā kathaṃ kālamativāhayatītyāha
body.translated_text: Thus, by the explained method, one who is devoted to the practice of advanced knowledge-<s>yoga</s> — how does he pass his remaining time through residual activity? He says:

children.translated_text: "Eating this or that, covered by whatever, peaceful,"
"dwelling wherever, the Self of all beings, he is liberated. (69)"
eating it,

children.text: camatkurvanna punarniyamenedaṃ pavitramidamapavitramidaṃ kadannamidaṃ miṣṭānnamiti heyopādeyakalpanāvirahādayatnenāpatitaṃ yadapi tadapi samāharan / tathā
children.translated_text: relishing it — but not with the rule that 'this is pure, this is impure, this is bad food, this is fine food' — due to the absence of conceptualizations of what is to be rejected or accepted, he also gathers whatever has come without effort. Likewise,
"covered by whatever" —

children.text: ityādi / kanthayā carmaṇā valkalena vā tūlapaṭādinā divyātmavastrairvā samācchādita ityubhayathotkarṣāpakarṣābhāvāccharīrācchādanārthakriyārthī bhūtvā nāpi kiñciddveṣṭi nāpi stautīti / kathametadyataḥ saḥ
children.translated_text: and so forth. Whether covered by a patched garment, by a skin, by bark-cloth, by cotton or silk fabrics, or by divine garments of the Self — in both ways, since there is no distinction of superiority or inferiority, desiring only to fulfill the purpose of covering the body, he neither despises anything nor praises anything. How is this? Because he is
"peaceful" —
one who has transcended the conceptualizations of pleasure, pain, and so forth. Likewise,
"dwelling wherever" —
in whatever

children.text: yādṛśe tādṛśe sthāne svapariśrayamātrārthī na punastasya kṣetrāyatanatīrthādi pavitratvātsvīkāryaṃ bhavati nāpi śmaśānaśvapacasadanādyapavitratvātparihāryaṃ syādayatnena yadyatsthānamāpatitaṃ tattadadhivasati pavitrāpavitrakalpanākalaṅkavirahāt /
children.translated_text: kind of place, desiring only shelter for himself — neither accepting a place as worthy because of its being a sacred field, temple, or <s>tīrtha</s> (pilgrimage site), nor avoiding it as unworthy because of its being a cremation ground, an outcaste's dwelling, and so forth — he inhabits whatever place comes to him without effort, due to the absence of the stain of conceptualizing pure and impure.
"He is liberated" —
even so, through his residual activity, engaged in bestowing grace upon others, passing his time,
he is liberated,

children.text: paramaśivībhavati / uktaṃ ca yena kenacidācchanno yena kenacidāśitaḥ / yatra kvacana śāyī yastaṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ //
children.translated_text: he becomes one with supreme <s>Śiva</s>. As it is said: 'He who is covered by whatever, fed by whatever, sleeping wherever — the gods know him as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.'

body.translated_text: Whatever object has fallen before him that is not unfit for eating,
And in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> also:

children.translated_text: "With no fixed rule as to what fruit, food, or drink to consume, with place and time distributed by the arrangement of providence,"
"this vow of the python, a joy to the heart, unserved by the miserly — this I practice purely."
"The Self of all beings" —

children.text: iti / yataḥ sa jñānī sarvabhūtātmā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmātmā sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni tasyātmeti kṛtvā na kiñcidbandhakatayā bhavati sarvaṃ vimuktaye 'sya saṃpadyata iti // 69 //
children.translated_text: since that <s>jñānin</s> is the Self of all beings — the Self of all beings, and all beings are his Self — therefore nothing exists as a cause of bondage; everything conduces to his liberation. (69)

body.translated_text: How even while acting thus does the <s>jñānin</s> become liberated? He says:
Nor is there any possibility of merit or demerit for one of such a nature, who is free from identification, even while performing any action — he says:

children.translated_text: "Even if he performs hundreds of thousands of horse-sacrifices, or even acts of brahminicide,"

children.text: paramārthavinna puṇyairna ca pāpaiḥ spṛśyate vimalaḥ // 70 //
children.translated_text: "the knower of ultimate reality is not touched by merit or by demerit — he is stainless. (70)"
knows the ultimate reality

children.text: svātmamaheśvarasvabhāvasatattvajñaḥ so 'śvamedharājasūyāptoryāmādiyajñānniḥsaṃkhyānphalakāmanābhimānavirahātkartavyatāmātramidamityevaṃ kṛtvā krīḍārthaṃ yadi kadācidvihitāni karmāṇi vidadhātyathavā brahmahananasurāpānastainyādīni pramādopanatāni mahāpātakānyavihitānyapyaśarīratayā cetyubhayathāhaṃ mametyabhimānābhāvātparameśvarecchaivetthaṃ vijṛmbhate mama kimāyātamiti buddhyā na
children.translated_text: He who truly knows the nature of his own Self as the Supreme Lord — he, out of playfulness, if he sometimes performs prescribed rites such as the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, <s>Rājasūya</s>, <s>Aptoryāma</s>, and other innumerable sacrifices — thinking 'this is merely something to be done,' free from the conceit of desire for their fruits — or if, by inadvertence, he commits even the great sins which are unpreferred, such as killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, drinking liquor, theft, and the like, since he is bodiless [i.e., identified with the Self beyond the body], and since in both cases there is no conceit of 'I' and 'mine,' [thinking] 'it is merely the will of the Supreme Lord that thus unfolds — what has befallen me?' — with such understanding, he is not
by merit —
by auspicious fruits, nor by
sin —
by inauspicious [fruits], that knower
is touched —
is tainted. How is this so? [The author] says:
'Stainless' —

children.text: iti / yatastasya vigatāḥ prakṣīṇā āṇavamāyīyakārmamalāḥ saṃsaraṇahetava iti / evaṃ malinasya hi pramāturvicchinnadehādipramātṛtayātmātmīyābhimānabhāvo yena mamedaṃ karma śubhamidamaśubhamityabhimānadaurātmyātpuṇyapāpasaṃcayayogaḥ syādyasya karmaphalasaṃcayo mamatvaheturmalapracayo vigataḥ syāttasyābhimānābhāvātkathaṃ puṇyapāpasparśaḥ / yathā śrībhagavadgītāsu
children.translated_text: because his impurities — the <s>āṇava</s> (innate), <s>māyīya</s> (illusory), and <s>kārma</s> (karmic) — the causes of transmigration, have departed, have been extinguished. For it is only for the impure subject, limited by the subjectivity of the body and the like, that there arises the conceit of self and mine — 'this deed of mine is auspicious, this is inauspicious' — and through the evil of such conceit, the accumulation of merit and sin occurs. He whose accumulation of karmic results — the cause of selfhood — the mass of impurity, has departed — for him, due to the absence of conceit, how could there be contact with merit and sin? As in the holy <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>:

body.translated_text: He who thus

children.text: yasya nāhaṅkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate /
children.translated_text: 'He who has no sense of ego, whose intellect is not tainted —

children.text: hatvāpi sa imāṃllokānna hanti na nibadhyate //
children.translated_text: even though he slays these people, he neither slays nor is bound.'

body.translated_text: Reflecting on the prescribed conduct of such a knower, [the author] says:

children.translated_text: Free from pride, excitement, anger, desire, despondency, fear, greed, and delusion,
devoid of hymns and <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-calls, like an inert person, he should wander, his mind free from dogmatic assertions. // 71 //
'Pride' (<s>mada</s>) —
the conceit of identification with the body as the subject.
'Excitement' (<s>harṣa</s>) —
joy from obtaining what was not [previously] obtained.
'Anger' (<s>kopa</s>) —
wrath.
'Desire' (<s>manmatha</s>) —
the longing for sensual enjoyment.
'Despondency' (<s>viṣāda</s>) —
bewilderment from separation from what is desired.
'Fear' (<s>bhaya</s>) —
dread of an enemy, or of a lion, tiger, and the like.
'Greed' (<s>lobha</s>) —
miserliness.
'Delusion' (<s>moha</s>) —

children.text: bhūteṣvātmātmīyabhāva ityetāndehasaṃskārapratyavamarśānmadhye madhye samāyātānapi sarvaṃ brahmāsmīti parivarjayatyavikalpakasaṃvidrūpānupraveśena svātmapratyavamarśaśeṣībhūtānsaṃpādayati / tathā nirgataḥ stotravaṣaṭkārebhyo yaḥ sa evaṃ stutyasya vyatiriktasyābhāvānna tasya stotrādyupayogo nāpi vaṣaḍādimantrasaṃśrayo bhinnasya devatāviśeṣasya virahātkevalaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: the sense of self and mine in beings — these mental imprints and reflective awarenesses of the body, though they arise from time to time, he abandons — [thinking] 'everything is <s>Brahman</s>' — through entering into the nature of non-conceptual consciousness, he renders them as mere residues of self-reflective awareness. Likewise, he from whom hymns and <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-calls have departed — since there is no entity separate from himself that could be praised, there is no use for him of hymns and the like, nor does he depend on <s>vaṣaṭ</s> and other <s>mantras</s>, since there is no particular deity separate [from himself]. He simply
should wander like an inert person, his mind free from dogmatic assertions —

children.text: iti / pūrṇatvādākāṅkṣāvirahācconmatta ivetikartavyatārūpe śāstrīye karmaṇi pramāṇopapanne vā prameyasatattve pramātṛbhiḥ sahedamupapannamidaṃ neti vicārabahiṣkṛtabuddhirnāpi svātmanyupadeśamapekṣate parānupadeṣṭuṃ vā prameyamupanyasyatīti dāntaprāyo bhūtvā sarvaṃ brahmāvalokayankrīḍārthaṃ viharedeveti jaḍatvena nirūpitaḥ // 71 //
children.translated_text: because of his completeness and the absence of want, like a madman, [he is] one whose intellect is excluded from deliberation about scriptural duties or about the reality of objects established by valid means of knowledge — [as to whether] 'this is established, this is not' — nor does he expect instruction regarding his own Self, nor does he present a cognizable [object] to instruct others. Having become mostly subdued, beholding everything as <s>Brahman</s>, he should sport playfully — thus his description as one who is 'inert.' // 71 //

body.text: evamapi parivarjyamānenāpi madādivargeṇa vayamiva jñānī sati śarīre kimiva na spṛśyata ityatra kāraṇamāha
body.translated_text: Even though the group beginning with pride is being avoided, the knower — like us — while possessing a body, why is he not touched by [these]? Regarding this, [the author] states the reason:

children.translated_text: This group beginning with pride and excitement arises from the delusion of difference.
How then could the one whose awakening is the non-dual Self be touched by it? // 72 //
this group beginning with pride — from the delusion of difference —
which is of the nature of self and mine,
the delusion of difference —
the perception of incompleteness — from that,
[it] arises —

children.text: paśupramātṛbhyo dvaitabhrāntyā heyopādeyatayā samutpadyate / yaḥ punaḥ sarvaṃ brahmāsmīti paramādvayātmabodhaḥ prakṛṣṭajñānyākāśakalpaḥ saḥ
children.translated_text: it originates for the <s>paśu</s>-subjects through the delusion of duality, as something to be rejected or accepted. But he who [possesses] the supreme non-dual self-awakening — 'everything is <s>Brahman</s>' — the supreme knower, like space, he
by that —
group beginning with pride,
how could he be touched? —

children.text: kena prakāreṇābilīkriyatāṃ bhinnaṃ vastu bhinnasya hi kadācitsvarūpamarpayatāṃ brahmabhūtatvena gṛhīto madādivargo brahmabhūtasya jñāninaḥ samānajāteḥ kathaṃ virodhāya syāditi // 72 //
children.translated_text: by what means could he be tainted? A differentiated thing can at some point confer its nature upon a differentiated [subject]. But the group of pride and the like, when grasped as having become <s>Brahman</s>, how could it be antagonistic to the knower who has become <s>Brahman</s>, since they are of the same class? // 72 //

body.translated_text: As explained in the immediately preceding <s>kārikā</s>,

body.text: bāhyastavanahavanavargo 'pi dvaitasamāśraya eva na tasya paritoṣāyālamityāha
body.translated_text: The external group of praising and fire-offering also depends on duality and is not sufficient for his satisfaction — [the author] says:

children.text: stutyaṃ vā hotavyaṃ nāsti vyatiriktamasya kiñcana ca /
children.translated_text: There is nothing separate from him that could be praised or that should be offered into the fire.
Would he be satisfied by hymns and the like? Being liberated, he is free from salutations and <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-calls. // 73 //
'Something to be praised' —
some deity-form;
'or something to be offered into the fire' —
anything [separate] from the knower whose nature is the awakening of non-duality —
nothing separate —

children.text: bhinnarūpaṃ vidyate yatstūyate hūyate veti / nāpi
children.translated_text: nothing of a different form exists that could be praised or offered into the fire. Nor is there
anything to be done —
of such a nature. And
by hymns and the like, he —

children.text: ātmajñaḥ paritoṣaṃ yātyabhedabodhasaṃbhogena hi nityānandamayatvātkṛtrimamānandaṃ nādriyate tasmānnirgato namaskṛtivaṣaṭkebhyo yaḥ sa eva
children.translated_text: the knower of the Self, would attain satisfaction — [but] since through the enjoyment of non-dual awakening he is of the nature of eternal bliss, he does not esteem artificial bliss. Therefore, he from whom salutations and <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-calls have departed — he alone is
liberated —
thus praised in the <s>Vedāntas</s>. // 73 //

body.text: na ca tasya bhinnena devagṛheṇopayogaḥ svaśarīramevātmadevatādhiṣṭhānaṃ saṃvidāśrayo vā nānyaḥ kaściditi no bhinnaṃ devagṛhamasyetyāha
body.translated_text: Nor is there any use for him of a separate temple; his own body is the abode of the Self-deity, or rather consciousness is the foundation — nothing else. Therefore he has no separate temple — [the author] says:

children.translated_text: Supported by the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>, filled with windows that are the arrangement of the body,

children.text: nijamanyadatha śarīraṃ ghaṭādi vā tasya devagṛham // 74 //
children.translated_text: his own or another's body, or a pot and the like — that is his temple. // 74 //
Of that

children.text: jñānino nijaḥ parakīyo vā deha eva devatāveśma svātmadevatāyā bhogyādhāratvāt / bāhyastu mervādiprāsādastadā devagṛhībhavati yadā guruṇā śarīravyāptyā ṣaṭtriṃśattattvakalanarūpayā parikalpitaḥ syāttadgato bāhyo 'pi devaḥ svātmavyāptyā cidghanatvena parigṛhītaścettadā so 'pi tatra devo bhavedanyathobhayametajjaḍaṃ śilāśakalakalpameva kathaṃ bhaktānuddharenmṛtānsāmīpyādi vā nayedityevaṃ mukhyayā vṛttyā
children.translated_text: knower, his own body or someone else's body is the abode of the deity — the temple of the Self-deity — because it is the locus of what is to be enjoyed. The external temple such as Mount <s>Meru</s> and the like becomes a temple when it is constructed by the <s>guru</s> through the extension of the body in the form of the arrangement of the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>. Even the external deity placed therein, if grasped through the extension of one's own Self as a solid mass of consciousness, then he too becomes a deity there. Otherwise, both this [body and temple] would be inert, like a piece of stone — how would they uplift devotees, or bring the dead to proximity [with the divine] and the like? Thus, in the primary sense,
the body —

children.text: saṃvidāśrayatvāddevagṛhaṃ tadgataḥ sarveṣāmapi svātmā deva iti deha eva saṃprabuddhasya devagṛham / kīdṛśaṃ tadityāha
children.translated_text: because it is the locus of consciousness, is the temple; the deity residing in it is the Self of everyone — thus, for the awakened one, the body alone is the temple. What is it like? [The author] says:
'Thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>' —

children.text: iti / bāhyaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvavyāptyā parikalpyate paraṃ dehadevagṛhaṃ punaḥ sākṣātṣaṭtriṃśatā tattvaiḥ
children.translated_text: the external [temple] is constructed through the extension of the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>, but the body-temple is directly
supported —
nourished by the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>. In the external temple there are window-constructions, but this [body-temple] is
filled with windows that are the arrangement of the body —
that is,
in the body —
the physical form,
the arrangement —
the series of sense-organ doors — that itself is the opening of windows; by that [arrangement]
[it is] filled —

children.text: akṣuṇṇamiti bāhyadevagṛhasadṛśam / na kevalaṃ sarīraṃ saṃvida āśraya iti kṛtvā devagṛhaṃ yāvadyatkiñcidvā saṃvidadhiṣṭhitaṃ tatsarvaṃ tasya devagṛhamityāha
children.translated_text: complete — thus resembling an external temple. Not only is the body a temple because it is the locus of consciousness, but whatever is presided over by consciousness — all of that is his temple — [the author] says:
'Or a pot and the like' —

children.text: iti / ghaṭādyupalakṣitaṃ viṣayapañcakamidaṃ bhogyarūpaṃ cakṣurādidvāreṇa saṃvidādhiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: the fivefold sense-objects, indicated by 'pot and the like,' which are of the nature of what is to be enjoyed, presided over by consciousness through the door of the eye and other [senses] —

body.translated_text: 'The experiencer alone, in the form of what is experienced, is always established everywhere' —

body.text: iti spandaśāstropadeśadṛśā saṃvinmayameva jñānino bhūtaśarīravadghaṭādi viśvaṃ bhāvaśarīramiti kṛtvā tadapyabhinnaṃ svaśarīravat

children.translated_text: a temple —
of the God, the freely sporting, autonomous Self-as-Supreme-Lord,
the abode —
the locus of what is to be enjoyed. // 74 //

body.translated_text: according to the teaching-perspective of the <s>Spanda</s> scripture, for the knower, the pot and the like — the entire universe — being of the nature of consciousness like the elemental body, is [another] body of existence; therefore that too, being non-different like one's own body, is

body.text: bāhyadevagṛhe kila bhaktaḥ puṣpādyāharaṇapūrvaṃ devapūjāparo dṛṣṭo dehadevagṛhe punarjñānī kiṃ kurvannadhitiṣṭhatītyāha
body.translated_text: In an external temple, a devotee is seen devoted to the worship of the deity, first bringing flowers and the like. But in the body-temple, the knower — what does he do while presiding? [The author] says:

children.translated_text: And there, worshipping the deity of the Supreme Self, the Great <s>Bhairava</s> — <s>Śiva</s>, accompanied by His own powers,
with offerings purified by the reflective awareness of the Self — he abides. // 75 //
supreme —
surpassing all, whose characteristic is consciousness,
the Self —
He Himself, because of His capacity to dissolve the enjoyment of all objects such as sound and the like without remainder,
[is] <s>Bhairava</s> —
whose nature is sustaining (<s>bharaṇa</s>), sounding (<s>ravaṇa</s>), and emitting (<s>vamana</s>) — He Himself is
the deity <s>Śiva</s> —
the God whose nature is supreme blessedness — that [deity],
worshipping, he abides —

children.text: anavarataṃ vakṣyamāṇena krameṇa tāṃ tarpayanparisphuret / nanu bāhyadevatā parivārayutā bhavatyetāṃ kiṃparivārayutāṃ samarcayedityāha
children.translated_text: he shines forth ceaselessly, satisfying [that deity] through the method to be described. But an external deity is accompanied by a retinue — this one too, with what retinue should he worship? [The author] says:
'Accompanied by His own powers' —
this [means]:
'One's own' —
the powers of the sense organs such as the eye, which are in the form of rays of consciousness, which are the glory of the powers of consciousness, bliss, will, knowledge, and action — by those,
'accompanied' —
surrounded on all sides. With what does he worship? [The author] says:
'By the reflective awareness of the Self' —
and so on. 'All this is my own Self' — that which is
the reflective awareness —

children.text: sarvapadārthānāṃ saṃvidrūpatayā pūrṇāhantāviśrāntilakṣaṇo yaḥ parāmarśastena dvaitakāluṣyakalaṅkaparikṣayāt
children.translated_text: the apprehension (<s>parāmarśa</s>) characterized by repose in the full I-consciousness regarding all entities as having the nature of consciousness — through that, due to the elimination of the stain of the impurity of duality,
pure —
the offerings in the form of the fivefold sense-objects — sound and the like — for the purpose of worship,
the substances (<s>dravya</s>) —

children.text: jāḍyāpagamena viśuddhāni tairātmāmarśanavimaladravyairiti / ayamāśayo jñānī heyopādeyabhedakalaṅkaparityāgenāyatnopanataṃ śabdādiviṣayapañcakaṃ śrotrādikaraṇadevībhiḥ samāhṛtyāntaścamatkurvansvātmanābhedamāpādayatītyevamanavarataṃ prativiṣayasvīkārakāle yo 'ntarabhedena camatkāraḥ pūrṇāhantāsphuraṇametadeva svātmadevatāpūjanamata eva śabdādayo viṣayāḥ pūjopakaraṇamityavadhānavatā viṣayagrahaṇakāle pratikṣaṇaṃ svātmadevatāpūjakena bhāvyamiti rahasyavidaḥ / etadeva stutidvāreṇa rājānakarāmo dṛbdhavānyathā
children.translated_text: purified through the removal of inertness — with those substances purified by the reflective awareness of the Self. The essential meaning is this: the knower, having abandoned the stain of the distinction between what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted, having gathered through the goddess-senses of hearing and the like the fivefold sense-objects of sound and the like which have arrived effortlessly, savoring them inwardly, brings them to non-difference with his own Self. Thus, at every moment of apprehending each object, the inner wonder of non-difference — the flash of the full I-consciousness — this itself is the worship of the Self-deity. Hence the sense-objects of sound and the like are the articles of worship. Therefore, one who is attentive should at every moment, when apprehending objects, be a worshipper of the Self-deity — [so say] those who know the secret. This very [teaching], through the medium of a hymn, King <s>Anakarāma</s> [Janaka?] has expressed otherwise:

body.translated_text: In that temple of his own body, the supreme <s>yogin</s> —

children.translated_text: 'With the offering of world-impressions ceaselessly gathered through perpetual unrestrained exertion,
by your powers beginning with <s>taijasī</s>, you are satisfied.
In this body — a charnel-house, flooded with flesh, blood, fat, and heaps of bones —
reveal to me, O hero who wanders through the night of existence, the form of <s>Bhairava</s>!'

body.text: pūjānte tāvadagnihavanena bhāvyamiti jñāninaḥ kathaṃ tadityāha
body.translated_text: After worship, the fire-offering should be contemplated — for the knower, how is that? [The author] says:

children.translated_text: For the one who offers into the exceedingly blazing fire of consciousness the great mass of seeds of the conceptual distinction of external and internal,
the fire-offering (<s>homa</s>) occurs without effort. // 76 //
'Of that one' —
of such a worshipper of the Self-deity,
'exceedingly blazing' —
in the fire of consciousness, radiant with the supreme I-consciousness wonder,
'without effort' —
without the trouble of procuring sesame, ghee, firewood, and the like,
the fire-offering (<s>homa</s>) —
the satisfaction of the fire is accomplished. What does he do? [The author] says:
'External and internal' —
and so on.
'External' —

children.text: nīlādau prameye yatsvaparapramātṛkalpanamantargrāhye sukhādau ca yatsaṃkalpanamityevaṃrūpo yaḥ
children.translated_text: regarding the cognizable [object] such as blue and the like, whatever conceptual construction [is made] of self and other subjects; and 'internal' — regarding the graspable [experience] such as pleasure and the like, whatever mental imaging — of such a nature, the
difference —
the diversity, whose nature is the activity of determination, imagination, and conceit regarding external and internal, subject and object — that itself is
the great seed —
the seed of difference, since [the experience of] subject and object arises from it, and since it is of the nature of conceptual construction;
the mass —
the heap of [difference], due to its infinity — that,
offering —

children.text: paramādvayadṛṣṭyāvikalpakasaṃvidrūpānupraveśena svātmavahnau juhvata iti / ayamāśayaḥ parabrahmātmakasya yogino dehādipramātṛtābhimānābhāvādyaḥ svarasasiddhaḥ svaparapramātṛprameyakalanaparikṣayaḥ sa evākṛtrimo homaḥ / yathāha bhaṭṭaśrīvīravāmanaḥ
children.translated_text: oblating into the fire of one's own Self through entering into the nature of non-conceptual consciousness from the perspective of supreme non-duality. The essential meaning is this: for the <s>yogin</s> whose nature is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, since there is no conceit of identification with the body and the like as the subject, the natural elimination of the conceptual construction of self and other, subject and object — that itself is the unconditioned fire-offering. As the venerable <s>Bhaṭṭa Śrī Vīravāmana</s> has said:
'Where the fuel is the forest of duality and death itself is the great sacrificial animal —
by that supramundane sacrifice we perpetually offer oblations.'

body.translated_text: Regarding the meditation of such a sacrificer, [the author] says:

children.translated_text: Meditation that never sets — for this Blessed One creates variegated forms;
that itself is meditation — because it has the nature of reality drawn by the creative will. // 77 //
meditation that never sets —
because
this Blessed One —
the infinite Supreme Lord whose nature is the Self, through the freedom of <s>vikalpa</s> (creative ideation) whose nature is the power of action, the
variegated forms He creates —
He ceaselessly inscribes various entities — forms of <s>vikalpa</s> — in the mirror of the intellect;
that itself —
free from setting and rising — is His
meditation.

children.text: cintanaṃ nāto 'nyatkiñcit / itaratra tu devatāviśeṣe nānāvaktrāṅgaparikalpanayā naiyatyaṃ syāt / sarvo manovyāpāraḥ parāśaktisphārapallavabhūta iti jānānasyānavacchinnamidaṃ sarvaṃ parameśvarībhūtam / tathā
children.translated_text: is meditation — nothing other than this. In other [systems], however, with the imagination of various faces and limbs for a particular deity, there would be rigidity. All mental activity is a bud of the expansion of the supreme power (<s>Parāśakti</s>) — for one who knows this, all this, without limitation, has become the Supreme Goddess Herself. Likewise,
by thought (<s>saṃkalpa</s>),
by the mind,
painted —
depicted upon the canvas of consciousness —
having the nature of reality —

children.text: paramārthatā yasya dhyānasya tat / evaṃ yataḥ sarvamidaṃ prakāśamānaṃ vikalpollikhitaṃ manovyāpārarūpamapi prakāśānatiriktaṃ satyaṃ sarvatra saṃvidanugamāditi / taduktaṃ śrīmatsvacchandaśāstre
children.translated_text: this is the ultimate truth of that meditation. Thus, since all this that appears, even though drawn by conceptual construction and having the form of mental activity, is not separate from the light [of consciousness] and is real, because consciousness pervades everywhere. As stated in the sacred <s>Svacchandatantra</s>:

body.translated_text: The form of an object contemplated in a fixed shape perishes when the mental activity moves elsewhere — but this is

children.text: yatra yatra mano yāti tatra tatraiva dhārayet /
children.translated_text: 'Wherever the mind goes, one should hold it right there; /

children.text: calitvā kutra gantāsi sarvaṃ śivamayaṃ yataḥ //
children.translated_text: having moved, where will you go? Since everything is pervaded by <s>Śiva</s>.' //

body.translated_text: And likewise in the <s>Śaivopaniṣad</s>:

children.text: yatra yatra mano yāti bāhye vābhyantare priye /
children.translated_text: 'Wherever the mind goes, whether external or internal, O beloved, /
there, there is the state of <s>Śiva</s> — being all-pervading, where will it go?' //

body.translated_text: Therefore, this meditation of the yogin arises spontaneously. // 77 //
He now says what kind of recitation (<s>japa</s>) belongs to this [yogin]:

children.translated_text: The entire succession of worlds, the arrangement of the <s>tattva</s> order, and the collection of senses — /

children.text: antarbodhe parivartayati ca yatso 'sya japa uditaḥ // 78 //
children.translated_text: that which revolves all these within inner consciousness — this is declared to be his recitation. // 78 //

body.text: vakṣyamāṇena krameṇa yo viśvasya pratikṣaṇamabhedena parāhantāpratyavamarśaḥ

children.translated_text: that
itself,
his recitation, has been declared —
described as being natural, not artificial. What is it? He says:
'The entire succession of worlds' —
the complete array of two hundred and twenty-four [worlds] existing within the totality of thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>; likewise,
'the arrangement of the <s>tattva</s> order' —
namely,
of the <s>tattva</s> sequence
designated as <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,
the arrangement,
the delimitation;
'and the collection of senses' (<s>akṣagaṇa</s>) —
the group of senses in the form of inner and outer instruments; and all this
within inner consciousness (<s>antarbodha</s>) —
in one's own self-awareness, which serves as the rosary-thread of the central vital force (<s>madhyamaprāṇaśakti</s>), through the flow of <s>nāda</s> (sound) and <s>bindu</s> (point) —
that which revolves —

children.text: araghaṭṭaghaṭīyantravatpratiprāṇavikṣepasṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārakrameṇa sarvametatsvasaṃvittau paribhramayati pratikṣaṇaṃ nādātmanā parāmṛśatīti yāvat / sa eva pūrṇāhantāviśrāntilakṣaṇo 'kṛtrimo 'sya japaḥ / ayamāśayo japaḥ kila vācyarūpāyā devatāyā vācakasya mantrasyoccāraḥ sa cākṣamālayā prāṇaśaktivyāptikayākṣaparivartanakrameṇa saṃkhyeyaḥ / paramādvayayoginastu svā prāṇaśaktistantubhūtā madhyamaprāṇe pravāhakrameṇa nadantī svarasoditā sarvākṣakroḍīkāreṇa sahajaivākṣamālocyate yataḥ sarvamidaṃ vācyaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvātmakaṃ viśvaṃ prāṇaśaktāveva pratiṣṭhitaṃ satpratiprāṇavikṣepamudayavyayakrameṇa parāsvabhāvā bhagavatī prāṇasvarūpamāśritya vimṛśantī pratiprāṇaspandamavadhānavato yogino japamakṛtrimaṃ sādhayati / atra japasaṃkhyā
children.translated_text: like the buckets of a water-wheel, through the sequence of emission, maintenance, and dissolution at each outgoing and incoming breath, causes all this to revolve in one's own self-awareness — that is, at every moment it reflectively apprehends [all] in the form of <s>nāda</s> (resonance). This itself, characterized by resting in the full I-consciousness, natural and unartificial, is his recitation. The purport is: recitation, indeed, is the utterance of a <s>mantra</s>, which is the signifier of a deity in the form of the signified; and that [recitation] is to be counted by a rosary in the form of the rotation of the senses through the activity of the vital force (<s>prāṇaśakti</s>). But for the yogin of supreme non-duality, his own vital force, serving as the thread, resonating in the central breath (<s>madhyamaprāṇa</s>) through the course of its flow, naturally arising — incorporating all the senses — constitutes the rosary; since this entire signified reality, the universe consisting of thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>, is established in the vital force, and at each exhalation and inhalation, the <s>Bhagavatī</s> whose nature is <s>Parā</s>, having assumed the form of the vital force, reflectively apprehending — at each pulsation of the breath — accomplishes the natural recitation for the yogin who is attentive. Here the count of recitations [is given in the <s>Śaivopaniṣad</s>]:

body.translated_text: The reflective awareness of the supreme I-consciousness (<s>parāhantā</s>), at every moment, in non-duality with the universe, in the manner to be described —

children.translated_text: 'Twenty-one thousand six hundred [breaths] day and night — /

children.text: japo devyāḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ sulabho durlabho jaḍaiḥ //
children.translated_text: this is declared to be the recitation of the Goddess, easy [to obtain] yet difficult [to realize] for the dull.' //

body.translated_text: And in the <s>Śivasūtras</s>:
'Discourse itself is recitation (<s>japa</s>).' /
Thus this [recitation] is within the scope only of those who have practiced at the feet [of the master] and who are attentive. // 78 //
He now says what his vow (<s>vrata</s>) is:

children.text: sarvaṃ samayā dṛṣṭyā yatpaśyati yacca saṃvidaṃ manute /
children.translated_text: That he sees all things with an equal vision, and that he contemplates consciousness — /
delighting in the universe as a cremation ground, adorned with the skull-staff fashioned from the body — // 79 //
filled with the wine of the essence of the universe, the skull-cup that is the fragment of the knowable held in one's own hand — /

children.text: rasayati ca yattadetadvratamasya sudurlabhaṃ ca sulabhaṃ ca // 80 //
children.translated_text: that he savors this — this is his vow, exceedingly difficult yet easy to obtain. // 80 //
that which —
will be described —
this itself is
the knower's
vow (<s>vrata</s>) —
the observance for the purpose of worshipping the deity who is one's own Self. What is its nature? He says:
'Exceedingly difficult yet easy to obtain' —

children.text: iti / suṣṭhu kṛtvā duḥkhenākhyātiparikṣayādanyopāyaparihārarupeṇa parameśvarānugraheṇa labhyata ityataḥ
children.translated_text: that is: it is obtained with great difficulty, through the exhaustion of non-manifestation, in the form of the renunciation of other means, through the grace of the Supreme Lord; therefore it is
exceedingly difficult;

children.text: tathā sukhena bāhyāsthibhasmādyābharaṇāhāraniyamādisvīkārakadarthanāṃ ca vinā labhyata ityataḥ
children.translated_text: and likewise, it is obtained easily, without the torment of adopting external ornaments of bones, ashes, and the like, or dietary restrictions and other observances; therefore it is
easy to obtain.
What is this vow? He says:
'All' —

children.text: ityādi / yatsarvamidaṃ prātītikaṃ bhedāvabhāsarūpaṃ yuktyāgamānubhavapariśīlanenābhedadṛśā sarvamidamekaḥ sphurāmīti samīkṣate / yathā śrībhagavadgītāsu
children.translated_text: and so forth. That [the yogin] beholds all this phenomenal appearance, which is in the form of differentiation, with a vision of non-difference, through the cultivation of reasoning, scripture, and experience — [thinking] 'I alone shine forth as all this.' As in the sacred <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>:
'He who sees the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self, /
the one whose self is united in <s>Yoga</s>, who sees equally everywhere.' //

body.translated_text: Thus,

children.translated_text: that he contemplates consciousness as delighting in the universe-as-cremation-ground —
that too is a vow. Just as:
the universe,
whose nature is the grasped and the grasper — since it is pervaded by hundreds of corpse-like inert objects such as pots, bodies, and the like — that itself is
the cremation ground (<s>śmaśāna</s>),

children.text: pitṛvanaṃ yataḥ saṃvidekā bhagavatyajaḍāto 'nyattadullāsitaṃ sarvamidaṃ śavasthānīyaṃ jaḍamato viśvasya śmaśānena sādṛśyam / tasmin
children.translated_text: the charnel ground; because consciousness alone, the <s>Bhagavatī</s>, is non-inert, and everything else, manifested by Her, is equivalent to a corpse, being inert — thus the universe resembles a cremation ground. In that
universe-cremation-ground,
completely,
the consciousness that delights —
dwelling in the midst of what is supremely terrifying, with its arising and perishing —
he contemplates,

children.text: avabudhyate / vratī kila śmaśāne vasatyayaṃ punaralaukiko vratī sarvatrāhamevaikacittatattvaparamārtha iti matvā jaḍaiḥ paśupramātṛbhirghaṭādibhiḥ prameyaiśca paretasthānīyaiḥ sahonmattavatkrīḍāṃ kurvāṇaḥ saṃsārabhuvamimāṃ sarvapramātṛprameyanidhanatayā bhīṣaṇaṃ śmaśānasvabhāvāmadhyāste / anyacca yat
children.translated_text: he realizes. An [ordinary] practitioner of the vow dwells in a cremation ground; but this extraordinary practitioner of the vow, knowing that everywhere 'I alone am the one reality of consciousness, the supreme truth,' plays like a madman with the inert objects — pots and the like, which are like the dead, and the bound subjects (<s>paśu-pramātṛs</s>) — and abides in this ground of <s>saṃsāra</s>, which has the nature of a cremation ground, being terrifying due to the death of all subjects and objects. And furthermore,
he contemplates consciousness as adorned with the skull-staff (<s>khaṭvāṅga</s>) fashioned from the body —
thus.
The body (<s>vigraha</s>) —
the physical frame — that itself becomes
the fashioning of the skull-staff (<s>khaṭvāṅga</s>) —

children.text: kaṅkālavidhiryoginaḥ kila svaśarīrapramātṛtābhimānadurgrahasaṃkṣayāccharīrātītaṃ svātmānaṃ manyamānasya saṃskāraśeṣībhūto vigrahaḥ śavaprāyamevetyavadhārayataḥ svaśarīrameva kaṅkālamudrākalpanā tayā
children.translated_text: the skeleton-observance: for the yogin who, through the destruction of the tenacious false identification of himself as the body-subject, considers his Self as transcending the body, the body — now a mere residue of impressions — is virtually a corpse; thus, for one who realizes this, his own body is itself the fashioning of the skeleton-<s>mudrā</s>, and by that [fashioning],
adorned —

children.text: bhogyādhāratvena mudritām / vīravratino hi śmaśānasthasya khaṭvāṅgamudrayā bhāvyamato 'sya svasaṃvidvapuṣaḥ svaśarīramapi vedyatayā bhinnamavadhārayataḥ saiva khaṭvāṅgamudretyetadapyasya vratam / tathā
children.translated_text: marked as the support of what is to be enjoyed. For the practitioner of the heroic vow, dwelling in the cremation ground, the skull-staff <s>mudrā</s> is to be practiced; thus for him, who perceives his own body — though being the body of his own consciousness — as separate in its knowability, this very [perception] is the skull-staff <s>mudrā</s>. This too is his vow. Likewise,
'he savors the skull-cup that is the fragment of the knowable' —
he chews, he savors — that which has the nature of the fivefold [offering] characterized by the five sense-objects beginning with sound — this entire enjoyable reality,
the knowable (<s>vedya</s>) —
delimited by its being knowable and being an effect —
a fragment (<s>khaṇḍaka</s>) —
like a broken shard; that itself is
the skull-cup (<s>kapāla</s>) —
a fragment of skull-bone;
that which he savors —

children.text: sārāharaṇakrameṇa pūrṇāhantāviśrāntyā camatkuruta ityetadapi vratam / vratinā kila kapālasthaṃ vīrapānaṃ rasyata ityāha
children.translated_text: by the method of extracting the essence, through resting in the full I-consciousness, he relishes with self-awareness — this too is a vow. Indeed, by the practitioner of the vow, the heroic drink contained in the skull-cup is savored; he says:
'The essence of the universe' (<s>viśvarasa</s>) —
thus.
In the universe —

children.text: vedyaśabdādiviṣayapañcakarūpe kapālakhaṇḍe yo 'sau sārabhāgaścarvaṇāmṛtamayoṃ'śaḥ sa eva paramānandadāyitvāt
children.translated_text: in the skull-fragment that has the form of the fivefold sense-objects beginning with sound that constitute the knowable — that which is the essential portion, the nectar-like share of chewing — that itself, being the bestower of supreme bliss, is
the wine, the distilled essence (<s>rasāsava</s>) —

the supreme drink.
With that,
full —

children.text: nirbharam / etaduktaṃ syādviśvasya yaḥ śalkasthānīyaḥ kaṭhinoṃ'śaḥ pātrakalpaḥ sa eva kapālaṃ tadgataḥ sārabhāgaścamatkārakṣama āhlādadāyitvātpānamiti / kapālaṃ tu vratinaḥ karagataṃ bhavatītyāha
children.translated_text: brimming over. This means: the hard, shell-like portion of the universe, which is like a vessel, is itself the skull-cup; the essential portion within it, which is worthy of self-awareness and capable of bestowing delight, is the drink. But the skull-cup is held in the hand of the practitioner; he says:
'held in one's own hand' (<s>nijakaragam</s>) —
thus.
One's own (<s>nija</s>) —
belonging to one's own Self; those which are
the hands (<s>kara</s>) —

children.text: cakṣurādikaraṇadevīsvabhāvāścinmarīcayasteṣu bhogyatayā tadvedyakhaṇḍakaṃ viṣayatvaṃ gacchatīti nijakaragaṃ yathā pāṇisthena kapālena pānaṃ pīyate tathaiva vedyakhaṇḍakakapālena viśvarasāsavaścakṣurādisaṃvitkarairyoginā samāhṛtyāsvādyate / ayamāśayo yogī sarvadaiva yathopanataṃ viṣayapañcakaṃ karaṇadevībhirāhṛtya yuktyā svacaitanyabhairavaviśrāntimavyucchinnāṃ bhajamānaścaramakṣaṇaparyantaṃ yathopadiṣṭamadvayadṛśā nirvāhayatītyetadevāsya pariśīlitasadgurucaraṇapaṅkajasya vratamato 'nyaccharīraśoṣaṇamātramiti // 80 //
children.translated_text: the rays of consciousness whose nature is the sense-deities beginning with the eye — into them, as what is to be enjoyed, that skull-fragment of the knowable enters into the state of an object; just as a drink is drunk from a skull-cup held in the hand, even so the wine of the essence of the universe is gathered and savored by the yogin through the consciousness-hands of the eye and other [senses], using the skull-cup of the fragment of the knowable. The purport is: the yogin, always, whatever fivefold sense-object presents itself, gathering it through the sense-goddesses, experiences an unbroken resting in the <s>Bhairava</s> of his own consciousness through [proper] method, and sustains this to the very last moment with the vision of non-duality as instructed — this alone is his vow, for one who has practiced at the lotus-feet of the true <s>Guru</s>; anything else is mere bodily mortification. // 80 //

body.translated_text: Thus, firmness in the conviction of non-difference is itself the vow. And furthermore,
Summarizing what has been previously set forth, he declares the excellence of this teaching:

children.translated_text: Having thus attained the supreme reality called the Great Lord, free from birth and destruction, /
through the manifestation of the experiencer-nature, one abides as one who has accomplished his purpose, as one pleases. // 81 //
Thus (<s>iti</s>) —
by the method just stated, the secret that has been set forth —
called 'the supreme reality, the Great Lord' —
the real Great Lord —
having attained (<s>upalabhya</s>) —
having fully realized through firm conviction in one's own Self. Of what nature? He says:
'Free from birth and destruction' —
meaning: by the attainment of which there would be neither birth nor death.
'One who has accomplished his purpose abides as one pleases' —
having attained this, since there is no remaining task to be accomplished, one who has accomplished the supreme goal of life —
as one pleases —
freely, without transgressing one's own will, maintaining the body like the spinning of a wheel —
abides —
spends one's time. How? He says:
'Through the manifestation of the experiencer-nature' —
that is: through the cultivation of this secret, the
manifestation (<s>prakāśa</s>),

children.text: parisphuraṇaṃ tasmāditi śarīrastho 'pi pūrṇānandamaya iti yāvat // 81 //
children.translated_text: the radiance, of the experiencer-nature in all states — therefore, even while embodied, one is full of complete bliss. // 81 //

body.text: itthaṃ svātmānaṃ yaḥ kaścijjīvatāṃ madhyājjānānaḥ sa sarvastadrūpaḥ syādityadhikāriniyamābhāvamāha
body.translated_text: Thus, whoever among living beings knows his own Self in this way becomes identified with That — he states the absence of any restriction on eligibility:

children.translated_text: Whoever knows the all-pervading [reality], thus described, the Self of all, with diversity dispelled, /

children.text: nirupamaparamānandaṃ yo vetti sa tanmayo bhavati // 82 //
children.translated_text: of incomparable supreme bliss — he becomes identified with That. // 82 //
'Thus' —
in the manner stated —
'the all-pervading' —
<s>Śiva</s>, the undivided mass of consciousness and bliss —
'thus described' —
made known through the cultivation of reasoning, scripture, and experience —
'whoever knows' —
whoever at all, any living being whatsoever, knows —
he
— having abandoned all contraction —
becomes identified with That (<s>tanmaya</s>),

children.text: śiva eva syāditi / atra svātmajñāne nādhikāriniyamo yato ye kecana janmamaraṇādidoṣāghrātāstiryañco 'pi vā te sarve svātmamaheśvarapratyabhijñānāttanmayā bhavantīti yacchabdasya parāmarśaḥ / kīdṛśaṃ ca
children.translated_text: becomes <s>Śiva</s> Himself. Here, there is no restriction on eligibility for Self-knowledge; since all beings whatsoever — even animals — who are tainted by the defects of birth, death, and the like, through the recognition of the Great Lord who is their own Self, become identified with Him; this is the import of the word 'whoever.' And of what nature is
'the Self of all' —

children.text: iti / sarveṣāṃ pramātṛprameyāṇāmātmā sarvāṇi vā pramātṛprameyāṇi yasyātmā taṃ sarvottīrṇaṃ sarvamayamiti yāvat / ata eva
children.translated_text: the Self of all subjects and objects; or that whose Self is all subjects and objects — Him who both transcends all and consists of all. For this very reason,
'with diversity dispelled' —
vanquished — because at all times and in all places [He] shines forth as having the nature of consciousness —
'diversity' —
the infinity of differentiation — Him who is thus described; and due to the absence of desire,
'incomparable' —
free from qualification, preeminent —
is the bliss

children.text: yasya tamevaṃvidhamiti svātmānaṃ jānānaḥ sarvaḥ śivarūpī syāditi // 82 //
children.translated_text: of whom — thus one who knows one's own Self in this way becomes of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. // 82 //

body.text: evamadhigatasvātmamaheśvaraḥ svaśarīrādhikāraparikṣaye kutra śarīraṃ parityajetkiṃ vā yātītyādisaṃśayaṃ pariharati
body.translated_text: Thus, for one who has realized the Great Lord as his own Self — when his entitlement to this body is exhausted, where should he abandon the body, and what state does he attain? He resolves this doubt:

children.translated_text: Whether at a sacred site or in the house of an outcaste, even with memory lost, abandoning the body, /
he who has been liberated at the very moment of knowledge attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute aloneness), free from sorrow. // 83 //

body.text: evaṃ pariśīlitasvasvarūpo jñānī sarvamidaṃ svātmaprakāśasvātantryamiti paramādvayadṛśā gāḍhaṃ samāśvastahṛdayaḥ

children.translated_text: at a sacred site (<s>tīrtha</s>) —

children.text: prayāgapuṣkarakurukṣetrādau mahāpuṇye sthāne 'tha vā śvapacasadane 'ntyajanagṛhopalakṣite 'tipāpīyasi śarīraṃ muñcannityubhayathā svīkāraparityāgakadarthanāvirahito 'pyātmajñānādeva
children.translated_text: at <s>Prayāga</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, and other supremely holy places; or, conversely, in the house of an outcaste (<s>śvapaca</s>), denoted as the dwelling of the lowest-born, an exceedingly sinful [place] — abandoning the body in either case, free from the torment of either acceptance or rejection — through Self-knowledge alone,
he attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute aloneness) —

children.text: kalevaraparikṣayātpradhānādikāryakāraṇavargebhyo 'nyāṃ cidānandaikaghanāṃ turyātītarūpāṃ kevalatāṃ yātīti yāvat / yato 'sya sarvamidaṃ viśvaṃ svātmanā pūrṇaṃ samadṛśā parameśvarādhiṣṭhitaṃ paśyato na kṣetrākṣetrapravibhāgo 'ta eva
children.translated_text: upon the dissolution of the body, from the groups of effects and causes such as <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and so forth, attains a solitude that is a compact mass of consciousness and bliss, of the nature of <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth). Since for one who sees this entire universe as filled with his own Self, with equal vision, presided over by the Supreme Lord, there is no distinction of sacred and non-sacred ground — for this very reason,
destroyed,
overcome — the
grief
arising from doubt and conceptualization, by which he is thus free. As it is said:

body.translated_text: Thus, the knower who has cultivated his own essential nature, with heart firmly convinced through the supreme non-dual vision that 'all this is the freedom of the light of my own Self' —

children.text: himavati gaṅgādvāre vārāṇasyāṃ kurau prayāge vā /
children.translated_text: "On the <s>Himālayas</s>, at the source of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, or at <s>Prayāga</s>,"
"or in the house of a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> and others — for those who know the <s>Śiva</s>-reality, death is equal everywhere."

body.text: iti śrīnirvāṇayogottare / nāpyasya dehapātāvasare smṛtyupayoga ityāha

children.translated_text: "Even with memory lost" —

children.text: iti / āstāṃ saṃsmṛtirityapiśabdārthaḥ / yadi vā sa jñānī śarīratyāgakāle tadutthavātapittaśleṣmābhibhavāt
children.translated_text: let alone remembrance — this is the meaning of the word 'api' (even). Or, if that <s>jñānin</s>, at the time of leaving the body, due to being overwhelmed by the wind, bile, and phlegm arising from that,
has lost his memory,

children.text: kāṣṭhapāṣāṇatulyatvādvigatasvātmasaṃbodhaḥ kalevaramavaśo bhutvā tyajati tathāpi prāgadhigatasvātmajñānaḥ kaivalyamavaśyaṃ yāti tato na svātmajñānādhigame pramayasamaye smaraṇāsmaraṇe viśeṣo 'sti / nanu tīrthātīrthapravibhāgo 'sya svātmajñānavido mā bhūdyatpunarantakāle sa naṣṭasmṛtirapīti yadeva svātmajñānamupāyatayā gṛhītaṃ tasya dehapātāvasare tu vismaraṇaṃ cettarhi kathaṃ sa muktaḥ syāt / yaduktam
children.translated_text: devoid of self-awareness like wood or stone — even while helplessly abandoning the body, nevertheless, having previously attained Self-knowledge, he certainly attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute aloneness). Therefore, at the attainment of Self-knowledge, remembrance or non-remembrance at the time of death makes no difference. But it might be objected: granted that for this knower of the Self there is no distinction of sacred and non-sacred ground; but since it is said that 'even with memory lost at the end' — if the very Self-knowledge that was adopted as the means is forgotten at the time of the body's fall, then how could he be liberated? As stated:

body.translated_text: Thus in the sacred <s>Nirvāṇayogottara</s>. Nor is there any use of remembrance for him at the time of the body's fall — he says:

children.translated_text: "One who at the time of death, remembering me alone, leaves the body,"

children.text: yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: "he attains my state — there is no doubt about this."

body.text: iti śrīgītāsu / evamapyatra smaraṇasyaiva upayogo yadapi parameśvarasmaraṇābhāve 'pyantakāle tadbhāvāpattiḥ syāttarhi sarvaḥ paśujanaḥ pramayasamaye mūḍho 'pi viśeṣābhāvātparameśvarasamāpattiṃ yāyādvākyāni caivamādīnyapramāṇāni syurna caivamityatrottaramāha

children.translated_text: "Liberated at the very moment of knowledge" —

children.text: iti / satyaṃ nāsya smaraṇenopayogaḥ kintu sadguruṇā yadaiva tasya karṇamūle svātmamaheśvarajñānopadeśaḥ kṛtastasminneva kāle 'hameva sarvamidamityadhirūḍhasvātmajñānaparamārtho vigalitamāyādikañcukabhāvo nānyatkiñcidapekṣate kevalaṃ saṃskāraśeṣatayā cakrabhramavaccharīraṃ vahamāna iti na punastasyottarakāle smaraṇāsmaraṇakadarthanā yasmādajñānajanitāṇavamāyīyakañcukasaṃbandhe sati dehakañcukaṃ prabhavati svātmajñānopadeśenājñānajanitakañcukakṣayātkathaṃ dehakañcukaṃ vinaṣṭaprāyaṃ paryante jñānino yantraṇāṃ kartumalamiti svātmajñānakathanāvasara eva sa jīvanneva muktaḥ syāt / yathoktaṃ kularatnamālikāyāṃ sāhastrikāyām
children.translated_text: truly, remembrance serves no purpose for him. Rather, at the very moment when the true <s>guru</s> whispers the teaching of Self-knowledge of the great Lord into his ear, at that very time — 'I alone am all this' — with the ultimate meaning of Self-knowledge firmly established, the coverings of <s>māyā</s> and the rest having dissolved, he requires nothing else. He merely carries the body as a residual momentum, like a potter's wheel continuing to spin. Therefore, there is no tormenting question of remembering or not remembering at a later time for him, since the bondage of the body-covering prevails only when there exists the connection with the coverings born of ignorance — through the teaching of Self-knowledge, when the coverings born of ignorance have been destroyed, how can the body-covering, which is all but destroyed, have the power to control the <s>jñānin</s> at the end? Thus at the very occasion of speaking Self-knowledge, he would be liberated while still living. As stated in the <s>Kularatnamālikā Sāhastrikā</s>:

body.translated_text: Thus in the sacred <s>Gītā</s>. Even so, if there is use only for remembrance here — and if even without remembrance of the Supreme Lord at the end, one were to attain his state — then every bound creature, even though deluded at the time of death, would attain union with the Supreme Lord due to the absence of any distinction, and such statements would be invalid. But this is not so — to this he replies:

children.translated_text: "When the supreme <s>guru</s> rightly speaks it — that is beyond doubt —"
"he is liberated at that very moment; he merely dwells like a machine."
