body.translated_text: And in the sacred <s>Niśāṭana</s> also:

children.translated_text: "For the duration of milking a cow, or the flight of an arrow, or the blinking of an eye —"

children.text: sakṛdyuktaḥ pare tattve sa mukto mocayetparān //
children.translated_text: "one who is even once united with the supreme reality is liberated and liberates others."

children.text: yasmātpūrvaṃ pare nyasto yenātmā brahmaṇi kṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: "Since previously the Self was deposited in <s>Brahman</s> for even a moment,"

children.text: smaraṇaṃ tu kathaṃ tasya prāṇānte samupasthite //
children.translated_text: "how could remembrance be relevant for him when death approaches?"

body.text: iti / atha vātmavidaḥ paryantakṣaṇaḥ svānubhavaikasākṣī kenānubhūyate yadvaśāttasya smaraṇamasmaraṇaṃ vā parikalpyate yāvatā tatrārvāgdṛśāṃ nāsti gocara iti sarvajñāstratra praṣṭavyā na punaḥ śarīraceṣṭāmātrānmaraṇāvasare 'dhigataparamārthasyāpi dehatyāgakṣaṇaḥ śubhāśubhatvenānumātuṃ śakyaḥ / tasmādavaśyameva sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaṃ svātmajñānavidaṃ svātmastha eva parameśvaro maraṇāvasare svaṃ svarūpaṃ kāṣṭhapāṣāṇatulyamapi smārayati / yaduktam
body.translated_text: Moreover, the final moment of the knower of the Self, witnessed solely by his own experience — by whom is it experienced, on the basis of which his remembrance or non-remembrance is to be imagined? Since those of ordinary vision have no access there, the omniscient ones alone should be questioned about it. And the final moment of one who has attained the ultimate reality at the time of death cannot be inferred as auspicious or inauspicious merely from bodily movements. Therefore, the Supreme Lord, who is established in his own Self, certainly at the time of death, reminds of his own true nature even one who is like wood or stone, provided he has always been imbued with that state of Self-knowledge. As stated:

children.text: svasthaceṣṭāśca ye martyāḥ smaranti mama nārada /
children.translated_text: "Those mortals who, while healthy, remember me, O <s>Nārada</s> —"
"those who at the end are like wood or stone, I remember them."

body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: sthire cetasi susvasthe śarīre sati yo naraḥ /
children.translated_text: "The man who, when the mind is stable, the body healthy,"

children.text: dhātusāmye sthire smartā viśvarūpaṃ ca māmakam //
children.translated_text: "and the bodily constituents in equilibrium and steady, remembers my universal form —"
"then, when he is dying and resembles wood or stone,"

children.text: ahaṃ smarāmi madbhaktaṃ nayāmi paramāṃ gatim //
children.translated_text: "I remember my devotee and lead him to the supreme goal."

body.text: iti bhagavatā lakṣmīsaṃhitāyāmuktam / evamatra sadātadbhāvabhāvitatvameva heturanyathā pūrvānubhavasaṃskāradārḍhyaṃ vinā kathamante smṛtirapi syāditi na kenacidapi jñānino maraṇāvasare samupayoga iti // 83 //
body.translated_text: Thus spoken by the Blessed One in the <s>Lakṣmīsaṃhitā</s>. Thus here, the cause is precisely having always been imbued with that state; otherwise, without the firmness of <s>saṃskāras</s> from previous experience, how could there be remembrance at the end? Therefore, nothing whatsoever is of use to the <s>jñānin</s> at the time of death. (83)

body.text: yadi punastīrthādyāśrayaṇamuktaprakāreṇa na kutracidapyaṅgabhāvaṃ yāti tarhi kimiti vidvadbhistatsamāśrīyata iti viṣayavibhāgamāha
body.translated_text: If, however, resorting to sacred places and so forth does not serve as an auxiliary in any way, as previously explained, then why is it resorted to by the learned? He describes the domain of applicability:

children.translated_text: "Pilgrimage to sacred places leads to merit; death at the dwelling of an outcaste leads to hell."
"But when there is no contact with the stain of merit or demerit, what use is any of that? (84)"

body.text: yeṣāṃ viduṣāmapi dehādipramātṛtāgrahaḥ sāmprataṃ na vigalitaḥ svātmajñānacarcāyāṃ ca na tathā samāśvāsasteṣāmiṣṭāpūrtādidharmasaṃgrahaṃ kurvatāmadharmasaṃgrahaṃ vā prayāgāditīrthasevā maraṇāvasare kṣetraparigrahaḥ

children.translated_text: leads to merit,
to the attainment of the higher worlds — this is certain. Similarly,
"death at the dwelling of an outcaste" —
at a sinful place characterized by the house of an outcaste and the like,
"the course of death"
— the attainment of death —
leads to hell,

children.text: avīcyādinarakapātāyaiteṣāṃ kimiti na bhaveddehapramātṛtāgrahasya vidyamānatvāt / maraṇasthānānuguṇaṃ bhogamapi bhuktvā śubhāśubheṣu deheṣu jāyante punarmriyante cetyanavaratajanmamaraṇaprabandhā dehādyātmamānina evaṃprāyāḥ syuḥ / yasya punaḥ svātmajñānapratyavamarśadārḍhyāddehādipramātṛtābhimāno niḥśeṣeṇa vigalitastasya cinnabhaḥsvabhāvasya dharmādharmasvabhāvavāsanāsparśaprakṣaye vṛtte sati kiṃ tena / evaṃ sa yataḥ śubhāśubhakarmabhājāṃ tīrthādiparigrahastatastena tīrthasevādinā vimalasya jñānino nāstyupayogaḥ / yaduktaṃ mānave dharmaśāstre
children.translated_text: to falling into hells such as <s>Avīci</s> and others. Why would this not be so for them, since the identification with body as the subject is present? Having enjoyed experience in accordance with the place of death, they are born in auspicious or inauspicious bodies, and die again — those who identify with body and so forth would be of such a nature, in an unceasing succession of births and deaths. But for one whose identification with body and other limited subjectivity has completely dissolved due to the firmness of Self-knowledge and self-reflection, for one whose nature is like the sky of consciousness, when the exhaustion of the touch of <s>vāsanās</s> whose nature is <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> has occurred — what use is any of that? Thus since the adoption of sacred places and so forth is for those who partake of auspicious and inauspicious <s>karma</s>, therefore pilgrimage to sacred places and so forth is of no use for the stainless <s>jñānin</s>. As stated in the <s>Mānava Dharmaśāstra</s>:

body.translated_text: For those who, even though learned, have not yet shed the identification with body and other limited subjectivity, and who have not achieved such firm confidence in the practice of Self-knowledge — for them, while accumulating <s>dharma</s> (merit) through acts of public and private charity, or accumulating <s>adharma</s> (demerit), pilgrimage to sacred places such as <s>Prayāga</s> and so forth, and the adoption of a sacred territory at the time of death,

children.text: yamo vaivasvato rājā yastavaiṣa hṛdi sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "King <s>Yama</s>, the son of <s>Vivasvat</s>, who is established in your heart —"

children.text: tena cedavivādastvaṃ mā gaṅgāṃ mā gayāṃ gamaḥ //
children.translated_text: "if you have no quarrel with him, do not go to the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, do not go to <s>Gayā</s>."

body.text: iti / atra dehātmamānitaiva hṛdayavartinī yamaḥ sā yaiḥ pūrṇasvātmamaheśvarasvabhāvamupalabhya saṃbhakṣitā teṣāṃ kathameṣa tīrthādisevāprayāsa iti siddhāntaḥ // 84 //
body.translated_text: Here, identification with body as the Self, dwelling in the heart, is <s>Yama</s>. Those who have consumed it by recognizing their own nature as the complete Self, the great Lord — for them, how could there be this exertion of pilgrimage and the like? This is the established conclusion. (84)

body.text: nanu prākpratipāditaṃ yathā jñānadagdhāṇavamāyīyakārmamalasvarūpa ātmā piṇḍapātātsvasvarūpastha eva na punarbhavaprarohaṃ vidhatte dagdhabījamivāṅkuramiti / svātmajñānāvirbhāvasamakālaṃ dehakañcukabhaṅgaścettarhyuttaratra mā vidhattāṃ yatpunarvidyamāne dehādikañcukabandhe kathaṅkāraṃ sa tadgatadharmācchurito na syāttadācchuritaḥ sanmṛtaḥ kathaṃ na saṃsārīti codyamapavadati
body.translated_text: Now, it was previously established that the Self, whose nature is the <s>āṇava</s>, <s>māyīya</s>, and <s>kārma</s> (action-born) impurities has been burnt by knowledge, upon the fall of the body, remains in its own true nature and does not produce any further growth of existence — like a burnt seed does not produce a sprout. If the breaking of the body-covering occurs simultaneously with the manifestation of Self-knowledge, then let there be no further growth. But as long as the bondage of the body-covering persists, how could he not be affected by the qualities pertaining to it? And if, being so affected, he dies, how is he not a <s>saṃsārin</s>? He answers this objection:

children.translated_text: "A grain of rice, well separated from its husk and chaff, even if thrown back among the husks,"
"does not again assume identity with them in their nature. (85)"
"Similarly, consciousness here, separated from the covering of sheaths, even though remaining due to residual impressions,"
"becomes a liberated Self, free from contact with them. (86)"
From the husk and chaff,
well,
separated,
detached — that which is a
grain of rice,
its
being thrown back among the husks —

children.text: prāgiva punastatraiva vinyāsaḥ sa yathā tuṣadalāntaraprakṣepaḥ
children.translated_text: being placed once again in the same position as before — just as that throwing back among the husks
does not produce in the grain of rice
— even though situated as if capable of generating a sprout in that form —
identity,
tight embrace;
it does not produce it.

children.text: ayaḥśalākāvadbhinnāveva tuṣataṇḍulau tiṣṭhato na punarekakāryajananavyagrau bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: Like an iron rod, the husk and rice remain separated and do not engage in producing a single effect.
So too,
in the same way, this
consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>)
— awareness —
from the covering of sheaths
— from the aggregate of sheaths such as the <s>āṇava</s> impurity and so forth —
separated,

children.text: ahameva svātmamaheśvarasvabhāvo viśvātmanā sarvadā sarvatra sphurāmīti svātmajñānapariśīlanadārḍhyātsamuddhṛtā
children.translated_text: 'I alone am of the nature of the great Lord, the Self; as the Self of all, I always pulsate everywhere' — extracted through the firmness of the cultivation of Self-knowledge,
here,
in this covering of sheaths, for some time through residual activity in the form of the body,
"even though remaining,"
being situated,
is a liberated Self,
whose bondage has been destroyed,
"becomes free from contact with them" —
of that covering of sheaths such as the body and so forth,
the contact —
the coloring, generated by <s>kārma</s> (action-born) impurity in the form of merit and demerit, which is capable of generating the sprout of <s>saṃsāra</s> — from that
she is free,

children.text: parihṛtā saṃpadyate yathā tuṣadalāntare kṣiptastaṇḍulo 'ṅkuraprarohasparśarahito bhavatīti / idamuktaṃ syādajñānakāraṇakastāvatsaṃsārastatra samuditasvātmajñānadalitakañcukasya yoginaḥ saṃvinna punaḥ saṃsāraheturajñānajanitasāmagrīvaikalyānnāpi tasya śeṣavartanayā saṃskāravaśena tiṣṭhannayaṃ dehakañcukabandho jñānāgnidagdhājñānamūlaḥ svagatadharmāvirbhāvena saṃsāraprarohaṃ dātumalamiti jñānī jīvanneva turīyarūpo dehābhāvātturyātītarūpa ityubhayathā punarna kācitsaṃsāraśaṅketi // 86 //
children.translated_text: she becomes released — just as a grain of rice thrown among the husks becomes free from the touch of sprouting. The meaning is: <s>saṃsāra</s> has ignorance as its cause; for the <s>yogin</s> whose sheaths have been destroyed by the Self-knowledge that has arisen therein, consciousness is no longer a cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, due to the incompleteness of the assemblage of conditions born of ignorance. Nor is this bondage of the body-covering, which remains through residual momentum due to <s>saṃskāras</s>, and whose root of ignorance has been burnt by the fire of knowledge, capable of producing the growth of <s>saṃsāra</s> through the manifestation of its own properties. Therefore, the <s>jñānin</s>, while living, is of the nature of <s>turīya</s> (the fourth); upon the absence of the body, of the nature of <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth) — thus in both ways, there is no suspicion of <s>saṃsāra</s> whatsoever. (86)

body.text: nanu śeṣavartanayā yāvaccharīrāvasthitaṃ yogisaṃvedanamadhigatasvasvarūpamapi dehopādhikṛtamālinyasyāpi tāvadaṃśena vidyamānatvādaśuddhameveti dṛṣṭāntena pariharati
body.translated_text: But the experience of the <s>yogin</s> during the residual period, even though it has attained its own true nature, is impure because of the impurity caused by the bodily adventitious condition still being present to that extent — he resolves this through an illustration:

children.translated_text: "A gem whose purity has been fashioned by a most skilled artisan, even though it appears soiled due to the adventitious condition of its casket,"
"when that adventitious condition is removed, is in reality pure and clear. (87)"
"Similarly, experience purified through the teaching of a true guru, though freed from the bodily adventitious condition,"
"appears as if devoid of any other adventitious condition — it shines as the form of <s>Śiva</s>. (88)"
a gem,
whose purity has been brought out by a most expert lapidary, yet because it has not been separated from its casket,
even though appearing soiled,
appears grayish — that very gem, however,
when the adventitious condition of the casket is removed,
when the particular covering is absent,
is in reality pure and clear —
it becomes of its pristine stainless nature.
In the same way,
by this very method, this
experience, purified through the teaching of a true <s>guru</s> —
one who has the knowledge of complete Self-realization, the supreme teacher, whose
teaching,

children.text: svātmajñānarahasyamukhāmnāyastasya pariśīlanena vigatā kālikārūpasyāṇavamalasya māyīyakārmamalabhittibhūtasya sthitiryasya tadevaṃvidhaṃ maulikamalaprakṣayānnabhorūpamapi vedanam
children.translated_text: the oral transmission of the secret of Self-knowledge — through the cultivation of which the persistence of the <s>āṇava</s> impurity, which is of the nature of a dark stain and which forms the foundation of the <s>māyīya</s> and <s>kārma</s> impurities, has been removed. Such experience, of the nature of sky, due to the exhaustion of the fundamental impurity, is
freed from the bodily adventitious condition — the body,
the bodily
adventitious condition,
the qualifying attribute — from that,
freed,
separated — due to the absence of any other qualifying attribute, that
shines as the form of <s>Śiva</s> —

children.text: dehabhaṅgātparamaśivatvena bhāsata iti yāvat / yathā samudgakopādhivirahānmaṇiḥ svasvarūpo bhāti tathaiva svasvarūpāvabodhādvimalamapyaśuddhābhimataśarīropādhikṣayādviśuddhameva saṃvedanaṃ bhāsate / nanu maṇiryathā samudgakopādhervimukto 'pi punaranyatamopādhiparigrahātsamalaḥ saṃpadyate tathaiva tanūpādhermuktamapi saṃvedanaṃ maṇivadupādhyantaraṃ cedgṛhṇāti tarhi punarapi sopādhitvādaśuddhameveti pariharati
children.translated_text: upon the dissolution of the body, it shines as supreme <s>Śiva</s>-hood. Just as a gem, freed from the adventitious condition of the casket, shines in its own true nature, so too experience, though stainless through the realization of its own true nature, upon the dissolution of the bodily adventitious condition, which was wrongly regarded as impure, shines as utterly pure. But just as a gem, even though freed from the adventitious condition of the casket, upon taking up another adventitious condition, becomes soiled again — would not experience similarly, even though freed from the bodily adventitious condition, become impure again if it takes up another adventitious condition, since it would again be conditioned? He addresses this:
"Even though devoid of any other adventitious condition" —

children.text: iti / na dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayoḥ sarvathā sāmyaṃ yataḥ piṇḍapātāttasya mahāprakāśavapuṣaḥ paramādvayarūpasya sarvamidamupādhyabhimataṃ svāṅgakalpaṃ bhāsate 'to vyatiriktasyopādhyantarasyābhāvānna punastadupādhyantareṇa viśiṣyata iti na maṇinopādhigrahaṇasya sāmyam / ajñānamūlaṃ kila śarīropādhigrahaṇaṃ taccetsvātmajñānakuṭhāreṇa dalitaṃ kathaṅkāraṃ punarupādhisaṃśrayo bhavet / yaduktam
children.translated_text: Thus — there is no complete similarity between the illustration and the thing illustrated, because from the falling of the body, all this [universe], superimposed through limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), shines as if a limb of that [Self] whose body is the great light, whose form is the supreme non-dual. Therefore, since there is no other limiting adjunct apart from [the body], it is not again qualified by another limiting adjunct — hence there is no similarity with the gem's acquisition of a limiting adjunct. The acquisition of the bodily limiting adjunct is indeed rooted in ignorance; if that [ignorance] has been cleft by the axe of self-knowledge, how could there again be resort to a limiting adjunct? As it is said:

body.translated_text: Just as
"Knowledge is covered by ignorance; thereby creatures are deluded."

children.translated_text: "But for those whose ignorance of the Self has been destroyed by knowledge,
Their knowledge, like the sun, illuminates that Supreme."

body.text: iti śrīgītāsu / tasmātsvasvarūpajñānādyoginaḥ svasaṃvedanaṃ sadaiva śuddhameveti // 88 //
body.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Gītā</s>. Therefore, from the knowledge of one's own true nature, the self-experience of the <s>yogin</s> is always pure alone. // 88 //

[Commentary:] He indicates that the ripening of mental impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — generated by a mind whose operations have been duly cultivated — is alone the cause of all arising of limiting adjuncts, and that nothing whatsoever comes anew:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] Through scripture and other valid means, with unwavering faith, having attained identity with that —

children.text: prāptaḥ sa eva pūrvaṃ svargaṃ narakaṃ manuṣyatvam // 89 //
children.translated_text: That very one [attains] previously [experienced] heaven, hell, or human state. // 89 //

body.text: āgamaprāmāṇyādgurūpadeśapāramparyakathanādyuktipariśīlanātprāgvāsanāprarūḍhayā śraddhayā vā svātmajñāna iṣṭāpūrte pāśave karmaṇi vā kṛtābhyāsaḥ pramātā tadaiva tatsaṃskārapraroheṇa

children.translated_text: 'having attained identity' —
having obtained the nature of each respective thing that was practiced,
'attained' —
being thus, subsequently, upon the fall of the body, in accordance with impressions,
'heaven' —
unsurpassed joy,
'hell' —
the suffering of <s>Avīci</s> and other [hells],
'human state' —

children.text: sukhaduḥkhobhayarūpaṃ manuṣyabhāvaṃ prāpnoti na punaranabhyastavāsanasyāpi puruṣasya dehapātādeva yatkiñcidāpatati / yataḥ sarvaḥ pramātā yenāśayena yadabhyasyati tadaiva sa tadrūpo bhavati kintu maraṇasamaye sphuṭatayā yadabhilaṣitaṃ vastu tatpramāturabhivyaktiṃ yātīti nābhyastavastunaḥ kadācidviparyayaḥ syānnāpyanabhyastavastusvarūpaṃ kiñcidapūrvatvenāpatediti sarvatra pūrvābhyāsa eva kāraṇamiti bhāvaḥ // 89 //
children.translated_text: the human condition consisting of both pleasure and pain — [that one] attains. But for a person in whom unpracticed impressions exist, nothing whatsoever befalls merely from the fall of the body. Because every perceiver, whatever disposition (<s>āśaya</s>) he practices, by that very [practice] he becomes of that nature. But at the time of death, whatever object is clearly desired, that manifests for the perceiver. Thus there is never a reversal for a thing that has been practiced, nor does the nature of an unpracticed thing ever arise as something new — therefore, in all cases, prior practice alone is the cause. This is the purport. // 89 //

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Through the authority of <s>āgama</s> (scripture), through the narration of the succession of the guru's instruction, through the cultivation of reasoning, or through faith rooted in the ripening of past impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — the perceiver who has practiced either self-knowledge, or ritual and meritorious works (<s>iṣṭāpūrta</s>), or actions in the <s>paśu</s> (bound) state — at that very [moment], through the sprouting of those impressions,

body.text: evaṃ sadā tadbhāvabhāvitatvaṃ svātmavido dehatyāgāvasare pūrṇaprathāheturna punarlokaparidṛśyaḥ puṇyāpuṇyarūpo maraṇāvasaraḥ kaścitsvarganirayādikāraṇaṃ parikalpanīyamityāha
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, since constant cultivation of that state is the cause of full manifestation for the knower of the Self at the time of departing the body, and since the moment of death — as commonly perceived, in the form of merit and demerit — is not to be imagined as a cause of heaven, hell, and such, he says:

children.text: antyaḥ kṣaṇastu tasminpuṇyāṃ pāpāṃ ca vā sthitiṃ puṣyan /
children.translated_text: [Verse:] But the final moment, nourishing either a meritorious or sinful condition,

children.text: mūḍhānāṃ sahakārībhāvaṃ gacchati gatau tu na sa hetuḥ // 90 //
children.translated_text: Becomes a contributing factor for the deluded; but for [the wise one's] departure, it is not the cause. // 90 //
[Verse:] Even animals, birds, reptiles, and others who know their own state as identical with That —
They too, sanctified by the impressions of prior awakening, attain that state. // 91 //
'the final moment' —

children.text: caramo dehavināśasahabhāvī kālo dhātudoṣavaśena duṣṭavyādhyanubhavādvā samīpasthitaiḥ pramātṛbhiranumitām
children.translated_text: the last time, concurrent with the destruction of the body, [arising] from the predominance of humoral imbalance or from the experience of severe disease, inferred by perceivers standing nearby as —
'nourishing either a meritorious or sinful condition' —
being attended by [such conditions],
'of the deluded' —
only of those perceivers who identify the body as the Self,
'a contributing factor' —
causality,
'becomes.' —

children.text: / gacchatu varāko naitāvatā nirbhagnadehātmamānitve sadā svātmamaheśvaranibhālanacature
children.translated_text: Let the poor [final moment] become [a cause for the deluded]; by that much, for one whose identification with the body and such has been always shattered, who is always skilled in beholding his own Self as the Great Lord —
'for that one' —
the <s>yogin</s>,
'it' —
the final moment,
'for departure' —
for the attainment of another body from [the present] body,
'is the cause' —
would be the cause. Showing whence this comes, he says:
'even those' —
thus.
'Even those' —

children.text: kenāpyāśayavaśena śāpādinā vā pāpayonayaḥ paśurūpatāmapi prāptāḥ
children.translated_text: who, by some disposition or by a curse and such, have entered sinful births and attained even the form of an animal,
'their own state' —
the state of the Self, at the time of death,
'as the Self' —
[if they] know [it],
'they' —

children.text: mūḍhāḥ santo 'pi prāgabhyastasvātmajñānavāsanāprabodhānugṛhītāḥ svātmasthitiṃ ca labhante / gajendramokṣaṇādau yathā hastinā paśusvabhāvenāpi satā prākpariśīlitaparameśvarabhaktisaṃskāraprabuddhena viṣṇuṃ bhagavantaṃ stutvā samyakkañcukaṃ vihāya svasvarūpamupalabdhaṃ kastatra smaraṇe heturabhūt / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ śarīrādyutthadhātudoṣavaśātkāṣṭhapāṣāṇaceṣṭo jñānī puṇyaṃ pāpamālabiḍālādikaṃ vā yatkiñcitpralapandehaṃ tyajati naitāvatā svasthaceṣṭatayā yadabhyastaṃ jñānādikaṃ tasya vipralopaḥ syāccharīrādigatā dharmāḥ śarīrādāveva nipatanti na punaḥ sadā bhāvitaṃ vastu sthagayituṃ prabhavantītyāmaraṇakṣaṇaṃ sarvatra prarūḍhireva paramārthaḥ / yathā gītāsūktam
children.translated_text: even though deluded, being favored by the awakening of the impressions of self-knowledge practiced in the past, attain the state of their own Self. As in the episode of the liberation of <s>Gajendra</s> (the elephant king): even though the elephant was of animal nature, having been awakened by the impressions of devotion to the Supreme Lord cultivated in a prior [life], having praised the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he properly cast off the covering [of ignorance] and attained his own true nature — what was the cause of that remembrance? The purport is this: the knower, whose body has become inert like wood or stone due to humoral imbalance arising from the body and such, [may] utter some meritorious or sinful [words], or [speak of] cats and crows and such, and [while] babbling thus departs the body — by that much, there is no destruction of the knowledge and such that was practiced while in a sound state. Properties belonging to the body and such fall upon the body and such alone; they are not able to obstruct what has always been cultivated. Thus, the ripening [of impressions] that has always been present up to the moment of death is in all cases the ultimate reality. As stated in the <s>Gītā</s>:

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, with regard to the knower who has been described,

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram /
children.translated_text: "Whatever state one remembers when abandoning the body at the end,
That very state one attains, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, being always absorbed in that state."

body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.translated_text: "To those who are constantly united, who worship with love,

children.text: dadāmi buddhiyogaṃ taṃ yena māmupayānti te //
children.translated_text: I grant that <s>buddhiyoga</s> (yoga of understanding) by which they come to Me."

body.translated_text: Thus, it is the cultivation of the inner faculty that is alone the cause of granting the final destination. // 91 //

body.text: evaṃ darśitadṛṣṭyā yataḥ sadā tadbhāvabhāvitatvamapahastya nūtanatvena śarīravināśe nāpūrvaṃ kiñcitsamāpatejjñānino yato deha eva vināśī kevalaṃ sa eva vinaśyati na punarvāsanāpraroha iti darśayannāha
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, since constant cultivation of that state prevails, setting aside [the notion of] anything new — at the destruction of the body, nothing unprecedented befalls the knower — since the body alone is perishable and it alone perishes, not the sprouting of impressions — showing this, he says:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] The person dwelling within the body is heaven-natured or hell-natured;
Upon its (the body's) destruction, by his own propriety, he attains connection with another body. // 92 //
[Verse:] Thus, at the moment of knowledge, whatever form the Self has once appeared in to him —

children.text: tādṛśa eva tadāsau na dehapāte 'nyathā bhavati // 93 //
children.translated_text: Of that very form it remains; at the fall of the body, it does not become otherwise. // 93 //
'That' —
therefore, the person dwelling in the body-pot and such,
'the person' —

the Self of everyone, perfumed by the impurity of <s>karma</s> (<s>kārmamala</s>), whose inner faculty is perfumed by the impressions of the fruits of actions done with prior intent toward heaven and such,
'heaven-natured' —

children.text: prarūḍhasvargaphalavāsanāviśiṣṭatvātsvargaphalabhokteti yāvat / evaṃ duṣkṛtapūrvakarmavāsanāprarūḍho narakaphalabhoktā kevalaṃ deha ubhayakarmaphalabhogāyatanam
children.translated_text: because of being distinguished by the fully developed impressions of heavenly fruition, [he is] an enjoyer of heavenly fruit — this is the meaning. Similarly, one in whom the impressions of prior evil deeds have developed is an enjoyer of hellish fruit. The body alone is the receptacle for the enjoyment of the fruits of both [kinds of] actions.
'Upon its destruction, by his own propriety' —
thus, upon the perishing of that body,
'of oneself' —

children.text: ātmano yathāhitavāsanānuguṇyādanyena bhogāyatanena śarīrāntareṇa samanantaraṃ saṃbandhamupayātyuttarakālaṃ yena viśiṣṭakarmavāsanādattaphalabhogabhāgī bhavati / tathaiva
children.translated_text: of the Self, in accordance with one's own deposited impressions, one immediately enters into connection with another receptacle of enjoyment, i.e., another body, by which in the subsequent time one becomes the partaker of the fruit bestowed by the particular karmic impressions. Likewise,
'at the moment of knowledge' —
at the time of the illumination of one's own Self as taught by the guru to the student,
'the Self' —
consciousness,
'once' —
at a single instance,
'whatever' —
of whatever kind,
'has appeared' —

children.text: upadeśakramānusāreṇa paripūrṇasvātantryalakṣaṇāṃ mitāṃ vā parāmarśadaśāṃ gataḥ

children.text: / na hi bhātamabhātaṃ syādaparathā na kaścitkiñcidabhyasediti sarvavyavahāravipralopo bhavet
children.translated_text: For what has shone cannot become un-shone; otherwise, no one would practice anything, and all worldly activity would collapse.
"By <s>dharma</s> (virtue), one goes upward; by <s>adharma</s> (vice), one goes downward;
By knowledge, there is liberation; from its opposite, bondage is taught."

body.text: ityādi sarvaṃ ca truṭyettasmānmaraṇakāle śarīraṃ yathāstu tathāstu kevalaṃ vāsanāprarohaḥ svātmagataḥ sarvasya bandhe mokṣe ca heturiti // 93 //
body.translated_text: All this and such [teachings] would be rendered false. Therefore, at the time of death, let the body be however it may be — only the sprouting of impressions belonging to one's own Self is the cause of both bondage and liberation for everyone. // 93 //

body.text: yadi punardhātuvaiṣamyāccharīre maraṇavyathopalabdhiḥ syānnaitāvatābhyāsaprarohe kācitkṣatirityāveditāmeva sthitimupalabdhuṃ parighaṭayate
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] If, however, due to humoral imbalance, there is an experience of suffering in the body at the time of death — even so, there is no harm whatsoever to the sprouting of [prior] practice. To establish this very position, he elaborates:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] Loss of the group of sense-organs, loss of memory, being choked with breath, severance
At the vital points, specific pains — this is the experience born of the body's constitution. // 94 //

children.text: sa kathaṃ vigrahayoge sati na bhavettena mohayoge 'pi /
children.translated_text: [Verse:] How would that not occur when there is connection with a body? Yet even when there is such delusion,
The knower at the time of death does not fall from the ultimate reality of the Self. // 95 //
[Commentary:] 'Of the group of sense-organs' —
of the thirteen-fold [organs], both external and internal, the complete
'loss' —

children.text: svarūpavipralopo yathā cakṣurādīnīndriyāṇi rūpādiviṣayālocanāyāṃ na pragalbhante vāgādikarmendriyāṇyapyevaṃ vacanādānādau na pravartante nāpi buddhiryathārthamarthamadhyavasyati manaso 'navasthitirahaṅkāro 'pi madhye madhye saṃskāratayāste / tathā
children.translated_text: destruction of their proper functioning: the sense-organs such as the eye and others are not capable of perceiving objects such as form and others; the organs of action such as speech and others likewise do not function in speaking, grasping, and such; nor does the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) determine objects correctly; the mind (<s>manas</s>) is unstable; and even the ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) exists intermittently in a latent state. Likewise,
'loss of memory' —

children.text: anubhūtaviṣayasya saṃpramoṣo bandhubhirarthyamāno 'pi mumūrṣuḥ puro 'vasthitaṃ vastu śataśo 'nubhūtamapi na pratyabhijānātyata eva sadā tadbhāvabhāvitatvaṃ vinā brahmavidyādikathanamantakāle dānamanyatkiñcidvā tasyāmavasthāyāṃ nabhaścitramiva na citte prarohati kintu taditikartavyatāmātraṃ kāryamiti niyogaḥ / tathā
children.translated_text: the obliteration of a previously experienced object: even when beseeched by relatives, the dying person does not recognize an object placed before him, [even one] experienced a hundred times. Therefore, without constant cultivation of that state, the utterance of <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>) and such, or charity or anything else at the time of death — in that [final] state, like a painting in the sky, does not take root in the mind. But merely the prescribed duty of doing that much should be done — this is the injunction. Likewise,

'specific pains' —
fever, dysentery, and such. Thus, this
'of the body' —
of the covering of elements (<s>bhūtakañcuka</s>), due to the imbalance of the humors — <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) —

'not occur?' —
It would indeed occur.
'Yet by that' —
reason,
'the knower' —

who has always trampled underfoot the identification with the body and such, and who has entered into the state of the Great Lord as his own Self — even when connected with bodily ignorance produced at the moment of death,
'from the ultimate reality of the Self' —
from the true nature of the fully developed reflective awareness of consciousness,
'does not fall' —

children.text: nānyathābhāvaṃ yāti / yato 'sau jñānī nyakkṛtadehasaṃbandho na tajjena bhogena tanmayīkartuṃ pāryate kevalaṃ lokavacceccharīrapātasamanantaraṃ kṣaṇaṃ nopalabhata ityetāvatā tasya svasthahṛdayasya svasaṃkalpitābhiprāyeṇa svasthaceṣṭatayābhyastabhagavadbhakterna kiñcidapūrvaṃ samāpatati tasmājjñānī svātmaprathāsamanantarameva mukto na śarīrasaṃskāro 'sya bandhadāyīti śataśaḥ prākpratipāditam / yastu sadā dehātmamānī puṇyapāpamayaḥ sa kathaṃ dehasaṃskārodbhūtasukhaduḥkhādibhogajanitaṃ tanmayatvaṃ nāyāti / yaduktam
children.translated_text: does not undergo alteration. Because that knower, having subdued the connection with the body, cannot be made one with the bodily experience. Only, as in the world, [when] the moment immediately after the fall of the body is not perceived — by that much, for one of steady heart, who has practiced devotion to the Lord in a composed state with self-willed purpose — nothing unprecedented befalls him. Therefore, the knower is liberated immediately upon the manifestation of his own Self; the bodily constitution does not bring him bondage — this has been established hundreds of times before. But one who always identifies with the body, who is of the nature of merit and demerit — how would he not arrive at identity with the experiences of pleasure and pain born from the bodily constitution? As it is said:

children.text: yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt /
children.translated_text: "When the embodied one meets dissolution while <s>sattva</s> (goodness) predominates,
Then he attains the stainless worlds of those who know the highest."

body.text: ityādi / sattvādayo guṇāḥ prakṛtidharmāstanmayasyaiva niyantraṇāṃ vidadhate yena punastato viviktatayā pariśīlitā na taṃ pratyete kecaneti jñānino 'nya eva panthāḥ / ye punaradṛṣṭagurucaraṇāḥ paśupramātāraste svagatāndharmānanyatrāpādayanti / yathā yadyayaṃ jñānī syātkimiti vyādhyādyupahataśarīro bhuṅkte paridadhāti ca yadi vā maraṇasamaye jāḍyamāyātaḥ smṛtamanena na kiñcidityevaṃ bahuprakāramavidyopahatatvādvivadamānāśca kena paryanuyujyantām / yadyayaṃ jñānī syāddehadharmasaṃskārayuktaśca bhavetkimetāvatā ca tasya duṣyet / jñāninaḥ svātmaprakāśastattadavasthāvicitro 'pi svātmaprakāśa eva na punastasya svātmānubhavitṛtayā vipralopaḥ syādyena jñānaṃ naśyet / pūrṇaṣāḍguṇyamahimāpi bhagavānvāsudevaḥ kṛṣṇāvatāre vyādhaśarāghātajanitavyatho bhūtaśarīraṃ tyaktavānityevaṃ kṛtvā kiṃ tasya jagatprabhoḥ svasvarūpavipralopo 'bhūdityā kīṭātsadāśivāntasyāpi dehasaṃskāra etādṛśa eva kintvekaḥ svātmapratyavamarśamātrasanāthadeho 'parastu dehādyātmamānitāsatattva itīyānviśeṣaḥ / tasmāccharīradharmā jñānyajñāninoḥ sadṛśā eva naitāvatā phalasāmyamityetadeva gītāsūktam
body.translated_text: And so on. The <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) — <s>sattva</s> and the rest — being properties of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), impose regulation only on one who is constituted by them; but for one who has cultivated [the Self] as distinct from them, these [qualities] have no [binding] effect whatsoever — thus the path of the <s>jñānin</s> (knower) is altogether different. But those who are <s>paśu-pramātṛs</s> (bound subjects), who have not beheld the feet of the <s>Guru</s>, superimpose their own [conditioned] dharmas onto others. For example: 'If this person were truly a <s>jñānin</s>, why does he eat and clothe himself while afflicted by disease and the like in the body? Or if at the time of death stupor has set in and he remembers nothing' — disputing in many such ways due to being afflicted by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), by whom should they be interrogated? Even if this person were a <s>jñānin</s> and were endowed with the bodily <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioning), what would be vitiated thereby? The <s>jñānin</s>'s self-luminosity, though variegated by various states, remains self-luminosity itself; there is no destruction of his nature as self-experiencer by which knowledge would perish. Even the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, possessing the glory of the full six divine attributes, in the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-incarnation abandoned his embodied form due to the pain caused by the hunter's arrow-strike — having done so, was there any loss of his own essential nature for that Lord of the universe? Thus, from the insect up to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the bodily conditioning is of exactly this nature; the only difference is that one [the jñānin] has a body sustained merely by the reflective awareness of the Self, while the other [the ignorant] has an unreal [identification] where the body and the like are mistaken for the Self. Therefore, the bodily <s>dharmas</s> are identical for both the <s>jñānin</s> and the <s>ajñānin</s> — but this does not entail equality of result. This very [teaching] is stated in the <s>Gītā</s>:

children.translated_text: Even the one who possesses knowledge acts in accordance with his own nature (<s>prakṛti</s>);

children.text: prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: beings follow [their] nature — what will restraint accomplish?

body.text: idānīmakrameṇa krameṇa ca jñānayogapariśīlane vicitraparaśaktipātameva kāraṇaṃ pratipādayanphalabhedamāha
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating that the varied descent of the supreme power (<s>paraśaktipāta</s>) is itself the cause for the cultivation of knowledge-yoga both instantaneously and gradually, [the author] states the distinction of results:

children.translated_text: When one suddenly receives this path of supreme reality from the mouth of the <s>Guru</s>,
due to the most intense descent of power (<s>atitīvra-śaktipāta</s>), at that very moment one becomes <s>Śiva</s>, without any obstacle. // 96 //
from the mouth of the <s>Guru</s> —
from the mouth of the most excellent preceptor (<s>daiśika</s>),
this —
which has been expounded hundreds of times,
the path of supreme reality —

receives —

at that very moment —
at that very occasion, immediately after the <s>Guru</s>'s instruction, having removed all obstacles,

he becomes [<s>Śiva</s>]. As stated in the <s>Śrīkula</s>:

body.translated_text: At the very time when a person in his final birth,

children.translated_text: 'Whether playfully, sportively, or with reverence, the knower of reality,
upon whomsoever he casts his gaze, that person is liberated at that very instant, O Beloved!'
'Due to the most intense descent of power (<s>atitīvra-śaktipāta</s>)' —
that is, exceedingly

power (<s>śakti</s>) known as grace (<s>anugraha</s>) —

children.text: paśuhṛtkamalāvataraṇaṃ yena paśurapi gurvāmnāyavedanācchivībhavati jīvanneva mukta iti yāvat / yathā tāmradravyaṃ siddharasapātātsuvarṇībhavati / ayamarthaḥ parameśvarānugrahopāya eva svātmajñānalābha iti nātra niyatiśaktisamutthaṃ japadhyānayajñādikamupāyatayā kramate / anugrahaśaktividdhahṛdayasya tu haṭhādevākramaṃ devatāmukhāmnāyarahasyaṃ hṛdayamāvarjayati yena jhaṭityeva parameśvarībhāvaṃ yātītyaparyanuyojyo vicitraḥ pārameśvaraḥ śaktipāta iti // 96 //
children.translated_text: the descent into the lotus of the <s>paśu</s>'s (bound soul's) heart, by which even a bound soul becomes <s>Śiva</s> through the knowledge received from the <s>Guru</s>'s tradition, becoming liberated while still alive — that is the meaning. Just as a copper substance becomes gold through the application of the alchemical elixir (<s>siddharasa</s>). The meaning is this: the means of the Supreme Lord's grace is itself the attainment of Self-knowledge; therefore, <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), and the like, which arise from the power of <s>niyati</s> (destiny), do not function as means here. But for one whose heart has been pierced by the power of grace, the secret of the deity's oral tradition (<s>mukhāmnāya</s>) forcefully and without gradual stages captivates the heart, by which one instantly attains the state of the Supreme Lord — thus the variegated descent of the Lord's power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) is beyond question. // 96 //

body.translated_text: Now, how could one impart such a secret of the oral tradition? [The author] says:

body.text: yasya punarmadhyamandamandatarādibhedena pravṛttaḥ śaktipātastasya gurūpadeśamāmaraṇakṣaṇaṃ yāvadyogakrameṇa vimṛśataḥ piṇḍapātācchivatvaṃ syāditi pratipādayati
body.translated_text: For one, however, whose <s>śaktipāta</s> has occurred in the distinctions of medium, mild, milder, and so forth, by contemplating through the gradual stages of yoga from the <s>Guru</s>'s instruction up to the moment of death, <s>Śiva</s>-nature would arise from the fall of the body — [the author] demonstrates this:

children.translated_text: For one who ascends to the form that transcends everything through the gradual steps of the ladder (<s>sopāna</s>),
upon attaining establishment in the supreme reality, at the end, [there is] becoming one with <s>Śiva</s>. // 97 //
the form that transcends everything —
that whose nature extends to the farthest limit of all <s>tattvas</s> (principles),
ascending to —

'Through the gradual steps of the ladder (<s>sopāna-pada-krama</s>)' —
that is, the
steps of the ladder —

the <s>kanda</s> (bulb), <s>nābhi</s> (navel), <s>hṛt</s> (heart), <s>kaṇṭha</s> (throat), <s>lampikā</s> (uvula), <s>bindu</s>, <s>nāda</s>, and <s>śakti</s> — these are the sacred fords (<s>tīrtha</s>) for ascending upward; their
station (<s>pada</s>) —

children.text: śanaiḥśanaiḥ kande tato nābhau tato hṛdītyevamākramaṇaṃ teneti / evaṃ yāvatparamārthaprarohopalabdhau piṇḍapātāvasare yoginastasya krameṇa śivatāsvabhāvā sthitirbhavatītyeṣā kramayuktiḥ kathitā // 97 //
children.translated_text: slowly, from the <s>kanda</s>, then to the <s>nābhi</s>, then to the heart — ascending in this manner. Thus, when the sprouting of supreme reality is attained at the time of the fall of the body, for that <s>yogin</s>, the state of <s>Śiva</s>-nature gradually becomes established — this is the method of gradual progression that has been stated. // 97 //

body.translated_text: Thus indeed, due to the mildness of <s>śaktipāta</s>, without having attained the complete instruction of knowledge,

body.text: evamapi kramayogamabhyasyato yoginaḥ samāśvastasyāpi satastathārūḍhirna syādabhīṣṭaprāptāvantarāyo jāyate yadi paramanāsāditatattvasya maraṇaṃ syāttadā kiṃ bhavedityāśaṅkāṃ pariharati
body.translated_text: Even for the <s>yogin</s> who practices such gradual yoga and is thus reassured, if such ascent does not occur — if an obstacle arises in attaining the desired goal, and if death comes for one who has not attained the reality — then what would happen? [The author] dispels this doubt:

children.translated_text: For one who has not reached the stream that consists of supreme reality, who has paused midway,
even for one whose mind is eager to attain that state — death may sometimes occur. // 98 //
The one fallen from yoga (<s>yogabhraṣṭa</s>), as described in scripture, becomes lord of realms of various enjoyments;
by the force of the station of repose, having [remained there], in the next birth he becomes <s>Śiva</s>. // 99 //
'paused midway' —
having attained experience at some point even in the <s>cakrādhāra</s> (base center) and having become satisfied with just that — therefore
'not having reached the stream of supreme reality' —

children.text: paratattvarūpāṃ pratijñātāṃ daśāṃ sarvādhvottīrṇāmaprāptavato yadi vā
children.translated_text: not having attained the state of the nature of the supreme <s>tattva</s> (principle), the promised condition that transcends all paths; or alternatively,
'even for one whose mind is eager to attain that state' —
even for one who has the desire to attain the promised reality of supreme existence,
'sometimes' —

children.text: madhye vipattiḥ saṃbhāvyate tadaitasyālabdhalābhasyāpi piṇḍapātātkā gatirityāha
children.translated_text: a calamity in the middle is conceivable — then, for this one who has not attained what was to be attained, what is the destiny upon the fall of the body? [The author] says:
'The one fallen from yoga (<s>yogabhraṣṭa</s>)' —
and so on. He,
from yoga —
from <s>samādhi</s>, in both ways,
fallen —
dislodged,
in scripture —

is described —

'lord' (<s>pati</s>) —

children.text: īśvaro bhavati maraṇasamanantarameva divyairbhogairyujyata iti yāvat / tadbhogādhikāraparikṣaye punarapi sa yogabhraṣṭaḥ kathaṃ syādityāha

'Repose' (<s>viśrānti</s>) —
and so on.
'Of the station of repose' —
of the location such as the <s>kanda</s> (bulb) and the like,
'by the force' —
by the potency of the awakening of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) from the practice of that [yoga], he,

children.text: saṃsāre 'dhikāriśarīraṃ yogābhyāsayogyaṃ prāpya pūrvābhyastaṃ yogaṃ prayāsena svīkṛtya helayā paramārthamayīṃ prāgjanmapratijñātāṃ daśāmadhiruhya piṇḍapātācchiva eva bhavati // 99 //
children.translated_text: having obtained in <s>saṃsāra</s> a qualified body suitable for the practice of yoga, having taken up with effort the yoga previously practiced, and then effortlessly ascending to the state of supreme reality that was promised in the prior birth, upon the fall of the body he becomes <s>Śiva</s> himself. // 99 //

body.translated_text: Thus, for one who practices yoga through the method of ascending, due to some obstacle,

body.text: athābhyasyato 'pi yogaṃ yogino manaścāñcalyādviśrāntimekadeśe 'pi manāgapyalabhamānasya yogaṃ prati śraddhāvataśca piṇḍapātātkā gatiḥ syādityāha
body.translated_text: Now, even for a <s>yogin</s> who practices yoga, if due to mental fickleness he does not attain repose even slightly in any single location, yet has faith in yoga — what would be his destiny upon the fall of the body? [The author] says:

children.translated_text: Indeed, even one who has practiced this path of supreme reality without attaining yoga,
partaking of the enjoyments of the divine realms, with a joyful mind, he rejoices for a long time. // 100 //

children.text: viṣayeṣu sārvabhaumaḥ sarvajanaiḥ pūjyate yathā rājā /

'Sovereign' (<s>sārva</s>) —

span of time,

children.text: sa yogabhraṣṭaḥ saṃsāre 'sminmanuṣyabhāvamāgatya yogābhyāsasādhanayogyaṃ śarīramāsādya prāgjanmani manaścāñcalyādyo yogo duṣprāpo 'bhūttameva
children.translated_text: that <s>yogabhraṣṭa</s> (one fallen from yoga), having come to human existence in this <s>saṃsāra</s>, having obtained a body suitable as an instrument for the practice of yoga — the very yoga that in the prior birth was difficult to attain due to mental fickleness — that same
yoga,
through the effortless awakening of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) of the yoga-<s>vāsanā</s> (dispositions) developed from the faith and devotion born in the prior life,
having attained —
having fully practiced, and at the end of the body,
'the divine nectar' (<s>divyam amṛtam</s>) —

children.text: paratattvasvarūpamupalabhate parasvarūpatādārḍhyaṃ gacchatīti yāvat / ata eva tasmātpunarāvartanaṃ tasya na syāditi / evaṃ mahati kalyāṇe svātmajñānaviṣaye manāgapi pratyavamarśaḥ saṃsārasaraṇāya na bhavati / yaduktaṃ śrīgītāsu
children.translated_text: he realizes the nature of the supreme <s>tattva</s> (reality), he attains firmness in the supreme nature — that is the meaning. Therefore there is no return from that for him. Thus, in this great blessedness regarding Self-knowledge, even a slight reflective awareness does not lead to continued wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>. As stated in the blessed <s>Gītā</s>:

body.translated_text: Having enjoyed the pleasures in the divine realms as described, after an exceedingly long

children.translated_text: 'In this there is no loss of endeavor, nor is there any adverse effect;
even a little of this <s>dharma</s> protects from great fear.'

body.translated_text: And also:

children.translated_text: 'The one who has fallen [from yoga], endowed with faith, whose mind has deviated from yoga,
not having attained the perfection of yoga...'

body.translated_text: Beginning from this question [in the <s>Gītā</s>],
'Perfected through many births, he then attains the supreme goal.'

body.text: ityuttaraparyanto grantho muninā pratipādito 'pi smartavya iti // 102 //
body.translated_text: The passage up to this concluding answer, as expounded by the Sage [<s>Vyāsa</s>], should also be recalled. // 102 //

body.text: evamanena jñānayogakrameṇa jantormanāgapi spṛṣṭasya sata iyānvibhūtyatiśayo yaḥ pravaktuṃ na pāryate tasmātsarvātmanā vivekārdrahṛdayairjananamaraṇanivṛttau sāvadhānairbhāvyamiti nirūpayati
body.translated_text: Thus, for a being even slightly touched by this method of knowledge-yoga, the extent of glorious abundance is such that it cannot be fully expressed; therefore, with hearts moistened by discrimination, one should be attentive to the cessation of birth and death — [the author] establishes this:

children.translated_text: Therefore, whoever is devoted to this noble path attains <s>Śiva</s>-nature;
having understood this, one should strive toward the supreme reality by whatever means possible. // 103 //
'therefore' —
on this most excellent
'path' —
the way that leads to the most eminent liberation,
'whoever is devoted' —
thus the absence of restriction regarding [eligible] practitioners is shown.
'Whoever' —
any person, tormented by hundreds of afflictions such as birth, death, disease, and the like,
'devoted' —

children.text: vivekabuddhyā niḥśeṣeṇa ratastatraiva śraddadhāno bhūtvā nimagnaḥ
children.translated_text: with discriminating intellect, completely absorbed therein, having become one who has faith in it, immersed,
'that person' —
that being, before long, in a short span of time,
'attains <s>Śiva</s>-nature' —

children.text: sakalasāṃsārikakleśānavadhūya paraśreyorūpadaśāmekenaiva janmanā prāpnoti / yathā śivadharmottare śāstre
children.translated_text: having shaken off all afflictions of <s>saṃsāra</s>, attains the state whose nature is the supreme good — in a single lifetime. As [stated] in the <s>Śivadharmo­ttara</s> scripture:

body.translated_text: Since thus the practice of reflective awareness of the Self, through the gradual stages that have been set forth, yields the highest result,

children.translated_text: 'This liberation in a single existence — let it first be examined;
the liberation that takes many existences — who among you can prevent [that]?'
'Having understood this' —
having reflected thus, in that
'supreme reality, by whatever means' —
by whatever manner,
'one should strive.'

children.text: prakarṣeṇa samudyamaḥ kāryaḥ / pradhāne yatnaḥ phalavāniti kṛtvātrārthe manāgapyavalepo na vidheyo yena yogābhyāsena svātmaprarūḍhiścetsamutpannā siddhaṃ naḥ samīhitaṃ na ceddivyalokāntaraprāptiḥ / tato 'pi pratyāvṛttasya prāksamabhyastayogavāsanāprabodhabalena punarapi yogasaṃbandha iti śreyomārgapariśīlanānna viruddhaṃ kiñcitkartuḥ samāpatatīti paramapuruṣārthasādhanāyāṃ manāgapyavalepo na kārya iti śivam // 103 //
children.translated_text: the utmost effort must be made. Effort directed toward the principal [goal] is fruitful — therefore, in this matter, not even the slightest negligence should be indulged, [thinking:] 'If through the practice of yoga the growth into one's own Self arises, then our aspiration is accomplished; if not, there will be attainment of another divine world. Even having returned from that [divine world], by the force of the awakening of the latent impressions of yoga previously practiced, there will again be connection with yoga.' Thus, since nothing contrary befalls one who assiduously cultivates the path of the highest good, not even the slightest negligence should be committed in the pursuit of the supreme aim of human existence. May there be auspiciousness! // 103 //

body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: evaṃ śāstrakāraḥ śeṣabhaṭṭārakoktaṃ paramārthasāropadeśaṃ śivādvayaśāsanakrameṇa yuktyanubhavāgamasanāthaṃ pratipādya svātmanaḥ paritoṣamātrārthitayā svābhidhānapradarśanapūrvakamayamevopadeśaḥ parapuruṣārthasādhanopāya iti nirūpayangranthārthopasaṃhāramāha
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, the author of the treatise, having established — supported by reasoning, experience, and scripture — the teaching of the essence of the supreme reality as stated by <s>Śeṣa Bhaṭṭāraka</s>, through the method of the non-dual <s>Śiva</s> teaching, and desiring nothing more than his own satisfaction, having first displayed his own name, determines that this very teaching is the means for accomplishing the supreme aim of others, and states the conclusion of the treatise's meaning:

children.translated_text: [Verse:] For one who meditates upon this concise [work] proclaimed by <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> —
the state of <s>Śiva</s> approaches before long, through immersion in one's own heart. // 104 //
[Commentary:] 'This' (<s>idam</s>) —
that which has been set forth at length and established; that which is
'supreme' (<s>param</s>) —
excellent,
'<s>Brahman</s>' —
one's own essential Self-nature, consisting of perfect bliss, because of its expansive nature (<s>bṛṃhakatva</s>) —
'for one who meditates' (<s>dhyāyataḥ</s>) —
for the person who effortlessly reflects upon it in his own Self,
'before long' (<s>acirāt</s>) —

children.text: śīghrameva na tu punarbahūnāṃ janmanāmanta iti / tadevaṃvidhasya brahmabhūtasya
children.translated_text: very quickly indeed, and not after many lifetimes. Thus, for one who has become of such a nature — who has become <s>Brahman</s> —
'the state of <s>Śiva</s> approaches' (<s>śivatvam abhyeti</s>) —
the attainment of the highest good becomes possible. How?
'Through immersion in one's own heart' (<s>nijahṛdayāveśam</s>) —
having performed,
'one's own heart' (<s>nijaṃ hṛdayam</s>) —
having entered the seat of reflective awareness (<s>parāmarśa</s>). Of what kind is that <s>Brahman</s>? By the name worthy of proclamation:
'proclaimed by <s>Abhinavagupta</s>' (<s>abhinavaguptenoditaḥ</s>) —
illuminated,
'concise' (<s>saṃkṣepaḥ</s>) —

children.text: tātparyaṃ yatra tadevaṃvidham / atra ca nāmavyājenedamapyuktaṃ syādyathā
children.translated_text: the purport — that is of such a nature. And here, by the device of the name, this too may be implied:
'<s>abhinava</s>' (novel) —
that which is unseen by others — the surpassing secret of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>;
'and <s>gupta</s>' (hidden) —
as if concealed, it remained thus;
'<s>udita</s>' (arisen) —
illuminated —
'the concise [teaching]' (<s>saṃkṣepaḥ</s>) —

children.text: yatra tadevaṃvidhaṃ brahmeti / evamāvedayatā durlabhatopadeśasya pratipāditā syāt // 104 //
children.translated_text: that is of such a nature — that <s>Brahman</s>. Thus, by declaring [the teaching] in this way, the rarity of the teaching is established. // 104 //
[Verse:] This essence of the teaching, exceedingly profound, has been condensed in a hundred <s>āryā</s> verses
by me, <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, who am ablaze with the remembrance of <s>Śiva</s>'s feet. // 105 //

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Determining the extent of the treatise, he states the authorship of this work:

children.translated_text: 'This essence of the teaching' (<s>idaṃ śāstrasāram</s>) —
that which is the excellent true reality of many treatises — that
'has been condensed by me' (<s>mayā saṃkṣiptam</s>) —

children.text: granthasahasrairapyupapādayitumaśakyaṃ tadeva laghunā vṛttaśataparimāṇena svīkṛtyoktamityanena pratibhākauśalamuktaṃ bhavet / kīdṛśeṇa mayā
children.translated_text: that which could not be established even by thousands of treatises has been taken up and stated in a brief compass of a hundred verses — by this, the skill of [his] creative intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) is expressed. By whom?
'ablaze with the remembrance of <s>Śiva</s>'s feet' (<s>śivacaraṇasmaraṇadīptena</s>) —
that is,
'of <s>Śiva</s>' —
whose nature is the supreme good, who abides in one's own Self, whose sole form is consciousness and bliss — His
'feet' (<s>caraṇāni</s>) —
the rays of consciousness — their
'remembrance' (<s>smaraṇam</s>) —
beholding at the moment of apprehending sense-objects such as sound and the like; the non-lapsing of self-experience at every moment — by that
'ablaze' (<s>dīpta</s>) —

children.text: parāhantācamatkārabhāsvaro 'ta eva kīrtanīyābhidhānena / anyathā kathaṃ dehādyātmamānino 'jñātasvātmamaheśvarasatattvasyeyati mahārthopadeśe 'sya kartṛtādhikāritvamupapadyate yato yo yatsvabhāvaḥ sa tatsvabhāvaṃ vivektuṃ pragalbhata ityupadeṣṭuḥ samāviṣṭamaheśvarasvabhāvo 'nena vākyenoktaḥ syāditi śivam // 105 //
children.translated_text: radiant with the splendor of the supreme I-consciousness (<s>parāhantā-camatkāra</s>) — hence [he is designated] by a name worthy of proclamation. Otherwise, how could someone who identifies with the body and the like, who does not know the true reality of the great Lord as his own Self, have the authority and competence to author such a teaching of great import? Since whoever is of a particular nature is bold enough to expound that nature — by this statement, the author is declared to be of the nature of one immersed in the great Lord. May there be auspiciousness! // 105 //

body.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Paramārthasāra</s>, composed by the eminent master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, the foremost teacher among the great Māheśvara teachers.

children.translated_text: [Colophon verse:] By me, the pupil of the blessed <s>Kṣemarāja</s>, who possesses the lineage of true teachers,
who has directly realized the great Lord, // 1 //
a renunciant ascetic from the blessed abode of <s>Vitastāpurī</s> [<s>Śrīnagar</s>],
this commentary named <s>Yoga[rāja-vivṛti]</s>, filled with perfect non-duality, has been composed. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Herewith is completed the commentary on the compendium of the <s>Paramārthasāra</s>, the work of the blessed <s>Rājānaka Yogarāja</s>, belonging to the supreme Māheśvara [tradition].
